objects.description: Sequence number type used by the API; 32-bit unsigned integer.
Count or limit of AMQP transfer frames; 32-bit unsigned integer.
Span of time in milliseconds; 32-bit unsigned integer. PN_MILLIS_MAX defines its maximum value.
Span of time in seconds; 32-bit unsigned integer.
64-bit timestamp in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
32-bit Unicode code point type.
32-bit decimal floating-point scalar stored as 32-bit unsigned integer per AMQP representation.
64-bit decimal floating-point scalar stored as 64-bit unsigned integer per AMQP representation.
128-bit decimal floating-point value stored as 16 raw bytes.
16-byte universally unique identifier stored as raw bytes.
Const byte buffer view: length plus pointer to const bytes. Immutable payload pointer.
Mutable byte buffer view: length plus pointer to writable bytes.
Bitflag state value encoding local/remote endpoint state; accessed via PN_LOCAL_MASK/PN_REMOTE_MASK and related bits. Specific flag constants are defined elsewhere.
Opaque AMQP connection handle. Manages sessions and links. Only a forward declaration appears here; constructed via API functions defined elsewhere.
Opaque AMQP session handle; contains links. Forward declaration only.
Opaque AMQP link handle (sender or receiver) with an ordered sequence of deliveries. Forward declaration only.
Opaque AMQP delivery handle representing a message transfer, owned by a link. Forward declaration only.
Opaque event collector used to receive high-level events. Forward declaration only.
Opaque listener for incoming connections. Forward declaration only.
Opaque transport/channel for an AMQP connection. Forward declaration only.
Opaque proactor harness for multithreaded I/O. Forward declaration only.
Opaque raw network connection type for use with the proactor. Forward declaration only.
Opaque batch of events that must be handled in sequence. Forward declaration only.
Opaque internal navigational handle (const void pointer).
Opaque type representing the type/descriptor of an internal Proton object. Forward declaration only.
Opaque type representing attached context information (property bag/record). Forward declaration only.
Opaque event handler type used internally with the (now internal/cond) reactor APIs. Forward declaration only.

objects.description: Conditional typedef for ssize_t to provide a signed size type on platforms or build configurations that lack it. On MSVC it aliases SSIZE_T; otherwise it aliases intptr_t. Only defined when PNI_DEFINE_SSIZE_T is set by the preprocessor logic in this header.

Conditional typedefs providing fixed-width integer types when a standard stdint.h is unavailable (primarily for older MSVC). This entry represents int8_t; see aliases for related types defined in the same block. Availability depends on PNI_DEFINE_STDINT being set by preprocessor logic.

Fixed-width integer typedefs for MSVC when stdint.h is unavailable. This canonical entry is int16_t; aliases list the other typedef names provided by the same block. Availability is conditional on PNI_DEFINE_STDINT.

Opaque error object that holds an integer error code and associated descriptive text. The concrete structure is not defined in this header, indicating it is an opaque type managed via the provided API. Use pn_error() to create, pn_error_free() to destroy, and helper functions to set/inspect code and text. Details of internal fields are unknown from this header.

Opaque AMQP condition handle used to hold exception/terminal-state information for endpoints and deliveries, including name, description, and an info map. Actual structure is not defined in this header (forward declaration only). Create with pn_condition(), free with pn_condition_free(), clear/set/query via provided APIs. Details of internal fields are unknown here.

objects.description: Enumeration of Proton internal class/identifier codes. Each enumerator names a distinct component or object category used internally (e.g., strings, links, sessions, reactor, proactor). Typically used to tag or discriminate object kinds at runtime for diagnostics, type checks, or memory accounting. Specific semantics beyond the names are not documented here.
Opaque runtime type descriptor for Proton objects. Only forward-declared here (no struct layout), used with pn_class_* functions to describe initialization/finalization and refcount operations.
Type for class identifiers returned by pn_class_id(). Declared in included proton/cid.h; only referenced here. No definition in this header.

Opaque handle type used as a unique key for attaching data to pn_record_t via PN_HANDLE macro. Actual type defined in included headers; this header provides the PN_HANDLE macro for creating unique handles in a C file.
Opaque key/value record for storing arbitrary per-object data keyed by pn_handle_t. Only forward-declared via included headers; manipulated via pn_record_* functions in this header.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
  PN_NULL = 1,
  PN_BOOL = 2,
  PN_UBYTE = 3,
  PN_BYTE = 4,
  PN_USHORT = 5,

  PN_LONG = 11,
  PN_TIMESTAMP = 12,

  PN_DOUBLE = 14,
  PN_DECIMAL32 = 15,
  PN_DECIMAL64 = 16,
  PN_DECIMAL128 = 17,
  PN_UUID = 18,
  PN_BINARY = 19,
  PN_STRING = 20,
  PN_SYMBOL = 21,
  PN_DESCRIBED = 22,
  PN_ARRAY = 23,
  PN_LIST = 24,
  PN_MAP = 25,

} pn_type_t;
objects.description: Enumeration identifying AMQP data types used by the codec and accessor APIs.
Discriminated union that can hold any scalar AMQP value. Field 'type' indicates which member in 'u' is valid. Used broadly by the data get/put APIs.
Alias of pn_atom_t restricted by convention to values valid for AMQP message-id/correlation-id fields.
Opaque handle to an AMQP Data tree. Provides decode/encode and navigation over AMQP values. Lifetime managed via pn_data() and pn_data_free().

Opaque handle for an AMQP message object. It is a mutable container for message sections (properties, annotations, body, etc.) that can be encoded/decoded to/from AMQP binary. The actual struct is not defined here; this is a forward typedef to an internal struct.
Opaque forward declaration of a link object (AMQP link). Only referenced here to allow pn_message_send() to accept a sender link. The struct layout is not defined in this header.

Opaque handle to a delivery disposition (delivery state/outcome) used to represent local/remote state for a delivery. Lifetime is tied to the parent delivery; many accessors expose condition, annotations, and state-specific fields.
Opaque subtype handle representing the non-terminal PN_RECEIVED state for a delivery, carrying section number and offset of received message data.
Opaque subtype handle representing the terminal PN_REJECTED outcome for a delivery; may carry a condition describing the reason for rejection.
Opaque subtype handle representing the terminal PN_MODIFIED outcome for a delivery; may carry failed/undeliverable flags and annotations.
Opaque subtype handle for PN_DECLARED disposition indicating a transaction has been declared; carries a transaction identifier.
Opaque subtype handle for PN_TRANSACTIONAL_STATE representing transactional state for a delivery; carries transaction id and provisional outcome type.
Opaque handle for a custom (non-predefined) delivery disposition; exposes raw pn_data_t and a 64-bit type code to represent extension states.
Alias type for an AMQP delivery tag. It is a typedef of pn_bytes_t (defined elsewhere) representing a byte sequence used as a delivery tag on a link.

Opaque handle type for a delivery object on an AMQP link. The concrete struct/class definition is not present in this header. It represents a single transfer of a message over a link, with lifecycle operations such as update, settle, and abort.
Opaque handle type for an AMQP link. Only referenced here; definition not present in this header. It owns/creates deliveries and maintains delivery sequencing.
Opaque handle for an attachments/record map associated with Proton objects. Only referenced here; definition not present in this header.
Opaque handle representing a disposition for a delivery (local or remote). Only referenced here; definition not present in this header.
Opaque handle type for an AMQP connection. Only referenced here; definition not present in this header.
Opaque handle to an AMQP terminus (source/target/coordinator) associated with a link. Actual structure is not defined in this header; it is managed via the provided API functions.
Enumeration of AMQP terminus roles: unspecified, source, target, or transaction coordinator.
Enumeration describing durability of a terminus: none, configuration only, or configuration plus delivery state.
Enumeration of when a terminus is considered orphaned for expiry timing: with link, session, connection, or never.
Enumeration of distribution modes for a source terminus resolving multiple receivers: unspecified, copy, or move.
Enumeration type describing permitted/expected settlement behaviors for a sending link: always unsettled, always settled, or a mix. Used to configure or query a link’s sender settle mode.
Enumeration type describing permitted/expected settlement behaviors for a receiving link: settle first or settle second (after sender). Used to configure or query a link’s receiver settle mode.

Opaque handle type for a Proton AMQP session. It represents a session associated with a pn_connection_t, managing links and flow windows. The concrete definition is not present in this header (forward-declared elsewhere), so treat it as an opaque endpoint object managed via the pn_session_* API. Construction/destruction and lifecycle are controlled only through the provided API functions.

Opaque attachments/record map associated with various Proton objects. Here it is used as the container of per-session attachments returned by pn_session_attachments. The actual definition is not present in this header.

Bitmask type representing endpoint state flags (e.g., local/remote open/closed). In this header it is only referenced as a value type for pn_session_state, pn_session_head, pn_session_next. The underlying typedef/enum is not defined here. Pointer form shown per requirements.
Opaque error object used to report additional error information. Deprecated here in favor of pn_session_condition. Definition is not in this header.

Condition object carrying error or close information for endpoints. Used here for local and remote session conditions via pn_session_condition and pn_session_remote_condition. Definition is not present in this header.
Opaque connection handle that owns sessions. Only referenced for association and traversal in this header. Definition is not present here.
Integral type used to represent counts of AMQP transfer frames for session window management. Not defined in this header; only referenced by functions managing incoming windows.
Opaque connection handle type for Apache Qpid Proton C API. The concrete struct/class is not defined in this header; only functions operating on it are declared here.

Endpoint state type referenced by this API. Not defined in this header; it represents bitflags for local/remote active/closed/uninit. Note: this header defines macros PN_LOCAL_*, PN_REMOTE_* and masks that operate on pn_state_t values, but the actual type definition is elsewhere.
Opaque error object type referenced for connection error reporting. Not defined in this header.
Opaque event collector type used to collect pn_event_t generated by a connection. Not defined in this header.
Opaque attachments record associated with a connection. Not defined in this header.
Opaque condition object representing local/remote endpoint conditions. Not defined in this header.
Opaque AMQP data tree used for capabilities and properties. Not defined in this header.
Opaque transport binding associated with a connection. Not defined in this header.
Trace-flag bitset type controlling what an AMQP transport logs. Values are combined bit flags like PN_TRACE_RAW, PN_TRACE_FRM, etc.
Function-pointer type for a logging callback used by a transport. The callback receives the transport and a textual message.

Opaque-like aggregate that bundles a Proton connection, transport, and event collector to drive AMQP I/O and event processing as a unit. The driver manages ownership of the contained connection, transport, and collector once initialized via pn_connection_driver_init(); they will be released by pn_connection_driver_destroy().

Opaque listener type representing a listening socket/resource used with the Proton proactor API. It is referenced throughout this header but not defined here; the concrete structure is defined elsewhere in the library.
Opaque Proton connection handle. Only referenced here as a parameter type; not defined in this header.
Opaque Proton transport handle. Only referenced here as a parameter type; not defined in this header.
Opaque Proton condition (error/status) object. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.
Opaque Proton attachments/record map used to associate application data with core objects. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.
Opaque Proton proactor object, event loop/IO orchestrator. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.
Opaque Proton event object used with the proactor. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.
Opaque Proton raw connection used for non-AMQP I/O. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.

Opaque unsettled-API type representing the network address associated with a proactor transport or listener. Only forward-declared here; actual structure is private. Instances are obtained from the Proton API (e.g., transport or listener queries) and are invalidated when the owning transport/listener closes.

Opaque handle for the Proton SASL (Simple Authentication and Security Layer) associated with a pn_transport_t. It represents the SASL negotiation layer used to authenticate and optionally secure an AMQP connection. The struct is incomplete here; it is managed via the SASL API functions in this header. Construction is via pn_sasl(transport); lifetime is tied to the owning transport.
Enumeration of SASL negotiation outcomes used to report the final result of authentication. Values indicate success, not completed, or failure categories (auth/system/permanent/transient).

Function table (vtable) defining the internal SASL authenticator plugin interface for Proton. Implementations fill in these callbacks to provide mechanism listing, initialization (client/server), message processing, and optional security layer encode/decode. Ownership, lifetime, and context are managed by the transport via pnx_sasl_set_implementation; the implementation's memory must remain valid until its free callback is invoked. Details of pn_transport_t and pn_bytes_t are external to this header.

objects.definition:
enum pnx_sasl_state {
  SASL_NONE,
  SASL_POSTED_INIT,
  SASL_POSTED_MECHANISMS,
  SASL_POSTED_RESPONSE,
  SASL_POSTED_CHALLENGE,
  SASL_RECVED_SUCCESS,
  SASL_RECVED_FAILURE,
  SASL_POSTED_OUTCOME,
  SASL_ERROR
};
objects.description: Enum representing the internal SASL state machine phases used by SASL implementations and the transport. Used to coordinate message posting/receiving and final outcome.

Opaque SSL configuration domain handle. Holds SSL/TLS configuration (certs, trusted CAs, verification policy, protocols, ciphers) shared by one or more SSL sessions. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the structure is defined privately in the implementation.

Opaque per-connection SSL/TLS session handle associated with a transport. Performs encryption/authentication for a single connection. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the structure is defined privately in the implementation.
Enumeration selecting the endpoint role for SSL/TLS domains and sessions: client or server.
Enumeration indicating whether an SSL/TLS session was resumed from a previous session or not, or unknown/not supported.
Enumeration controlling peer-certificate verification policy for a domain/session: none/internal, verify certificate, allow anonymous, or verify certificate and peer name (default for clients).
Enumeration of common X.509 certificate Subject subfields used to query components of the peer certificate subject.
Enumeration of hash algorithms available for computing certificate fingerprints: SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, and MD5.

Opaque proactor handle type referenced throughout this header. It represents the event-driven IO orchestrator that binds AMQP connections/transports to network IO and emits event batches. Definition is not provided in this header; it is defined elsewhere.
Opaque handle for a batch of proactor events returned by pn_proactor_wait()/pn_proactor_get(). The concrete definition is not present in this header.
Opaque listener type representing a listening socket/source managed by the proactor. Not defined in this header.
Opaque AMQP connection handle from the core API, associated with a transport by the proactor. Only referenced here; definition is elsewhere.
Opaque transport handle for AMQP protocol IO binding. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.
Opaque condition/error container type used to convey disconnect reasons. Referenced only; not defined here.
Opaque single event handle iterated from an event batch. Only referenced; not defined here.
Opaque handle for a raw (non-AMQP-framed) network connection managed by the proactor. Only referenced here; definition is elsewhere.

Typedef for a millisecond time quantity used with timeouts; exact underlying type is not defined in this header (likely provided by <proton/types.h>). Pointer form is shown as required by the output schema.

Platform-dependent typedef representing a socket handle/file descriptor for integration with the Proton proactor import API. On Windows it aliases uintptr_t (suitable for SOCKET-like handles); on non-Windows it aliases int (POSIX file descriptor).

Descriptor for a single raw I/O buffer used with pn_raw_connection. Holds an application context handle, a byte pointer, total capacity, current data size, and an offset indicating the first byte to read/write. Read operations update size only; write operations do not modify the struct or buffer contents. Intended to pass buffers to and from the raw connection for reading and writing.

Opaque handle for a proactor-managed raw socket connection. Created by pn_raw_connection() and thereafter owned and lifecycle-managed by the proactor; there is no public destructor/free. Provides APIs to supply/read buffers, close read/write sides or entire connection, query closure state, wake, and access condition/context/attachments. Concrete definition is not present in this header.
Alias typedef for pn_handler_t representing a handler that performs AMQP connection handshaking. Exact behavior is not defined in this header, it is an alias to the generic pn_handler_t type.
Alias typedef for pn_handler_t representing an input/output event handler. Specific responsibilities are not documented here; it is an alias to pn_handler_t.
Alias typedef for pn_handler_t representing a flow-control handler, typically managing link credit/windows. This header provides no further details; it is an alias to pn_handler_t.
Opaque handle to a Proton reactor object that manages event-driven I/O, timers, and handlers. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the actual structure is defined elsewhere.
Opaque handle for a listening/accepting endpoint owned by a reactor, used to accept incoming connections. Forward-declared only.
Opaque timer scheduler used by the reactor to manage timed tasks and deadlines. Forward-declared only.
Opaque handle representing a scheduled task (timer task) managed by a reactor or timer. Forward-declared only.
Opaque forward declaration of an internal list type used by the reactor API (e.g., to return children). No definition is provided here.

objects.definition:
#if defined(_WIN32) && ! defined(__CYGWIN__)
#ifdef _WIN64
typedef unsigned __int64 pn_socket_t;
#else
typedef unsigned int pn_socket_t;
#endif
#define PN_INVALID_SOCKET (pn_socket_t)(~0)
#else
typedef int pn_socket_t;
#define PN_INVALID_SOCKET (-1)
#endif
objects.description: Platform-dependent typedef representing an abstract, non-blocking I/O socket/file-descriptor handle used by Proton. On Windows it is an unsigned integer type (32-bit or 64-bit depending on architecture); on other platforms it is an int. PN_INVALID_SOCKET provides the invalid sentinel for the platform.

Opaque handle for a selectable object used to integrate Proton I/O with external event loops. Each selectable is associated with exactly one socket/file descriptor and can express interest in read, write, and timer (deadline) events. Lifecycle is managed via pn_selectable_free(); it becomes terminal when pn_selectable_is_terminal() returns true, after which it should be removed from external loops and freed.
Referenced via include <proton/logger.h> but not defined in this header; ignore per instructions. No custom types are defined in this header file.

Opaque logger handle for configuring and receiving Proton library log output. The struct is forward-declared here and defined privately in the library; users manipulate it via the provided API (e.g., setting masks and sinks, querying sink/context, logging messages). Lifetime and allocation are managed by the library functions that return it (e.g., pn_default_logger); no destructor is declared in this header.

objects.definition:
typedef enum pn_log_subsystem_t {
    PN_SUBSYSTEM_NONE    = 0,    /**< No subsystem */
    PN_SUBSYSTEM_MEMORY  = 1,    /**< Memory usage */
    PN_SUBSYSTEM_IO      = 2,    /**< Low level Input/Output */
    PN_SUBSYSTEM_EVENT   = 4,    /**< Events */
    PN_SUBSYSTEM_AMQP    = 8,    /**< AMQP protocol processing */
    PN_SUBSYSTEM_SSL     = 16,   /**< TLS/SSL protocol processing */
    PN_SUBSYSTEM_SASL    = 32,   /**< SASL protocol processing */
    PN_SUBSYSTEM_BINDING = 64,   /**< Language binding */
    PN_SUBSYSTEM_ALL     = 65535 /**< Every subsystem */
} pn_log_subsystem_t;
objects.description: Bitmask enum identifying Proton subsystems that can emit log messages. Values are exclusive bits to allow combining multiple subsystems in masks.

objects.definition:
typedef enum pn_log_level_t {
    PN_LEVEL_NONE     = 0,    /**< No level */
    PN_LEVEL_CRITICAL = 1,    /**< Something is wrong and can't be fixed - probably a library bug */
    PN_LEVEL_ERROR    = 2,    /**< Something went wrong */
    PN_LEVEL_WARNING  = 4,    /**< Something unusual happened but not necessarily an error */
    PN_LEVEL_INFO     = 8,    /**< Something that might be interesting happened */
    PN_LEVEL_DEBUG    = 16,   /**< Something you might want to know about happened */
    PN_LEVEL_TRACE    = 32,   /**< Detail about something that happened */
    PN_LEVEL_FRAME    = 64,   /**< Protocol frame traces */
    PN_LEVEL_RAW      = 128,  /**< Raw protocol bytes */
    PN_LEVEL_ALL      = 65535 /**< Every possible level */
} pn_log_level_t;
objects.description: Bitmask enum defining severities of log messages. Values are exclusive bits so multiple levels can be enabled in a mask. PN_LEVEL_CRITICAL is always logged irrespective of masks.

objects.definition: typedef void (*pn_log_sink_t)(intptr_t sink_context, pn_log_subsystem_t subsystem, pn_log_level_t severity, const char *message);
objects.description: Function pointer type for log message callbacks. Called with an application-provided context, the emitting subsystem, severity level, and a null-terminated message string.

Opaque handle to a parsed URL used by the Proton C API. It represents the components of a URL (scheme, username, password, host, port, path) and provides getters/setters plus functions to construct, clear, stringify, and free. The struct is forward-declared here; its layout is private/unknown to callers. All API functions in this header are deprecated in favor of third-party URL libraries.

This header does not define any structs, enums, typedefs, or classes. It only includes other Proton headers and has an include guard. Therefore there are no custom data types to document from this header itself.

Opaque TLS configuration object ("domain") used to hold settings shared by one or more TLS sessions. Instances are created with pn_tls_config() and freed with pn_tls_config_free(). The internal structure is not defined in this header.

Opaque per-connection TLS session object that performs encryption/decryption and authentication. Constructed from a pn_tls_config_t with pn_tls() and freed with pn_tls_free(). Internal layout is hidden.
Enumeration selecting TLS endpoint role for sessions created by a configuration: client or server.
Enumeration controlling peer-certificate verification policy used by a TLS configuration and its sessions.
Enumeration identifying subfields within a certificate subject, used to query values from the peer certificate.
Enumeration of hashing algorithms to compute certificate fingerprints.

Opaque handle for a high-level AMQP messenger that manages single incoming and outgoing message queues, routing, I/O, and related configuration. Only the opaque typedef is defined here; the struct layout is private.
Opaque handle representing a subscription (request for incoming messages) created by a messenger. Only the opaque typedef is defined here; the struct layout is private.
Integral handle used to track the status of individual incoming or outgoing deliveries associated with a messenger. It is a typedef of int64_t in this header.
Enumeration of possible message/disposition states for a delivery identified by a pn_tracker_t.

functions.name: pn_bytes
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN inline pn_bytes_t pn_bytes(size_t size, const char *start)
functions.description: Constructs and returns a pn_bytes_t value that references an external, read-only byte sequence. It simply assigns the provided size and pointer to the struct and returns it; no allocation or copying is performed. Use this as a lightweight view over an existing const buffer.
requirements: The function does not validate inputs; it only packages them into a pn_bytes_t.
If start is non-NULL, it must point to at least size bytes of readable memory for as long as any consumer uses the returned pn_bytes_t (lifetime is managed by the caller).
No ownership is transferred; the caller retains responsibility for the memory referenced by start.
The contents referenced by start are treated as read-only (const).
Passing a null pointer is permissible only if any subsequent users of the pn_bytes_t are prepared to handle a null start; the function itself will not dereference start.

functions.name: pn_rwbytes
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN inline pn_rwbytes_t pn_rwbytes(size_t size, char *start)
functions.description: Constructs and returns a pn_rwbytes_t value that references an external, writable byte sequence. It simply assigns the provided size and pointer to the struct and returns it; no allocation or copying is performed. Use this as a lightweight mutable view over an existing buffer.
requirements: The function does not validate inputs; it only packages them into a pn_rwbytes_t.
If start is non-NULL, it must point to at least size bytes of writable memory for as long as any consumer uses the returned pn_rwbytes_t (lifetime is managed by the caller).
No ownership is transferred; the caller retains responsibility for the memory referenced by start.
Callers must ensure that any writes through the referenced memory are valid and synchronized as appropriate for concurrent access.
Passing a null pointer is permissible only if any subsequent users of the pn_rwbytes_t are prepared to handle a null start; the function itself will not dereference start.

functions.name: pn_code
functions.description: Returns the human-readable name of an error code. Intended to map PN_* error constants to a static, constant string for diagnostics and logging. The returned pointer refers to a static constant and must not be freed.
requirements: code should be a valid PN_* error code defined in this header (e.g., PN_OK, PN_EOS, etc.), inferred from usage
Caller must not free or modify the returned string (explicitly documented: returned pointer is to a static constant)

functions.name: pn_error
functions.description: Creates a new pn_error_t object representing an error container with a code and text. Use to accumulate and inspect error details across API calls. Must be freed with pn_error_free.
requirements: Caller must eventually free the returned pn_error_t using pn_error_free
The returned object must be passed to other pn_error_* APIs only while it remains valid (i.e., before pn_error_free)

functions.name: pn_error_free
functions.description: Frees a pn_error_t object previously created with pn_error(). After this call, the object must not be used.
requirements: error must be a pn_error_t previously allocated by pn_error (inferred from naming and allocation/free pair)
Do not use the pn_error_t after it has been freed

functions.name: pn_error_clear
functions.description: Resets the pn_error_t to a no-error state (code == 0) and clears any associated text. Useful to reuse an error object.
requirements: error must be a valid, initialized pn_error_t (created by pn_error and not yet freed)

functions.name: pn_error_set
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN int pn_error_set(pn_error_t *error, int code, const char *text);
functions.description: Sets the error code and text on the pn_error_t. The function makes an internal copy of the provided text.
requirements: error must be a valid, initialized pn_error_t (created by pn_error and not yet freed)
code should be a valid PN_* error code (inferred from API design)
text must point to a NUL-terminated C string; the function copies the text so it only needs to remain valid for the duration of the call (explicitly: makes a copy of text)
Caller should handle the returned int status; specific return semantics are not documented in this header (unknown)

functions.name: pn_error_vformat
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN int pn_error_vformat(pn_error_t *error, int code, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Sets the error code and formats the error text using a printf-style format string and a va_list of arguments. Useful when forwarding variadic arguments.
requirements: error must be a valid, initialized pn_error_t (created by pn_error and not yet freed)
code should be a valid PN_* error code (inferred)
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string
ap must be a properly initialized va_list that matches fmt (i.e., corresponds to the arguments for the given format)
Caller should handle the returned int status; specific return semantics are not documented in this header (unknown)

functions.name: pn_error_format
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN int pn_error_format(pn_error_t *error, int code, PN_PRINTF_FORMAT const char *fmt, ...) PN_PRINTF_FORMAT_ATTR(3, 4);
functions.description: Sets the error code and formats the error text using a printf-style format string and variadic arguments. The attributes indicate compile-time format checking where supported.
requirements: error must be a valid, initialized pn_error_t (created by pn_error and not yet freed)
code should be a valid PN_* error code (inferred)
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; the variadic arguments must match the format specifiers
Caller should handle the returned int status; specific return semantics are not documented in this header (unknown)

functions.name: pn_error_code
functions.description: Returns the current error code stored in the pn_error_t. Typically 0 indicates no error (PN_OK).
requirements: error must be a valid, initialized pn_error_t (created by pn_error and not yet freed)

functions.name: pn_error_text
functions.description: Returns the current error text stored in the pn_error_t. The returned pointer is owned by the pn_error_t and must not be freed. Its lifetime is tied to the pn_error_t and may change on subsequent modifications.
requirements: error must be a valid, initialized pn_error_t (created by pn_error and not yet freed)
Caller must not free or modify the returned string (explicitly documented: owned by pn_error_t)
Do not use the returned pointer after the pn_error_t is modified or freed (inferred from ownership/lifetime)

functions.name: pn_error_copy
functions.description: Copies the contents (code and text) from src into error, replacing any previous state in error.
requirements: Both error and src must be valid, initialized pn_error_t objects (created by pn_error and not yet freed)
After the call, error's previous error text/state may be overwritten (inferred)
Caller should handle the returned int status; specific return semantics are not documented in this header (unknown)

functions.name: pn_condition_is_set
functions.description: Returns true if the condition currently holds any information (the name is non-NULL); false otherwise. Use to check whether a condition has been set before reading details.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t* (created by pn_condition() or obtained from a Proton object). [inferred]
Caller should not assume thread-safety; access from one thread at a time unless documented elsewhere. [inferred]

functions.name: pn_condition_clear
functions.description: Clears all information from the condition. After this call, pn_condition_is_set() will be false, pn_condition_get_name()/pn_condition_get_description() return NULL, and the pn_data_t from pn_condition_info() remains valid but is cleared.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
Any previously obtained pn_data_t* via pn_condition_info() remains valid but its content will be cleared (see pn_data_clear()).
Do not use concurrently with other operations on the same condition from multiple threads. [inferred]

functions.name: pn_condition_get_name
functions.description: Gets the symbolic name of the condition, or NULL if no condition information is set.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
Returned pointer is owned by the condition; do not free it and its lifetime follows the condition. [inferred]

functions.name: pn_condition_set_name
functions.description: Sets the symbolic name associated with the condition. Returns 0 on success or a non-zero error code on failure.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
name should point to a valid, null-terminated UTF-8/ASCII string expected by AMQP condition names. [inferred]
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_condition_get_description
functions.description: Gets the human-readable description of the condition, or NULL if none is set.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
Returned pointer is owned by the condition; do not free it and its lifetime follows the condition. [inferred]

functions.name: pn_condition_set_description
functions.description: Sets the human-readable description for the condition. Returns 0 on success or a non-zero error code on failure.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
description should point to a valid, null-terminated string. [inferred]
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_condition_info
functions.description: Returns a pn_data_t object that holds the additional information map for the condition. Can be used to read or modify the condition’s info. The returned object remains valid across pn_condition_clear(), but will be cleared by that call.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
The returned pn_data_t* is owned by the condition; do not free it directly. Modify using pn_data_* API following expected AMQP map structure. [partially inferred]
Be aware that pn_condition_clear() clears the returned pn_data_t’s content.

functions.name: pn_condition_vformat
functions.signature: int pn_condition_vformat(pn_condition_t *condition, const char *name, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Sets the condition name and a printf-style formatted description using a va_list. Returns 0 on success or a non-zero error code on failure. Use when forwarding variadic arguments.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
name should be a valid, null-terminated string and typically non-NULL to mark the condition as set. [inferred]
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with the supplied va_list ap.
ap must be initialized and correspond exactly to fmt’s format specifiers.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_condition_format
functions.signature: int pn_condition_format(pn_condition_t *condition, const char *name, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Sets the condition name and a printf-style formatted description using variadic arguments. Returns 0 on success or a non-zero error code on failure.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
name should be a valid, null-terminated string and typically non-NULL to mark the condition as set. [inferred]
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; the following variadic arguments must match fmt’s specifiers.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_condition_is_redirect
functions.description: Returns true if the condition represents a redirect; false otherwise.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]

functions.name: pn_condition_redirect_host
functions.description: If the condition is a redirect, returns the redirect host string; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
Only meaningful if pn_condition_is_redirect(condition) is true; otherwise expect NULL.
Returned pointer is owned by the condition; do not free it. [inferred]

functions.name: pn_condition_redirect_port
functions.description: If the condition is a redirect, returns the redirect port; otherwise returns an error code.
requirements: condition must be a valid pn_condition_t*. [inferred]
Only meaningful if pn_condition_is_redirect(condition) is true; otherwise caller must handle the returned error code.
Caller must check the return value and treat non-port values (error code) appropriately; exact error values are library-defined and unspecified here.

functions.name: pn_condition_copy
functions.description: Copies all information from src condition to dest condition. Returns 0 on success or a non-zero error code on failure.
requirements: dest and src must both be valid pn_condition_t* objects. [inferred]
dest may be overwritten; ensure it is distinct from src unless the implementation allows self-copy. [inferred]
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_condition
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new condition object.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for allocation failure (may be NULL). [inferred]
Objects created must be released with pn_condition_free().

functions.name: pn_condition_free
functions.description: Frees a condition object created by pn_condition().
requirements: condition must have been created by pn_condition() or be otherwise owned by the caller. [inferred]
Do not use the condition after freeing it. [inferred]
Passing NULL is unspecified by this header; avoid passing NULL unless documented elsewhere. [inferred]

functions.name: pn_class_create
functions.signature:
PN_EXTERN pn_class_t *pn_class_create(const char *name,
                                      void (*initialize)(void*),
                                      void (*finalize)(void*),
                                      void (*incref)(void*),
                                      void (*decref)(void*),
                                      int (*refcount)(void*));
functions.description: Create a class descriptor for Proton-managed objects with custom lifecycle handlers. Intended for internal use to define object types, their initialization/finalization, and reference-count operations.
requirements: Function pointers passed for initialize, finalize, incref, decref, and refcount must match the declared types.
The provided callbacks are expected to correctly manage the lifecycle and reference counting of instances of this class; exact semantics are not documented here.
The name string must point to a valid, null-terminated C string; ownership and lifetime requirements are unknown.
Usage of this function is marked internal (@cond INTERNAL).

functions.name: pn_class_new
functions.description: Allocate a new object instance associated with the given class descriptor. The allocated object memory size is specified by the caller.
requirements: clazz must be a valid class previously created with pn_class_create (or provided by the library).
size must be the total size in bytes to allocate for the object; exact constraints beyond being a valid size_t are unknown.
Returned pointer must be treated as a Proton-managed object; lifetime, initialization details, and ownership semantics beyond creation are unknown.

functions.name: pn_class_name
functions.description: Return the human-readable name of a class descriptor.
requirements: clazz must be a valid pn_class_t pointer.
The returned const char* refers to storage owned by the library; mutating it is not allowed. Lifetime/validity duration is unknown.

functions.name: pn_class_id
functions.description: Return the class identifier (pn_cid_t) for a class descriptor.
requirements: clazz must be a valid pn_class_t pointer.

functions.name: pn_class
functions.description: Return the class descriptor associated with a Proton-managed object instance.
requirements: object must be a valid Proton-managed object pointer created by this API.
If object is invalid or not Proton-managed, behavior is unknown/unspecified.

functions.name: pn_incref
functions.description: Increment the reference count of a Proton-managed object and return the object pointer.
requirements: object must be a valid Proton-managed object pointer.
Caller must pair increments with corresponding pn_decref calls to avoid leaks; exact refcount semantics not documented here.

functions.name: pn_decref
functions.description: Decrement the reference count of a Proton-managed object. Returns an int (semantics unspecified in this header).
requirements: object must be a valid Proton-managed object pointer.
Caller must not use the object after its reference count reaches zero and it is freed; exact return value meaning is not documented here.

functions.name: pn_refcount
functions.description: Return the current reference count of a Proton-managed object.
requirements: object must be a valid Proton-managed object pointer.
Returned value semantics (e.g., whether it includes the caller’s reference) are not documented here.

functions.name: pn_free
functions.description: Free a Proton-managed object, releasing associated resources. Typically used when reference count reaches zero.
requirements: object must be a valid Proton-managed object pointer.
After pn_free, the object pointer becomes invalid and must not be used.
Interaction with reference counting (e.g., whether to call pn_free directly vs. pn_decref) is not specified here; follow the library’s refcount model.

functions.name: pn_tostring
functions.description: Return a string representation of a Proton-managed object.
requirements: object must be a valid Proton-managed object pointer.
Ownership and lifetime of the returned char* are not documented; whether the caller must free it is unknown.
Returned string encoding/format is unspecified.

functions.name: pn_record
functions.description: Create or obtain a new record object (a key/value attachment map) for associating data with handles.
requirements: Returned pn_record_t* must be treated as a Proton-managed object; ownership, lifetime, and freeing mechanism are not specified here.

functions.name: pn_record_def
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_record_def(pn_record_t *record, pn_handle_t key, const pn_class_t *clazz);
functions.description: Define a key in a record with an associated expected class/type for values stored under that key.
requirements: record must be a valid pn_record_t pointer.
key must be a pn_handle_t obtained via the PN_HANDLE macro or otherwise uniquely defined.
clazz must be a valid pn_class_t pointer defining the expected value type for this key.
This function should be called before setting or getting values for the key to establish type association (inferred from naming).

functions.name: pn_record_has
functions.description: Check whether a record has an entry for the specified key.
requirements: record must be a valid pn_record_t pointer.
key must be a pn_handle_t previously defined for the record (recommended; exact requirement not documented).

functions.name: pn_record_get
functions.description: Retrieve the value associated with a key from a record.
requirements: record must be a valid pn_record_t pointer.
key should be a pn_handle_t defined for the record via pn_record_def (inferred).
Returned pointer type is expected to match the class specified in pn_record_def; exact enforcement is not documented.
If the key is not present, the return value and behavior are not documented here.

functions.name: pn_record_set
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_record_set(pn_record_t *record, pn_handle_t key, void *value);
functions.description: Associate a value with a key in a record.
requirements: record must be a valid pn_record_t pointer.
key should be a pn_handle_t defined for the record via pn_record_def (inferred).
value should be a pointer to an object whose class matches the clazz provided in pn_record_def for this key (inferred).
Ownership transfer, reference counting behavior, and whether NULL is allowed are not documented.

functions.name: pn_record_clear
functions.description: Clear all entries from a record, removing associations for all keys.
requirements: record must be a valid pn_record_t pointer.
After clearing, previously retrieved pointers from the record may no longer be accessible via the record; validity of the underlying objects depends on their own lifetimes (not specified).

functions.name: pn_type_name
functions.description: Return the string name of an AMQP type enum value for diagnostics or display.
requirements: type should be a valid pn_type_t value; otherwise the returned string may identify it generically or be implementation-defined.
The returned string is not specified to be dynamically allocated; treat it as read-only and do not free it.

functions.name: pn_data
functions.description: Construct a pn_data_t container for AMQP values. The container grows automatically; an initial capacity of 0 is allowed.
requirements: capacity may be 0 or greater.
Caller owns the returned pn_data_t* and must free it with pn_data_free().

functions.name: pn_data_free
functions.description: Free a pn_data_t and its associated resources. Safe to pass NULL.
requirements: data may be NULL.
After calling, any pointers obtained from this pn_data_t (including pn_bytes_t values from getters and pn_error_t from pn_data_error) become invalid.

functions.name: pn_data_errno
functions.description: Return the current error code for the pn_data_t.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.

functions.name: pn_data_error
functions.description: Access the pn_data_t’s error object which is updated when operations fail; it lives and dies with the pn_data_t.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Do not free the returned pn_error_t; its lifetime is tied to data.

functions.name: pn_data_clear
functions.description: Clear the pn_data_t to an empty state, equivalent to newly constructed.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Clearing invalidates pn_bytes_t values previously returned by getters.

functions.name: pn_data_size
functions.description: Return the total number of nodes (all descendants/ancestors relative to current, including current if any) contained in the pn_data_t.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.

functions.name: pn_data_rewind
functions.description: Reset navigation: clear the current node and set parent to the root; next() will advance to the first node.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.

functions.name: pn_data_next
functions.description: Advance current node to its next sibling. Returns true if moved; false if there is no next sibling.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.

functions.name: pn_data_prev
functions.description: Move current node to its previous sibling. Returns true if moved; false otherwise.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.

functions.name: pn_data_enter
functions.description: Enter the current compound node (list/map/array/described), making it the parent and preparing to iterate its children.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
There must be a current node and it must be a compound type; otherwise returns false.

functions.name: pn_data_exit
functions.description: Exit to the parent level: set current to parent and parent to its parent. Returns false if there is no current or no parent.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
A valid parent context must exist to succeed.

functions.name: pn_data_type
functions.description: Return the AMQP type of the current node, or PN_INVALID if there is no current node.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.

functions.name: pn_data_print
functions.description: Pretty-print the contents of the pn_data_t to stdout using pn_data_format(). Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller should check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_format
functions.description: Render a human-readable representation of the pn_data_t into a caller-provided buffer. On success, *size is updated to the number of bytes used.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
bytes must point to a writable buffer with at least *size bytes available on entry.
size must be a non-NULL pointer to the buffer capacity on entry; it is updated to used length on success.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_encode
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN ssize_t pn_data_encode(pn_data_t *data, char *bytes, size_t size);
functions.description: Encode the pn_data_t as an AMQP data stream into the provided buffer. Returns encoded size on success or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
bytes must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
To avoid overflow, size should be at least pn_data_encoded_size(data).
Caller must check for negative return values indicating errors.

functions.name: pn_data_encoded_size
functions.description: Return the number of bytes required to encode the pn_data_t, or an error code if the data is invalid.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check for negative return values indicating errors.

functions.name: pn_data_decode
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN ssize_t pn_data_decode(pn_data_t *data, const char *bytes, size_t size);
functions.description: Decode one AMQP value from the input buffer into the pn_data_t at the current position (overwriting current if present, else appending). Returns number of bytes consumed or an error code.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
bytes must point to at least size bytes of encoded AMQP data.
Caller should manage current/parent position if overwrite vs append behavior matters.
Caller must check for negative return values indicating errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_list
functions.description: Insert an empty list node after the current node (or append) and make it the current node. Populate by enter(), put elements, then exit().
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
After calling, use pn_data_enter() before putting list elements, and pn_data_exit() when done.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_map
functions.description: Insert an empty map node as the next value/current. Populate by entering and writing alternating key/value elements.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
When filling, write alternating key then value entries inside the map.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_array
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN int pn_data_put_array(pn_data_t *data, bool described, pn_type_t type);
functions.description: Insert an empty array node of a specified element type, optionally described. If described, the first child is the descriptor (any type), followed by elements all of the declared element type.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
If described == true, the first child written after enter() must be the descriptor; subsequent children must be elements of the declared type.
All array elements must be of the specified pn_type_t type.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_described
functions.description: Insert an empty described value node. It has two children: the descriptor and the value; provide them by entering, putting descriptor then value, and exiting.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
After calling, use pn_data_enter(), then put exactly two children: descriptor then value; then pn_data_exit().
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_null
functions.description: Insert a PN_NULL scalar at the current position.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_bool
functions.description: Insert a PN_BOOL scalar with the given value.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_ubyte
functions.description: Insert a PN_UBYTE (8-bit unsigned) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Value must fit in uint8_t (enforced by type).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_byte
functions.description: Insert a PN_BYTE (8-bit signed) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Value must fit in int8_t (enforced by type).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_ushort
functions.description: Insert a PN_USHORT (16-bit unsigned) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Value must fit in uint16_t (enforced by type).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_short
functions.description: Insert a PN_SHORT (16-bit signed) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Value must fit in int16_t (enforced by type).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_uint
functions.description: Insert a PN_UINT (32-bit unsigned) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Value must fit in uint32_t (enforced by type).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_int
functions.description: Insert a PN_INT (32-bit signed) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Value must fit in int32_t (enforced by type).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_char
functions.description: Insert a PN_CHAR (32-bit Unicode code point) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
c should be a valid Unicode code point (not explicitly enforced by this header).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_ulong
functions.description: Insert a PN_ULONG (64-bit unsigned) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Value must fit in uint64_t (enforced by type).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_long
functions.description: Insert a PN_LONG (64-bit signed) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Value must fit in int64_t (enforced by type).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_timestamp
functions.description: Insert a PN_TIMESTAMP (milliseconds since epoch) scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_float
functions.description: Insert a PN_FLOAT scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_double
functions.description: Insert a PN_DOUBLE scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_decimal32
functions.description: Insert a PN_DECIMAL32 scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_decimal64
functions.description: Insert a PN_DECIMAL64 scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_decimal128
functions.description: Insert a PN_DECIMAL128 scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_uuid
functions.description: Insert a PN_UUID scalar.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_binary
functions.description: Insert a PN_BINARY value; the bytes are copied into the pn_data_t.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
bytes.size may be zero; bytes.start need not be NUL-terminated.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_string
functions.description: Insert a PN_STRING; provided bytes (UTF-8) are copied into the pn_data_t.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
string bytes are treated as UTF-8 and need not be NUL-terminated.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_symbol
functions.description: Insert a PN_SYMBOL; provided bytes (ASCII) are copied into the pn_data_t.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
symbol bytes are 7-bit ASCII and need not be NUL-terminated.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_put_atom
functions.description: Insert any scalar value from a pn_atom_t; the atom’s type field selects which union member is used.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
atom.type must be set to the correct PN_* scalar type matching the union member used.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: pn_data_get_list
functions.description: If current node is a list, return its element count; otherwise return 0. Elements are read by entering the list and iterating children.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Caller should pn_data_enter() to access list items and pn_data_exit() when done.

functions.name: pn_data_get_map
functions.description: If current node is a map, return the number of child elements (keys and values); otherwise return 0. Iterate by entering the map.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Inside the map, children appear as alternating key then value. Count is total children, so number of pairs is count/2.

functions.name: pn_data_get_array
functions.description: If current node is an array, return the number of elements; otherwise return 0. If described, the descriptor is the first child before the elements.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
To read contents, pn_data_enter() then optionally consume the descriptor (if pn_data_is_array_described()) before iterating elements.

functions.name: pn_data_is_array_described
functions.description: Return true if the current node is a described array.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Meaningful only when current node is an array.

functions.name: pn_data_get_array_type
functions.description: Return the element type of the current array node, or PN_INVALID otherwise.
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
Meaningful only when current node is an array.

functions.name: pn_data_is_described
functions.description: Return true if the current node is a described value (descriptor + value).
requirements: data must be a valid pn_data_t*.
To access descriptor and value, pn_data_enter() and iterate two children.

functions.name: pn_data_is_null
functions.description: Return true if the current node is PN_NULL.

functions.name: pn_message_errno

functions.name: pn_message_decode
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN int pn_message_decode(pn_message_t *msg, const char *bytes, size_t size);
functions.description: Clears the message and decodes AMQP-formatted binary data from bytes[0..size) into the message.
requirements: msg must be a valid pn_message_t pointer (not NULL).
bytes must point to at least size bytes of readable encoded AMQP data.
On success, any prior content of msg is cleared/replaced.
Check return value: 0 on success, non-zero error code on failure.

functions.name: pn_message_encode
functions.description: Encodes the message to AMQP-formatted bytes into the provided buffer. If the buffer is too small, returns PN_OVERFLOW and sets no data.
requirements: msg must be a valid pn_message_t pointer (not NULL).
bytes must point to at least *size bytes of writable memory on entry.
size must be non-NULL; on return, *size is set to the number of bytes written.
Caller must check return value: 0 on success, PN_OVERFLOW or other error codes on failure.

functions.name: pn_message_encode2
functions.description: Unsettled API: Encodes the message, allocating or growing buf as needed using malloc/realloc. Returns encoded length or <0 on error; details via pn_message_error(msg).
requirements: msg must be a valid pn_message_t pointer (not NULL).
buf must be non-NULL unless the caller intends to pass ownership to pn_message_send (see that API).
If buf->start == NULL, memory will be allocated with malloc().
If buf->size is too small, buffer will be expanded with realloc().
On return, buf contains the final address and size; buf->size may exceed the encoded length.
Caller is responsible for freeing buf->start if they provided buf (per typical malloc/realloc semantics).
On error (return < 0), consult pn_message_error(msg) for details.

functions.name: pn_message_send
functions.description: Unsettled API: Encodes and sends a message on a sender link. Internally uses pn_message_encode2(), pn_link_send(), and pn_link_advance(). Returns encoded length or <0 on error; details via pn_message_error(msg).
requirements: msg must be a valid pn_message_t pointer (not NULL).
sender must be a valid sending pn_link_t and a delivery must have been created before calling (see pn_delivery()).
buf may be NULL; if NULL, any memory needed for encoding is allocated and freed by pn_message_send().
If buf is non-NULL, it follows pn_message_encode2 buffer semantics (may allocate/grow with malloc/realloc).
Caller must check return value (<0 indicates error) and consult pn_message_error(msg) on error.

functions.name: pn_message_data

requirements: msg must be a valid pn_message_t pointer (not NULL).

functions.description: Gets the section offset associated with the disposition (used by PN_RECEIVED to indicate byte offset within the section).
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_disposition_set_section_offset
functions.description: Sets the section offset associated with the disposition (typically for PN_RECEIVED).
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_disposition_is_failed
functions.description: Returns whether the disposition has the failed flag set.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_disposition_set_failed
functions.description: Sets or clears the failed flag on the disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_disposition_is_undeliverable
functions.description: Returns whether the disposition has the undeliverable-here flag set.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_disposition_set_undeliverable
functions.description: Sets or clears the undeliverable-here flag on the disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_disposition_annotations
functions.description: Returns the annotations (pn_data_t) associated with the disposition. Modify before updating a delivery; data is conveyed for applicable states (e.g. PN_MODIFIED). The data must be empty or contain a symbol-keyed map. Pointer valid until the parent delivery is settled.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t
The returned pn_data_t* is valid only until the parent delivery is settled
When setting annotations, the pn_data_t must be empty or contain a symbol-keyed map
Modify annotations prior to updating the delivery for them to be sent

functions.name: pn_custom_disposition
functions.description: Converts a generic disposition to a custom disposition view, allowing access to custom disposition data and type.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_received_disposition
functions.description: Converts a generic disposition to a PN_RECEIVED disposition. Returns NULL if the disposition is not of that type.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t
Caller must handle a NULL return when disposition is not PN_RECEIVED

functions.name: pn_rejected_disposition
functions.description: Converts a generic disposition to a PN_REJECTED disposition. Returns NULL if the disposition is not of that type.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t
Caller must handle a NULL return when disposition is not PN_REJECTED

functions.name: pn_modified_disposition
functions.description: Converts a generic disposition to a PN_MODIFIED disposition. Returns NULL if the disposition is not of that type.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t
Caller must handle a NULL return when disposition is not PN_MODIFIED

functions.name: pn_declared_disposition
functions.description: Converts a generic disposition to a PN_DECLARED (transaction declared) disposition. Returns NULL if the disposition is not of that type.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t
Caller must handle a NULL return when disposition is not PN_DECLARED

functions.name: pn_transactional_disposition
functions.description: Converts a generic disposition to a PN_TRANSACTIONAL_STATE disposition. Returns NULL if the disposition is not of that type.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_disposition_t
Caller must handle a NULL return when disposition is not PN_TRANSACTIONAL_STATE

functions.name: pn_custom_disposition_data
functions.description: Returns the raw pn_data_t of a custom disposition for direct AMQP data access. Pointer is valid until the parent delivery is settled.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_custom_disposition_t
The returned pn_data_t* is valid only until the parent delivery is settled

functions.name: pn_custom_disposition_get_type
functions.description: Gets the disposition type code of a custom disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_custom_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_custom_disposition_set_type
functions.description: Sets the disposition type code on a custom disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_custom_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_rejected_disposition_condition
functions.description: Returns the condition object associated specifically with a PN_REJECTED disposition for conveying error details. Pointer valid until the parent delivery is settled.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_rejected_disposition_t
The returned pn_condition_t* is valid only until the parent delivery is settled

functions.name: pn_received_disposition_get_section_number
functions.description: Gets the section number for a PN_RECEIVED disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_received_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_received_disposition_set_section_number
functions.description: Sets the section number for a PN_RECEIVED disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_received_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_received_disposition_get_section_offset
functions.description: Gets the section offset for a PN_RECEIVED disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_received_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_received_disposition_set_section_offset
functions.description: Sets the section offset for a PN_RECEIVED disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_received_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_modified_disposition_is_failed
functions.description: Returns whether a PN_MODIFIED disposition has the failed flag set.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_modified_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_modified_disposition_set_failed
functions.description: Sets or clears the failed flag on a PN_MODIFIED disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_modified_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_modified_disposition_is_undeliverable
functions.description: Returns whether a PN_MODIFIED disposition has the undeliverable-here flag set.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_modified_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_modified_disposition_set_undeliverable
functions.description: Sets or clears the undeliverable-here flag on a PN_MODIFIED disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_modified_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_modified_disposition_annotations
functions.description: Returns the annotations (pn_data_t) associated with a PN_MODIFIED disposition. The pn_data_t must be empty or contain a symbol-keyed map. Pointer valid until the parent delivery is settled.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_modified_disposition_t
The returned pn_data_t* is valid only until the parent delivery is settled
When setting annotations, the pn_data_t must be empty or contain a symbol-keyed map

functions.name: pn_declared_disposition_get_id
functions.description: Gets the transaction id associated with a PN_DECLARED disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_declared_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_declared_disposition_set_id
functions.description: Sets the transaction id for a PN_DECLARED disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_declared_disposition_t
id must be a valid pn_bytes_t representing the transaction id

functions.name: pn_transactional_disposition_get_id
functions.description: Gets the transaction id associated with a PN_TRANSACTIONAL_STATE disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_transactional_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_transactional_disposition_set_id
functions.description: Sets the transaction id on a PN_TRANSACTIONAL_STATE disposition.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_transactional_disposition_t
id must be a valid pn_bytes_t representing the transaction id

functions.name: pn_transactional_disposition_get_outcome_type
functions.description: Gets the provisional terminal outcome type that will apply if the transaction commits successfully.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_transactional_disposition_t

functions.name: pn_transactional_disposition_set_outcome_type
functions.description: Sets the provisional terminal outcome type for a transactional disposition, used if the transaction commits successfully.
requirements: disposition must be a valid pn_transactional_disposition_t
outcome must be one of the terminal states: PN_ACCEPTED, PN_REJECTED, PN_RELEASED, or PN_MODIFIED

functions.name: pn_dtag
functions.description: Construct an AMQP delivery tag from a byte sequence. Typically used to create a unique tag to identify a delivery on a link.
requirements: bytes should point to at least size bytes of valid memory; behavior for bytes == NULL is unknown unless size is 0 (not specified).
size is the length of the tag in bytes; may be 0 for an empty tag (not explicitly stated but implied by size type).
Callers should ensure the resulting tag is suitable/unique for use on a link if used in pn_delivery().

functions.name: pn_delivery
functions.description: Create a new delivery on the given link using the supplied delivery tag. Links keep deliveries in creation order. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t* referring to an existing link.
tag must be unique among all deliveries on the same link.
On success, the returned delivery is owned by the link; manage its lifecycle via settle/abort as appropriate.
Do not reuse the tag for another delivery on the same link.

functions.name: pn_delivery_get_context
functions.description: Get the application-defined context pointer associated with the delivery. Use with pn_delivery_set_context() to store/retrieve user data.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Returned pointer is application-managed; may be NULL if none was set.

functions.name: pn_delivery_set_context
functions.description: Associate an application-defined context pointer with the delivery for later retrieval via pn_delivery_get_context().
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
context may be any pointer value, including NULL; lifetime is managed by the application.

functions.name: pn_delivery_attachments
functions.description: Get the attachments record associated with the delivery for storing arbitrary typed application data.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
The returned pn_record_t* is owned by the delivery; do not free it directly.

functions.name: pn_delivery_tag
functions.description: Return the delivery tag associated with the delivery.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.

functions.name: pn_delivery_link
functions.description: Return the parent link that owns the delivery.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
The returned link pointer remains valid as long as the link exists.

functions.name: pn_delivery_local
functions.description: Get a pointer to the local disposition for the delivery. Pointer remains valid until the delivery is settled.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Do not use the returned pn_disposition_t* after the delivery is settled.

functions.name: pn_delivery_local_state
functions.description: Return the local disposition state code for the delivery.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Interpretation of the state value follows AMQP delivery state codes (see disposition definitions).

functions.name: pn_delivery_remote
functions.description: Get a pointer to the remote disposition for the delivery. Pointer remains valid until the delivery is settled.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Do not use the returned pn_disposition_t* after the delivery is settled.

functions.name: pn_delivery_remote_state
functions.description: Return the remote disposition state code for the delivery.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Interpretation of the state value follows AMQP delivery state codes (see disposition definitions).

functions.name: pn_delivery_settled
functions.description: Return true if the delivery is settled at the remote endpoint, false otherwise.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.

functions.name: pn_delivery_pending
functions.description: Return the number of pending message bytes available for the delivery.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.

functions.name: pn_delivery_partial
functions.description: Return true if the delivery contains only part of a message and more data is expected on subsequent PN_DELIVERY events.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.

functions.name: pn_delivery_aborted
functions.description: Return true if the received delivery has been aborted by the sender; any received data should be discarded. You must still call pn_delivery_settle() to free local resources.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
If this returns true, callers must still settle the delivery to free resources.

functions.name: pn_delivery_writable
functions.description: Return true if the delivery is the current delivery on an outgoing link and the link has positive credit (i.e., it is writable).
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Only meaningful for deliveries on outgoing links.

functions.name: pn_delivery_readable
functions.description: Return true if the delivery is the current delivery on an incoming link (i.e., it is readable).
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Only meaningful for deliveries on incoming links.

functions.name: pn_delivery_updated
functions.description: Return true if the peer has communicated a new disposition for the delivery since it was last cleared. Remains true until pn_delivery_clear() is called.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Call pn_delivery_clear() to reset the updated flag when handled.

functions.name: pn_delivery_update
functions.description: Update the local disposition state of the delivery and communicate it to the peer.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
state should be a valid AMQP delivery state code as defined by the library (see proton/disposition.h).

functions.name: pn_delivery_clear
functions.description: Clear the updated flag on the delivery so future disposition changes can be detected via pn_delivery_updated().
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.

functions.name: pn_delivery_current
functions.description: Return true if the delivery is the current delivery for its link.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.

functions.name: pn_delivery_abort
functions.description: Abort a delivery being sent by the local endpoint. Any further data will not be sent; the peer should discard previously sent data. The delivery is freed and cannot be used after the call.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer for an outgoing (being sent) delivery.
Do not use the delivery after this call; it is freed.
Only call for deliveries that have not already been settled.

functions.name: pn_delivery_settle
functions.description: Settle (finalize) the delivery locally. A settled delivery can never be used again. If the delivery is current on its link, pn_link_advance(pn_delivery_link(delivery)) is called automatically.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Do not use the delivery after this call; it is settled and invalid for further operations.

functions.name: pn_delivery_dump
functions.description: Utility function that prints diagnostic details of the delivery (intended for debugging).
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
Output destination/format is determined by the library; callers should not rely on a specific format.

functions.name: pn_delivery_buffered
functions.description: Return true if the delivery has been buffered locally and has not yet been written to the wire. False does not guarantee it was written.
requirements: delivery must be a valid delivery pointer.
A false return value does not guarantee the data was sent; callers must not assume delivery to peer.

functions.name: pn_work_head
functions.description: Deprecated: Return the first delivery on the connection that has pending operations (readable, writable, or updated). Use PN_DELIVERY events instead.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Function is deprecated; new code should use the PN_DELIVERY event mechanism.

functions.name: pn_work_next
