functions.description: Deprecated: Given a delivery returned by pn_work_head() or pn_work_next(), return the next delivery on the connection that has pending operations, or NULL if none.
requirements: delivery must be a valid pn_delivery_t* previously obtained from pn_work_head() or pn_work_next().
Function is deprecated; new code should use the PN_DELIVERY event mechanism.

functions.name: pn_terminus_get_type
functions.description: Returns the AMQP terminus type (unspecified/source/target/coordinator) for the given terminus. Use to query whether a terminus is configured as a source or target.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
No side effects; safe to call multiple times.

functions.name: pn_terminus_set_type
functions.description: Sets the AMQP terminus type for the given terminus (e.g., PN_SOURCE, PN_TARGET). Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
Caller must pass a valid pn_terminus_type_t enum value.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero is an error code.

functions.name: pn_terminus_get_address
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the AMQP address string of the terminus. The returned pointer remains valid until pn_terminus_set_address() is called or the terminus is freed due to its parent link being freed.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer whose parent link has not been freed.
The returned pointer becomes invalid after calling pn_terminus_set_address() on the same terminus or when the parent link/terminus is freed; callers must not retain or use it past that point.
The returned pointer may be NULL if no address is set (not specified in header; callers should handle NULL defensively).

functions.name: pn_terminus_set_address
functions.description: Sets the AMQP address string for the terminus. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
address must point to a valid, null-terminated string if non-NULL (exact constraints beyond this are not specified).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero is an error code.
Any previously returned pointer from pn_terminus_get_address() becomes invalid after this call.

functions.name: pn_terminus_get_distribution_mode
functions.description: Gets the distribution mode for the terminus (applicable to a source), indicating how messages are distributed when multiple receivers address the same node.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
May return PN_DIST_MODE_UNSPECIFIED if not set.

functions.name: pn_terminus_set_distribution_mode
functions.description: Sets the distribution mode for the terminus (for sources). Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
mode must be a valid pn_distribution_mode_t value.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero is an error code.

functions.name: pn_terminus_get_durability
functions.description: Returns the durability mode of the terminus (non-durable, configuration-only durable, or durable deliveries).
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.

functions.name: pn_terminus_set_durability
functions.description: Sets the durability mode of the terminus. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
durability must be a valid pn_durability_t value.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero is an error code.

functions.name: pn_terminus_get_expiry_policy
functions.description: Gets the expiry policy of the terminus, which determines when the terminus is considered orphaned for the purposes of timeout.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.

functions.name: pn_terminus_has_expiry_policy
functions.description: Returns true if the terminus has an explicit expiry policy set, false otherwise.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.

functions.name: pn_terminus_set_expiry_policy
functions.description: Sets the expiry policy for the terminus. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
policy must be a valid pn_expiry_policy_t value.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero is an error code.

functions.name: pn_terminus_get_timeout
functions.description: Gets the timeout associated with the terminus (in seconds). The timeout is used with the expiry policy to determine orphaning behaviour.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.

functions.name: pn_terminus_set_timeout
functions.description: Sets the timeout (in seconds) for the terminus. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
timeout must be a valid pn_seconds_t value (exact valid range not specified).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero is an error code.

functions.name: pn_terminus_is_dynamic
functions.description: Returns true if the terminus has the dynamic flag set, false otherwise. Dynamic indicates that the node (e.g., address) may be created dynamically by the peer.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.

functions.name: pn_terminus_set_dynamic
functions.description: Sets or clears the dynamic flag on the terminus. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero is an error code.

functions.name: pn_terminus_properties
functions.description: Returns a pn_data_t handle to access/modify the AMQP properties for the terminus. The data persists while the terminus exists (until its parent link is freed). Must encode a symbol-keyed map per AMQP spec.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer whose parent link has not been freed.
The returned pn_data_t pointer remains valid only until the terminus (or its parent link) is freed.
Caller must ensure the pn_data_t content is a symbol-keyed map; other forms are invalid.
Modifications to the returned pn_data_t affect what is sent as the terminus properties.

functions.name: pn_terminus_capabilities
functions.description: Returns a pn_data_t handle to access/modify the AMQP capabilities for the terminus. The data persists while the terminus exists. Must encode an array of symbols.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer whose parent link has not been freed.
The returned pn_data_t pointer remains valid only until the terminus (or its parent link) is freed.
Caller must ensure the pn_data_t content is an array of symbols; other forms are invalid.
Modifications to the returned pn_data_t affect what is sent as the terminus capabilities.

functions.name: pn_terminus_outcomes
functions.description: Returns a pn_data_t handle to access/modify the AMQP outcomes for the terminus. The data persists while the terminus exists. Must encode an array of symbols.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer whose parent link has not been freed.
The returned pn_data_t pointer remains valid only until the terminus (or its parent link) is freed.
Caller must ensure the pn_data_t content is an array of symbols; other forms are invalid.
Modifications to the returned pn_data_t affect what is sent as the terminus outcomes.

functions.name: pn_terminus_filter
functions.description: Returns a pn_data_t handle to access/modify the AMQP filter set for a source terminus. The data persists while the terminus exists. Must encode a symbol-keyed map.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized pn_terminus_t pointer whose parent link has not been freed.
The returned pn_data_t pointer remains valid only until the terminus (or its parent link) is freed.
Caller must ensure the pn_data_t content is a symbol-keyed map; other forms are invalid.
Intended for source termini; using on non-source is not described in the header.

functions.name: pn_terminus_copy
functions.description: Copies the contents of src terminus into terminus. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure. Use to duplicate terminus configuration/state.
requirements: terminus must be a valid, initialized destination pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
src must be a valid, initialized source pn_terminus_t pointer that has not been freed.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero is an error code.
Both termini must be associated with a valid context (e.g., not freed due to parent link being freed).

functions.name: pn_sender
functions.description: Constructs a new sending link (sender) on the given session. Each sending link between two AMQP containers must be uniquely named; the API does not enforce uniqueness. Returns a new pn_link_t* or NULL on error.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t* created/opened by the application
name must point to a NUL-terminated string identifying the link; link names must be unique per connection (not enforced)
Check for a NULL return to detect construction failure

functions.name: pn_receiver
functions.description: Constructs a new receiving link (receiver) on the given session. Each receiving link between two AMQP containers must be uniquely named; the API does not enforce uniqueness. Returns a new pn_link_t* or NULL on error.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t* created/opened by the application
name must point to a NUL-terminated string identifying the link; link names must be unique per connection (not enforced)
Check for a NULL return to detect construction failure

functions.name: pn_link_free
functions.description: Frees a link object. Frees all pn_delivery_t objects associated with the link and settles any unsettled deliveries on the link. Safe to pass NULL (no-op).
requirements: If link is non-NULL, it must be a valid pn_link_t* obtained from the API
Do not use the link or any of its deliveries after calling this function

functions.name: pn_link_get_context
functions.description: Returns the application-defined context pointer associated with the link, previously set via pn_link_set_context. Returns whatever pointer was stored, or NULL if none.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_set_context
functions.description: Associates an application-defined context pointer with the link. Retrievable with pn_link_get_context.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
context may be any pointer value including NULL; lifetime/ownership is managed by the caller

functions.name: pn_link_attachments
functions.description: Returns the attachments record associated with the link. The returned pn_record_t* remains valid until the link is freed.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Do not use the returned pn_record_t* after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_link_name
functions.description: Returns the link's name as a NUL-terminated string.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
The returned pointer remains valid for the lifetime of the link

functions.name: pn_link_is_sender
functions.description: Returns true if the link is a sender, false otherwise.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_is_receiver
functions.description: Returns true if the link is a receiver, false otherwise.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_state
functions.description: Returns the endpoint state flags for the link (local/remote active/closed, etc.).
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Interpretation of returned flags follows pn_state_t semantics

functions.name: pn_link_error
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns the link’s error object for additional details after a link operation fails; may also be used to clear the condition. Pointer valid until the link is freed.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Use pn_link_condition for new code
Do not use the returned pn_error_t* after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_link_condition
functions.description: Returns the local condition associated with the link endpoint. May be modified before closing the link to communicate a condition to the remote peer. Pointer valid until the link is freed. Note: will always return an empty error object per deprecation notice.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Only modify before closing the link if you intend to signal a condition
Do not use the returned pn_condition_t* after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_link_remote_condition
functions.description: Returns the remote condition for the link endpoint. Read-only. Useful to inspect any condition indicated when the remote closed the link. Pointer valid until the link is freed.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Do not modify the returned pn_condition_t*
Do not use the returned pointer after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_link_session
functions.description: Returns the parent session that owns the link.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_head
functions.description: Returns the first link on the connection that matches the given state mask. If both local and remote flags are present, requires an exact match; if only one side present, matches if any such flags are set. state==0 matches all links.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*
state is a mask of pn_state_t flags
Use pn_link_next to iterate subsequent matches; check for NULL when no match

functions.name: pn_link_next
functions.description: Given a link previously returned by pn_link_head or pn_link_next, returns the next link on the same connection that matches the state mask. Returns NULL if no further matches.
requirements: link must be a pn_link_t* obtained from pn_link_head or pn_link_next
state is a mask of pn_state_t flags

functions.name: pn_link_open
functions.description: Opens the link. On completion, PN_LOCAL_ACTIVE will be set.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
May be called at most once per link open cycle before close/detach
Caller should drive I/O/engine to propagate the open to the peer

functions.name: pn_link_close
functions.description: Closes the link. On completion, PN_LOCAL_CLOSED will be set. If called without a prior pn_link_open, it behaves as open then close.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_detach
functions.description: Detaches the link (AMQP detach).
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_source
functions.description: Returns the locally defined source terminus for the link. Pointer is valid until the link is freed.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Do not use the returned pn_terminus_t* after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_link_target
functions.description: Returns the locally defined target terminus for the link. Pointer is valid until the link is freed.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Do not use the returned pn_terminus_t* after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_link_remote_source
functions.description: Returns the remotely defined source terminus. It will be empty until the link is remotely opened (PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE). Pointer valid until the link is freed.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Only expect non-empty data after PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE is set
Do not use the returned pointer after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_link_remote_target
functions.description: Returns the remotely defined target terminus. It will be empty until the link is remotely opened (PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE). Pointer valid until the link is freed.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Only expect non-empty data after PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE is set
Do not use the returned pointer after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_link_current
functions.description: Returns the current delivery for the link, or NULL if none. The current delivery is where send/recv operations act. It is initialized automatically when a new delivery is created and remains until advanced or settled.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
If NULL is returned, the caller must create/await a delivery before send/recv

functions.name: pn_link_advance
functions.description: Advances the current delivery pointer to the next delivery on the link. For senders: finish sending current outgoing delivery and move to next. For receivers: finish accessing current incoming delivery and move to next. Returns true if the current delivery changed (including becoming NULL).
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_credit
functions.description: Returns the current credit balance for the link. On senders this may go negative due to buffered deliveries when receiver credit is exhausted.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Interpret credit relative to link role and flow control; zero means sender must pause sending on-wire until credit is granted

functions.name: pn_link_queued
functions.description: Returns the number of queued deliveries on the link (e.g., due to insufficient credit or not yet written to the wire).
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_remote_credit
functions.description: Returns the remote view of credit for the link, defined as pn_link_credit(link) - pn_link_queued(link).
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_get_drain
functions.description: Returns true if the link is in drain mode. Only the receiving endpoint can set drain mode.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_drained
functions.description: Handles drain behavior. On a sending link in drain mode: releases excess credit back to the receiver and returns the number of credits released. On a receiving link: returns and resets the number of credits the sender has released back.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
For senders, effect occurs only if link is in drain mode; otherwise it is a no-op

functions.name: pn_link_available
functions.description: Returns a hint of the number of deliveries that might be sendable if sufficient credit were available. Used with pn_link_offered.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_snd_settle_mode
functions.description: Returns the local sender settle mode for the link.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_rcv_settle_mode
functions.description: Returns the local receiver settle mode for the link.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_set_snd_settle_mode
functions.description: Sets the local sender settle mode for the link.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
mode must be a valid pn_snd_settle_mode_t value (PN_SND_UNSETTLED, PN_SND_SETTLED, or PN_SND_MIXED)
Call before opening the link to ensure it is advertised to the peer

functions.name: pn_link_set_rcv_settle_mode
functions.description: Sets the local receiver settle mode for the link.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
mode must be a valid pn_rcv_settle_mode_t value (PN_RCV_FIRST or PN_RCV_SECOND)
Call before opening the link to ensure it is advertised to the peer

functions.name: pn_link_remote_snd_settle_mode
functions.description: Returns the remote sender settle mode for the link.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_remote_rcv_settle_mode
functions.description: Returns the remote receiver settle mode for the link.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_unsettled
functions.description: Returns the number of unsettled deliveries on the link.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_unsettled_head
functions.description: Returns the first unsettled delivery on the link, or NULL if none.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Use pn_unsettled_next to iterate further unsettled deliveries

functions.name: pn_unsettled_next
functions.description: Returns the next unsettled delivery following the given delivery, or NULL if none.
requirements: delivery must be a valid pn_delivery_t* previously returned by pn_unsettled_head or pn_unsettled_next for the same link

functions.name: pn_link_offered
functions.description: Signals the number of potentially available deliveries for a sender link (a hint to the receiver).
requirements: sender must be a valid sender pn_link_t*
credit is a non-negative integer indicating potential deliveries (semantics are a hint)

functions.name: pn_link_send
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN ssize_t pn_link_send(pn_link_t *sender, const char *bytes, size_t n);
functions.description: Sends message data bytes for the current delivery on a sender link. Returns the number of bytes sent or an error code.
requirements: sender must be a valid sender pn_link_t*
There must be a current delivery on the link (see pn_link_current)
bytes must point to a buffer of at least n bytes
Check the return value for errors (negative codes) and partial sends

functions.name: pn_link_flow
functions.description: Grants additional credit for incoming deliveries on a receiver link by incrementing its link credit.
requirements: receiver must be a valid receiver pn_link_t*
credit should be a non-negative integer to increment available credit

functions.name: pn_link_drain
functions.description: Grants credit and sets drain mode to true on a receiver link. Equivalent to granting credit and enabling drain in one call.
requirements: receiver must be a valid receiver pn_link_t*
credit should be a non-negative integer

functions.name: pn_link_set_drain
functions.description: Explicitly sets the drain mode for a receiver link.
requirements: receiver must be a valid receiver pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_recv
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN ssize_t pn_link_recv(pn_link_t *receiver, char *bytes, size_t n);
functions.description: Receives message data for the current delivery on a receiver link. Use pn_delivery_pending on the current delivery to size the buffer. Returns number of bytes received or an error code: PN_EOS when the message is completely received, 0 if no data now (expect further PN_DELIVERY events if partial), PN_STATE_ERR if no current delivery, PN_ABORTED if the delivery was aborted.
requirements: receiver must be a valid receiver pn_link_t*
There must be a current delivery on the link; otherwise PN_STATE_ERR is returned
bytes must point to a buffer with capacity at least n
Caller should loop until PN_EOS to ensure full message is read, or check (!pn_delivery_partial(d) && !pn_delivery_aborted(d) && pn_delivery_pending(d)==0)

functions.name: pn_link_draining
functions.description: Returns true if the link is currently draining (drain mode set and sender still has excess credit).
requirements: receiver must be a valid receiver pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_max_message_size
functions.description: Returns the maximum message size for the link, where 0 means unlimited.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_set_max_message_size
functions.description: Sets the maximum message size for the link; 0 means unlimited.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_remote_max_message_size
functions.description: Returns the remote peer's view of the maximum message size for the link; 0 means unlimited.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*

functions.name: pn_link_properties
functions.description: Returns a pn_data_t used to access/modify AMQP link properties to be sent when the link opens. The data must be a symbol-keyed map to be valid. Pointer valid until the link is freed.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Any data written must form a symbol-keyed map to be valid AMQP properties
Set properties before calling pn_link_open to ensure they are sent
Do not use the returned pn_data_t* after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_link_remote_properties
functions.description: Returns a pn_data_t containing the AMQP link properties supplied by the remote endpoint. It will be empty until the remote link is opened (PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE). Pointer valid until the link is freed.
requirements: link must be a valid pn_link_t*
Do not expect non-empty data until PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE is set
Do not use the returned pn_data_t* after the link is freed

functions.name: pn_session
functions.description: Create a new AMQP session on the given connection and add it to that connection's set of sessions. Use when you need a session scope for links on a pn_connection_t.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*
Returned pn_session_t* is owned by the connection; free with pn_session_free when no longer needed

functions.name: pn_session_free
functions.description: Free a session object. Frees all links on the session and settles any deliveries on those links. Safe to pass NULL.
requirements: session may be NULL (no-op)
After calling, the session will be released once internal references are no longer needed
Do not use the session or its links after freeing

functions.name: pn_session_get_context
functions.description: Return the application-defined context pointer associated with the session, previously set with pn_session_set_context.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*
Returned pointer is whatever the application set; may be NULL

functions.name: pn_session_set_context
functions.description: Associate an application-defined context pointer with the session for later retrieval via pn_session_get_context.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_attachments
functions.description: Return the attachments record associated with the session for storing arbitrary keyed data.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*
Returned pn_record_t* remains valid while the session is alive

functions.name: pn_session_state
functions.description: Return the endpoint state flags for the session (local/remote active/closed).
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_error
functions.description: Deprecated: use pn_session_condition(). Returns an error object associated with the session. Note: will always return an empty error object. Pointer valid until the session is freed.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*
Do not rely on contents for error details (deprecated and always empty)
Do not free the returned pn_error_t*; it is owned by the session

functions.name: pn_session_condition
functions.description: Return the local condition object for the session endpoint. May be modified before closing the session to communicate a condition (often errors) to the remote peer.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*
Modify only prior to pn_session_close
Do not free the returned pn_condition_t*; it is owned by the session
Pointer remains valid until the session is freed

functions.name: pn_session_remote_condition
functions.description: Return the remote condition associated with the session endpoint. Inspect to see if the peer indicated an exceptional condition when closing. Must not be modified.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*
Do not modify the returned pn_condition_t*
Do not free the returned pn_condition_t*; it is owned by the session
Pointer remains valid until the session is freed

functions.name: pn_session_connection
functions.description: Return the parent connection that owns the session.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*
Returned pn_connection_t* remains valid while the connection is alive

functions.name: pn_session_open
functions.description: Open the session endpoint. Upon completion sets PN_LOCAL_ACTIVE on the session state.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*
Call after creating the session and configuring any pre-open settings (e.g., incoming window)

functions.name: pn_session_close
functions.description: Close the session endpoint. Upon completion sets PN_LOCAL_CLOSED. If called before open, equivalent to open followed by close.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_get_incoming_capacity
functions.description: Deprecated: use pn_session_incoming_window(). Return the incoming capacity (bytes) the session can buffer for incoming message data.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_set_incoming_capacity
functions.description: Deprecated: set the incoming capacity (bytes) that the session can buffer, influencing the computed incoming window with the transport's max frame size.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*
If set, capacity must be greater than or equal to the transport's negotiated frame size
Effective only when both capacity and the transport max frame size have been set

functions.name: pn_session_incoming_window
functions.description: Return the configured maximum incoming window (as a count of transfer frames) for the session, or 0 if not set.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_incoming_window_lwm
functions.description: Return the low water mark used to govern how often the session updates the peer about incoming window changes. Zero means Proton chooses a default strategy.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_set_incoming_window_and_lwm
functions.description: Set the maximum incoming window (transfer frames) and low water mark for updates. Must be called before opening the session. Affects flow control and buffering behavior; effective only if a max frame size is also set on the session's connection.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*
Must be called before pn_session_open; otherwise returns PN_STATE_ERR
window must be non-zero; otherwise returns PN_ARG_ERR
lwm must be less than or equal to window; otherwise returns PN_ARG_ERR
If lwm is 0, Proton chooses a default updating strategy
Settings only take effect if a max frame size is set on the session's connection

functions.name: pn_session_remote_incoming_window
functions.description: Return the remote peer's current view of this session's incoming window (last communicated value minus subsequent transfers sent). Does not include transfers that may be generated from locally buffered outgoing bytes.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_get_outgoing_window
functions.description: Return the session's outgoing window size.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_set_outgoing_window
functions.description: Set the session's outgoing window size.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_outgoing_bytes
functions.description: Return the number of outgoing bytes currently buffered by the session.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_incoming_bytes
functions.description: Return the number of incoming bytes currently buffered by the session.
requirements: session must be a valid pn_session_t*

functions.name: pn_session_head
functions.description: Return the first session on the connection whose state matches the provided mask. If both local and remote flags are present, requires exact match of those flags; if only local or only remote flags are provided, matches if any of those flags are set.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*
Use together with pn_session_next to iterate all matching sessions

functions.name: pn_session_next
functions.description: Return the next session on the same connection after the given session that matches the provided state mask. Use with pn_session_head to iterate matching sessions.
requirements: session must be the previous pn_session_t* obtained from pn_session_head or pn_session_next
State mask matching semantics are as described for pn_session_head

functions.name: pn_connection
functions.description: Factory that constructs a new AMQP connection object. Use to create a connection before configuring properties (container, hostname, auth) and binding to a transport.
requirements: Callers must eventually release resources via pn_connection_free() or pn_connection_release().
The returned pointer is a new, uninitialized connection endpoint.

functions.name: pn_connection_free
functions.description: Free a connection object. Frees all pn_session_t, pn_link_t, and pn_delivery_t objects associated with the connection. Accepts NULL.
requirements: If connection is non-NULL, it must have been created by pn_connection() or otherwise be a valid pn_connection_t*.
After calling, the connection and all associated sessions, links, and deliveries are invalid.
Passing NULL is allowed and has no effect.

functions.name: pn_connection_release
functions.description: Release a connection object. Releases all pn_session_t and pn_link_t associated with it and settles all pn_delivery_t objects.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t* created by pn_connection().
After release, previously associated sessions/links are released and deliveries are settled; the connection object itself is no longer usable.

functions.name: pn_connection_error
functions.description: Deprecated: retrieve additional error information for the connection. Pointer is valid until the connection is freed. Note: will always return an empty error object in current implementation.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller may inspect or clear the returned pn_error_t; it remains valid until the connection is freed.

functions.name: pn_connection_collect
functions.description: Associate a connection with an event collector so endpoint state changes are reported as pn_event_t instances to the collector.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
collector must be a valid pn_collector_t*.
Callers should process events to avoid unbounded growth of queued events.

functions.name: pn_connection_collector
functions.description: Get the collector associated with the connection via pn_connection_collect(). Returns NULL if none set.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Returned pointer is owned elsewhere; do not free via this function.

functions.name: pn_connection_get_context
functions.description: Get the application-defined context pointer associated with the connection.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Returned pointer is whatever was set via pn_connection_set_context().

functions.name: pn_connection_set_context
functions.description: Set an application-defined context pointer on the connection for later retrieval via pn_connection_get_context().
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
context may be any pointer value; lifetime is managed by the caller.

functions.name: pn_connection_attachments
functions.description: Get the attachments record associated with the connection for storing custom key/value data.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Returned pn_record_t* is valid for the lifetime of the connection.

functions.name: pn_connection_state
functions.description: Return the endpoint state flags for the connection (combination of PN_LOCAL_* and PN_REMOTE_*).
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller should interpret flags using PN_LOCAL_MASK and PN_REMOTE_MASK if needed.

functions.name: pn_connection_open
functions.description: Open the connection endpoint. On completion, the PN_LOCAL_ACTIVE state flag will be set.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t* in an unopened or reset state.

functions.name: pn_connection_close
functions.description: Close the connection endpoint. On completion, PN_LOCAL_CLOSED will be set. If called before open, it is equivalent to open followed by close.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
May be called without a prior pn_connection_open().

functions.name: pn_connection_reset
functions.description: Reset the connection to the uninitialized state without removing contained sessions, links, or deliveries.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Callers must account for existing pn_session_t, pn_link_t, and pn_delivery_t objects remaining after reset.

functions.name: pn_connection_condition
functions.description: Get the local condition object for the connection. May be modified before closing to communicate a condition (e.g., error or redirect) on close. Pointer valid until the connection is freed.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller may modify the returned pn_condition_t prior to closing the connection.

functions.name: pn_connection_remote_condition
functions.description: Get the remote condition object set by the peer when the remote endpoint closed. The returned condition must not be modified. Pointer valid until the connection is freed.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Do not modify the returned pn_condition_t.

functions.name: pn_connection_get_container
functions.description: Get the local AMQP container-id configured for the connection. Pointer valid until pn_connection_set_container() is called or the connection is freed.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Returned pointer remains valid until next pn_connection_set_container() call or connection free.

functions.name: pn_connection_set_container
functions.description: Set the local AMQP container-id advertised by the connection.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
container must point to a valid NUL-terminated string for the duration of the call.

functions.name: pn_connection_set_user
functions.description: Set the authentication username for a client connection. Must be set before binding the connection to a transport and cannot be changed after binding.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Must be called before the connection is bound to a transport; changing it after binding is not allowed.
user must point to a valid NUL-terminated string for the duration of the call.

functions.name: pn_connection_set_password
functions.description: Set the authentication password for a client connection. Must be set before binding to a transport and cannot be changed after binding. Password is write-only; implementation copies it and zeros it after use.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Must be called before the connection is bound to a transport; changing it after binding is not allowed.
password must point to a valid NUL-terminated string for the duration of the call.

functions.name: pn_connection_set_authorization
functions.description: Set the authorization ID for a client connection. Useful if the SASL mechanism supports separate authorization identity. Must be set before binding and cannot change after binding.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Must be called before the connection is bound to a transport; changing it after binding is not allowed.
authzid must point to a valid NUL-terminated string for the duration of the call.

functions.name: pn_connection_get_user
functions.description: Get the authentication username previously set for the connection.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Returns the username that was set via pn_connection_set_user(); may be NULL if not set.

functions.name: pn_connection_get_authorization
functions.description: Get the authorization ID previously set for the connection.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Returns the authorization ID set via pn_connection_set_authorization(); may be NULL if not set.

functions.name: pn_connection_get_hostname
functions.description: Get the local AMQP hostname (virtual host) configured for the connection. Pointer valid until pn_connection_set_hostname() is called or the connection is freed.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Returned pointer remains valid until next pn_connection_set_hostname() call or connection free.

functions.name: pn_connection_set_hostname
functions.description: Set the AMQP virtual host name for the connection. Sent in the Open performative and used by SSL/SASL to identify the peer. The string is passed verbatim (not parsed as a URL).
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
hostname must be a valid NUL-terminated string for the duration of the call.
Do not include numeric IPs or port numbers unless you intend to send them verbatim as the virtual host name.

functions.name: pn_connection_remote_container
functions.description: Get the remote peer's AMQP container-id. Returns NULL until PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE. Pointer valid until the connection is unbound from a transport or freed.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller must handle NULL prior to PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE state.
Non-NULL pointer remains valid until unbind or free.

functions.name: pn_connection_remote_hostname
functions.description: Get the remote peer's AMQP hostname. Returns NULL until PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE. Pointer valid until the connection is unbound from a transport or freed.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller must handle NULL prior to PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE state.
Non-NULL pointer remains valid until unbind or free.

functions.name: pn_connection_offered_capabilities
functions.description: Access/modify the AMQP offered capabilities for the connection. Data must be an array of symbols. Pointer valid until the connection is freed.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller must ensure the pn_data_t content, if set, takes the form of an array of symbols.

functions.name: pn_connection_desired_capabilities
functions.description: Access/modify the AMQP desired capabilities for the connection. Data must be an array of symbols. Pointer valid until the connection is freed.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller must ensure the pn_data_t content, if set, takes the form of an array of symbols.

functions.name: pn_connection_properties
functions.description: Access/modify the AMQP properties for the connection. Data must be a symbol-keyed map. Pointer valid until the connection is freed.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller must ensure the pn_data_t content, if set, takes the form of a symbol-keyed map.

functions.name: pn_connection_remote_offered_capabilities
functions.description: Access the AMQP offered capabilities provided by the remote peer. Pointer valid until the connection is freed. Data is empty until PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller must handle that the returned pn_data_t will be empty until PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE.

functions.name: pn_connection_remote_desired_capabilities
functions.description: Access the AMQP desired capabilities provided by the remote peer. Pointer valid until the connection is freed. Data is empty until PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller must handle that the returned pn_data_t will be empty until PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE.

functions.name: pn_connection_remote_properties
functions.description: Access the AMQP connection properties provided by the remote peer. Pointer valid until the connection is freed. Data is empty until PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller must handle that the returned pn_data_t will be empty until PN_REMOTE_ACTIVE.

functions.name: pn_connection_transport
functions.description: Get the transport currently bound to the connection, or NULL if unbound.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Caller must handle NULL when the connection is unbound.

functions.name: pn_transport
functions.description: Factory function that creates a new AMQP transport. A transport is used by one AMQP connection to interface with the network. Initially configured as a client transport; use pn_transport_set_server() to switch to server mode.
requirements: At most one pn_connection_t can be associated with a single pn_transport_t.
Transport protocol layers for a client must be configured explicitly by the application.
Server transports may auto-configure based on incoming protocol headers.

functions.name: pn_transport_set_server
functions.description: Configure an existing transport to operate as a server transport (accepts incoming connections, may auto-configure protocol layers).
requirements: transport must refer to a valid pn_transport_t created by pn_transport().

functions.name: pn_transport_free
functions.description: Free a transport object. Automatically unbinds it from any associated connection.
requirements: transport may be NULL (a no-op).
After calling, the pn_transport_t pointer must not be used.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_user
functions.description: Retrieve the authenticated user name for the transport. On the server, this is the authenticated user. On the client, it returns the user set on the bound connection via pn_connection_set_user(). Returns "anonymous" for anonymous connections.
requirements: The returned value is only reliable after the PN_TRANSPORT_AUTHENTICATED event has been received.

functions.name: pn_transport_require_auth
functions.description: Set whether non-authenticated connections are allowed. If required is true, only authenticated connections are permitted; otherwise unauthenticated connections are allowed.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t.
This setting influences whether connections without SASL or with SASL ANONYMOUS are permitted.

functions.name: pn_transport_is_authenticated
functions.description: Report whether the transport connection is authenticated.
requirements: The authentication status may not be stable until the PN_CONNECTION_REMOTE_OPEN event is received.

functions.name: pn_transport_require_encryption
functions.description: Set whether non-encrypted connections are allowed. If required is true, the transport must use encryption (e.g., TLS or a SASL security layer).
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t.

functions.name: pn_transport_is_encrypted
functions.description: Report whether the transport connection is encrypted.
requirements: The encryption status may not be stable until the PN_CONNECTION_REMOTE_OPEN event is received.

functions.name: pn_transport_condition
functions.description: Access the transport’s condition object for additional error details (e.g., after a PN_TRANSPORT_ERROR event). The returned pointer remains valid until the transport is freed.
requirements: Callers should consult this after a negative return indicating an error from transport APIs.
The returned pn_condition_t pointer must not be used after the transport is freed.

functions.name: pn_transport_logger
functions.description: Get the transport’s logger object to control logging emitted by the transport. The pointer is valid until the transport is freed.
requirements: The returned pn_logger_t pointer must not be used after the transport is freed.

functions.name: pn_transport_error
functions.description: Deprecated: Use pn_transport_condition(). Historically returned the transport’s error. Kept for backward compatibility.
requirements: Prefer pn_transport_condition() for error details.

functions.name: pn_transport_bind
functions.description: Deprecated: Use pn_connection_driver_init(). Bind the transport to an AMQP connection. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t and connection must be a valid pn_connection_t.
Only one connection may be associated with a transport.

functions.name: pn_transport_unbind
functions.description: Deprecated: Use pn_connection_driver_destroy(). Unbind a transport from its AMQP connection. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: transport must be bound to a connection to have an effect.

functions.name: pn_transport_trace
functions.description: Update a transport’s trace flags controlling what is logged (PN_TRACE_OFF, PN_TRACE_RAW, PN_TRACE_FRM, PN_TRACE_DRV, PN_TRACE_EVT).
requirements: trace should be a bitwise combination of PN_TRACE_* flags.
Logging/tracing is marked internal and may be deprecated when logging becomes independent.

functions.name: pn_transport_set_tracer
functions.description: Set a custom tracing (logging) callback for the transport to direct log output.
requirements: tracer must be a function compatible with pn_tracer_t (void (*)(pn_transport_t*, const char*)).
Logging/tracing is marked internal and may be deprecated.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_tracer
functions.description: Get the tracing (logging) callback currently used by the transport.
requirements: Logging/tracing is marked internal and may be deprecated.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_context
functions.description: Get the application-defined context pointer associated with the transport.
requirements: The context is application-managed and is set via pn_transport_set_context().

functions.name: pn_transport_set_context
functions.description: Associate an application-defined context pointer with the transport.
requirements: context is an opaque application pointer; lifetime is managed by the application.

functions.name: pn_transport_attachments
functions.description: Get the attachments (pn_record_t) associated with the transport for storing keyed data.
requirements: The returned pn_record_t is tied to the transport’s lifetime.

functions.name: pn_transport_log
functions.description: Log a message using the transport’s logging mechanism; the message is prefixed with the transport’s identifier. Intended for debugging.
requirements: message should be a valid, null-terminated string.
Logging is marked internal and may be deprecated.

functions.name: pn_transport_vlogf
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_transport_vlogf(pn_transport_t *transport, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Log a printf-formatted message using a va_list with the transport’s logging mechanism; message is prefixed with the transport identifier.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with the variadic arguments provided via ap.
ap must be initialized for the format.
Logging is marked internal and may be deprecated.

functions.name: pn_transport_logf
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_transport_logf(pn_transport_t *transport, PN_PRINTF_FORMAT const char *fmt, ...) PN_PRINTF_FORMAT_ATTR(2, 3);
functions.description: Log a printf-formatted message using variadic arguments with the transport’s logging mechanism; message is prefixed with the transport identifier.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string for the provided variadic arguments.
Logging is marked internal and may be deprecated.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_channel_max
functions.description: Get the current maximum allowed channel number for the transport, considering implementation, remote, and application-imposed limits.
requirements: None beyond a valid transport; value reflects the minimum of implementation, remote, and application limits.

functions.name: pn_transport_set_channel_max
functions.description: Set the maximum allowed channel number for the transport (valid channel range is [0..channel_max]). Returns PN_OK on success, PN_STATE_ERR if it is too late to change.
requirements: May be called more than once to raise or lower the application-imposed limit.
Smaller limits may also be imposed by the library or remote peer.
After the OPEN frame has been sent to the remote, further calls have no effect and may return PN_STATE_ERR.

functions.name: pn_transport_remote_channel_max
functions.description: Get the maximum allowed channel number as advertised by the remote peer.
requirements: Requires a valid transport; reflects remote peer’s limit once negotiated.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_max_frame
functions.description: Get the transport’s maximum frame size.
requirements: Valid after configuration/negotiation.

functions.name: pn_transport_set_max_frame
functions.description: Set the transport’s maximum frame size. Has no effect after the transport has started sending AMQP frames. Typically set at transport creation.
requirements: Must be set before the transport starts sending AMQP frames to have an effect.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_remote_max_frame
functions.description: Get the remote peer’s maximum frame size.
requirements: Requires a valid transport; value available after negotiation.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_idle_timeout
functions.description: Get the transport’s idle timeout in milliseconds. A value of 0 means heartbeats are disabled.
requirements: None beyond a valid transport.

functions.name: pn_transport_set_idle_timeout
functions.description: Set the transport’s idle timeout in milliseconds. A value of 0 disables heartbeats.
requirements: timeout is in milliseconds; 0 disables heartbeats.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_remote_idle_timeout
functions.description: Get the remote peer’s idle timeout in milliseconds. A value of 0 means remote heartbeats are disabled.
requirements: Requires a valid transport; value available after negotiation.

functions.name: pn_transport_input
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN ssize_t pn_transport_input(pn_transport_t *transport, const char *bytes, size_t available);
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Push input bytes into the transport. Returns number of bytes consumed or a negative error code.
requirements: bytes points to at least 'available' bytes of input data.
On error (negative return), further details can be obtained from pn_transport_condition().

functions.name: pn_transport_output
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN ssize_t pn_transport_output(pn_transport_t *transport, char *bytes, size_t size);
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Obtain output bytes from the transport into the provided buffer. Returns number of bytes written or a negative error code.
requirements: bytes must point to a buffer of at least 'size' bytes.
On error (negative return), consult pn_transport_condition().

functions.name: pn_transport_capacity
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Get free space for input following the transport’s tail pointer. Negative return indicates EOS or error; consult pn_transport_condition() for details.
requirements: Callers should handle negative returns (PN_EOS or error codes).
Calls to pn_transport_process() may change the capacity and tail pointer.

functions.name: pn_transport_tail
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Get the transport’s input tail pointer. The free space after this pointer is given by pn_transport_capacity().
requirements: May return NULL if no capacity is available.
Calls to pn_transport_process() may change the tail pointer and capacity.

functions.name: pn_transport_push
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN ssize_t pn_transport_push(pn_transport_t *transport, const char *src, size_t size);
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Push bytes into the transport’s input (equivalent to copying bytes after the tail pointer then calling pn_transport_process(size)). Returns number of bytes pushed or a negative error code.
requirements: Only up to the available capacity will be pushed; use pn_transport_capacity() to determine capacity.
On error (negative return), consult pn_transport_condition().

functions.name: pn_transport_process
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Consume 'size' bytes of input that were written after the tail pointer. May change the tail pointer and capacity.
requirements: size must be the amount of data written to the transport’s input buffer after the tail pointer.
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code.

functions.name: pn_transport_close_tail
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Indicate that the input has reached End Of Stream (EOS). No more input will be provided.
requirements: Returns 0 on success or a negative error code.

functions.name: pn_transport_pending
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Get the number of pending output bytes after the head pointer. Negative value indicates EOS or error; consult pn_transport_condition().
requirements: Calls to pn_transport_pop() may change the head pointer and pending count.

functions.name: pn_transport_head
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Get the transport’s output head pointer referencing queued output data. The number of bytes following is given by pn_transport_pending().
requirements: May return NULL if no pending output.
Calls to pn_transport_pop() may alter this pointer and the referenced data.

functions.name: pn_transport_peek
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN ssize_t pn_transport_peek(pn_transport_t *transport, char *dst, size_t size);
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Copy 'size' bytes from the output head into dst. Returns number of bytes copied or a negative error code.
requirements: size must be less than or equal to the value returned by pn_transport_pending().
dst must point to a buffer with capacity of at least 'size' bytes.

functions.name: pn_transport_pop
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Remove 'size' bytes of output from the pending queue after the head pointer. May update the head pointer and pending count.
requirements: size must be the number of bytes to remove; callers should ensure it does not exceed pn_transport_pending().

functions.name: pn_transport_close_head
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Indicate that output has closed; no more output will be popped.
requirements: Returns 0 on success or a negative error code.

functions.name: pn_transport_quiesced
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Return true if the transport has no buffered data.
requirements: Requires a valid transport.

functions.name: pn_transport_head_closed
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Return true if pn_transport_close_head() has been called.
requirements: Requires a valid transport.

functions.name: pn_transport_tail_closed
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Return true if pn_transport_close_tail() has been called.
requirements: Requires a valid transport.

functions.name: pn_transport_closed
functions.description: Deprecated: Use the connection_driver API. Equivalent to pn_transport_head_closed(transport) && pn_transport_tail_closed(transport).
requirements: Requires a valid transport.

functions.name: pn_transport_tick
functions.description: Process pending transport timer events and return the monotonic deadline for the next pending timer event (or 0 if none). Should be called after processing input and before generating output. Does nothing until first data is read from or written to the transport.
requirements: now must be a monotonically increasing time value in milliseconds (not necessarily wall-clock).
If the return is non-zero, the caller must invoke pn_transport_tick again at or before the returned deadline.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_frames_output
functions.description: Deprecated: No replacement. Get the number of frames output by the transport.
requirements: Requires a valid transport pointer; read-only.

functions.name: pn_transport_get_frames_input
functions.description: Deprecated: No replacement. Get the number of frames input by the transport.
requirements: Requires a valid transport pointer; read-only.

functions.name: pn_transport_connection
functions.description: Access the AMQP connection associated with the transport, or NULL if none.
requirements: Requires a valid transport.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_init
functions.description: Initialize a connection driver with the provided connection and transport, creating missing ones if NULL. The driver takes ownership of the provided connection/transport and will free them on destroy. Transport binding happens automatically after PN_CONNECTION_INIT is handled, or can be forced via pn_connection_driver_bind(). Use this to set up an AMQP connection driver before IO handling.
requirements: d must point to an initialized pn_connection_driver_t struct memory.
If connection or transport are non-NULL, the caller transfers ownership to the driver; do not free or use them independently after initialization.
If you need to set username/password or server role, call pn_connection_set_username(), pn_connection_set_password(), pn_transport_set_server() before the transport is bound.
Check the return value; returns PN_OUT_OF_MEMORY on allocation failure.
Eventually call pn_connection_driver_destroy() to free resources owned by the driver.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_bind
functions.description: Force binding of the transport to the connection driver. Normally binding occurs automatically after PN_CONNECTION_INIT is processed; this call binds earlier.
requirements: d must be a valid, initialized driver.
Do not call if the transport is already bound; the function returns PN_STATE_ERR in that case.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_destroy
functions.description: Unbind, release, and free the connection and transport owned by the driver, and set their pointers to NULL. Does not free the pn_connection_driver_t struct itself.
requirements: The driver pointer must be valid.
After this call, do not use the connection or transport pointers from the driver (they are set to NULL and freed).
Call this to free memory once pn_connection_driver_finished() is true or when you are done with the driver.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_release_connection
functions.description: Disassociate the driver's connection from its transport and collector, set d->connection to NULL, and return the previous connection pointer. The returned connection becomes the caller's responsibility to free. Transport and collector remain owned by the driver and will be freed by pn_connection_driver_destroy(). Not related to pn_connection_release().
requirements: d must be a valid driver.
The caller assumes ownership of the returned pn_connection_t and must free it appropriately.
Do not free the driver's transport or collector; they remain owned by the driver.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_read_buffer_sized
functions.description: Request a read buffer, attempting to grow it to at least n bytes, and return the available buffer (which may be smaller). Copy incoming bytes into buf.start up to buf.size and then call pn_connection_driver_read_done() with the number of bytes provided. If buf.size==0, reading is not possible (no buffer space or read side closed).
requirements: The driver must be valid and not have the read side closed to receive a non-zero buffer.
Do not write more than buf.size bytes to buf.start.
Call pn_connection_driver_read_done(d, nbytes) after copying data, where nbytes is the number of bytes written (0 <= nbytes <= buf.size).
If buf.size == 0, do not attempt to read or write into buf.start.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_read_buffer
functions.description: Get the current read buffer for receiving incoming bytes. Copy up to buf.size bytes into buf.start and then call pn_connection_driver_read_done(). If buf.size==0, reading is not possible (no buffer space or read side closed).
requirements: The driver must be valid and read side must be open to obtain a non-zero buffer.
Do not write more than buf.size bytes to buf.start.
Call pn_connection_driver_read_done(d, nbytes) after copying data (0 <= nbytes <= buf.size).
If buf.size == 0, do not attempt to read or write into buf.start.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_read_done
functions.description: Notify the driver that the first n bytes placed in the most recently obtained read buffer are ready to be processed and reclaim the buffer space.
requirements: Call only after obtaining a read buffer via pn_connection_driver_read_buffer[_sized]().
n must be the number of bytes actually written into the provided buffer and must not exceed the size of that buffer.
Calling with n > last buf.size causes undefined/invalid behavior (not specified in header).

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_read_close
functions.description: Close the read side of the connection driver when further IO reads are not possible.
requirements: Call when the IO source can no longer provide data (read side shutdown).
After closing, expect pn_connection_driver_read_buffer() to return buf.size==0 and pn_connection_driver_read_closed() to be true.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_read_closed
functions.description: Return true if the read side is closed.
requirements: The driver pointer must be valid.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_write_buffer
functions.description: Get the buffer containing encoded bytes ready to be written to the output IO. Write up to buf.size bytes from buf.start to the destination, then call pn_connection_driver_write_done() with the number of bytes written. If buf.size==0, there is currently nothing to write.
requirements: The driver must be valid and write side must be open to obtain non-zero data.
Do not attempt to write more than buf.size bytes.
Call pn_connection_driver_write_done(d, nbytes) after writing (0 <= nbytes <= buf.size).
If buf.size == 0, skip writing.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_write_done
functions.description: Inform the driver that the first n bytes returned by the last pn_connection_driver_write_buffer() call have been written to the IO. Reclaims written buffer space and resets/updates the write buffer; returns the (possibly updated) write buffer state.
requirements: Call only after a preceding pn_connection_driver_write_buffer() call.
n must be the number of bytes actually written and must not exceed the size of the last returned write buffer.
Use the returned pn_bytes_t to continue writing remaining data, if any.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_write_close
functions.description: Close the write side of the connection driver when further IO writes are not possible.
requirements: Call when the IO sink can no longer accept data (write side shutdown).
After closing, expect pn_connection_driver_write_buffer() to eventually return buf.size==0 and pn_connection_driver_write_closed() to be true.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_write_closed
functions.description: Return true if the write side is closed.
requirements: The driver pointer must be valid.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_close
functions.description: Close both the read and write sides of the connection driver.
requirements: The driver pointer must be valid.
After closing both sides, no further read buffers will be available and no more bytes will be produced for writing.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_next_event
functions.description: Get the next event to handle from the driver's event queue. Returns NULL if no event is currently available; further reading or writing may produce more. The returned pointer is valid only until the next call to pn_connection_driver_next_event().
requirements: Use the returned pn_event_t* only until the next call to pn_connection_driver_next_event(); do not retain it longer.
The driver must be valid.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_has_event
functions.description: Return true if pn_connection_driver_next_event() will return a non-NULL event.
requirements: The driver pointer must be valid.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_finished
functions.description: Return true if the driver is closed for both reading and writing and there are no more events pending. When finished is true, call pn_connection_driver_destroy() to free related memory.
requirements: The driver pointer must be valid.
If this returns true, the caller should call pn_connection_driver_destroy() to free resources.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_errorf
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_connection_driver_errorf(pn_connection_driver_t *d, const char *name, PN_PRINTF_FORMAT const char *fmt, ...) PN_PRINTF_FORMAT_ATTR(3, 4);
functions.description: Set a transport error on the driver's transport, with a name and a formatted description. The error will be surfaced as a PN_TRANSPORT_ERROR event from pn_connection_driver_next_event(). Must be called before closing the read or write sides to ensure the error is processed.
requirements: d must be a valid driver.
Call before pn_connection_driver_read_close() or pn_connection_driver_write_close() to ensure the error is emitted as an event.
name should identify the condition; fmt must be a valid printf-style format string and the variadic arguments must match it.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_verrorf
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_connection_driver_verrorf(pn_connection_driver_t *d, const char *name, const char *fmt, va_list);
functions.description: va_list variant of pn_connection_driver_errorf(); sets a transport error with name and formatted description using an existing va_list.
requirements: d must be a valid driver.
Call before pn_connection_driver_read_close() or pn_connection_driver_write_close() to ensure the error is emitted as an event.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with the provided va_list.

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_log
functions.description: Deprecated: log a message for the connection driver. Prefer pn_transport_log().
requirements: d must be valid if used.
For new code, do not use; replace with pn_transport_log().

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_logf
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_connection_driver_logf(pn_connection_driver_t *d, PN_PRINTF_FORMAT const char *fmt, ...) PN_PRINTF_FORMAT_ATTR(2, 3);
functions.description: Deprecated: printf-style logging for the connection driver. Prefer pn_transport_logf().
requirements: d must be valid if used.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string and the variadic arguments must match it.
For new code, do not use; replace with pn_transport_logf().

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_vlogf
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_connection_driver_vlogf(pn_connection_driver_t *d, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Deprecated: va_list printf-style logging for the connection driver. Prefer pn_transport_vlogf().
requirements: d must be valid if used.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with ap.
For new code, do not use; replace with pn_transport_vlogf().

functions.name: pn_connection_driver_ptr
functions.description: Return a pointer to the pn_connection_driver_t* field stored within a pn_connection_t. Intended only for IO integration writers; if using the standard pn_proactor_t you must not use this. The double pointer enables atomic load/store by the caller if desired.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t pointer.
Only IO integration code should call this; do not use if you rely on pn_proactor_t.

functions.name: pn_listener
functions.description: Create a new listener object to be passed to pn_proactor_listen(). You can attach application data via pn_listener_attachments() to be accessed when accepting connections. Thread safety: listeners follow core-object rules; calls to a single listener must be serialized except pn_listener_close().
requirements: Calls that operate on the same pn_listener_t must be serialized from the application thread(s), except pn_listener_close() which is thread-safe.
Intended for use with pn_proactor_listen(); otherwise, lifecycle management is application-defined.
Returned pointer must be checked by the caller before use if defensive coding is required (success/failure details are not documented here).

functions.name: pn_listener_free
functions.description: Free a listener object. Typically only needed if you created a listener with pn_listener() but never passed it to pn_proactor_listen().
requirements: Only call if the listener was not passed to pn_proactor_listen() (implied by documentation).
The pn_listener_t* must refer to a valid, unfreed listener.
Do not use the listener after calling pn_listener_free().
Calls operating on a given listener (including free) must be serialized by the caller; see listener thread-safety note.

functions.name: pn_listener_accept2
functions.description: Accept an incoming connection on a listener using an optional pre-configured connection and transport. Must be called in response to a PN_LISTENER_ACCEPT event. If connection or transport is NULL, a new one is created. Errors surface as PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED events via pn_proactor_wait(). If you supply a transport, this call marks it as a server via pn_transport_set_server(); however, when using SASL, you must call pn_transport_set_server() yourself before invoking pn_sasl() to set up a server SASL configuration. Memory management for created objects is the same as pn_proactor_connect2() (details not provided here).
requirements: Must be called only after receiving a PN_LISTENER_ACCEPT event for the listener.
If providing a pn_transport_t and using SASL, the caller must call pn_transport_set_server() before calling pn_sasl().
If a pn_transport_t is provided, pn_listener_accept2() will call pn_transport_set_server() on it.
The provided pn_connection_t and pn_transport_t, if non-NULL, must be valid and in a state suitable for accepting a new incoming connection (precise prep steps not documented here).
If connection or transport is NULL, the function creates a new object; memory management semantics are the same as pn_proactor_connect2() (exact details not specified here).
Listener API calls (other than pn_listener_close) must be serialized for a single listener.

functions.name: pn_listener_accept
functions.description: Deprecated: use pn_listener_accept2(). Accepts an incoming connection using an optional pre-configured connection. Specific memory-management and transport behavior are not documented here; refer to pn_listener_accept2() for current semantics.
requirements: Deprecated API; new code should call pn_listener_accept2() instead.
Should be called in response to a PN_LISTENER_ACCEPT event (inferred from the accept2 replacement and naming).
The provided pn_connection_t, if non-NULL, must be valid (other specifics unknown).
Listener method calls (other than pn_listener_close) must be serialized for a given listener.

functions.name: pn_listener_condition
functions.description: Return the error condition associated with a listener. Use to inspect error state if operations fail.
requirements: The listener pointer must refer to a valid listener.
The returned pn_condition_t* is associated with the listener; ownership and lifetime semantics are not stated here (do not assume it should be freed by the caller).
Calls on a single listener must be serialized (except pn_listener_close).

functions.name: pn_listener_get_context
functions.description: Get the application context pointer associated with the listener (set via pn_listener_set_context).
requirements: listener must be a valid, initialized pn_listener_t*.
Returned pointer may be NULL if no context is set (not explicitly documented but typical for context accessors).
Listener-related calls must be serialized (except pn_listener_close).

functions.name: pn_listener_set_context
functions.description: Associate an application-defined context pointer with the listener so it can be retrieved by pn_listener_get_context().
requirements: listener must be a valid, initialized pn_listener_t*.
The context pointer is opaque to the library; its allocation and lifetime are managed by the caller.
Listener-related calls must be serialized (except pn_listener_close).

functions.name: pn_listener_attachments
functions.description: Return the attachment record (pn_record_t) associated with the listener. Applications can store and retrieve key/value-like data here, including data used when accepting connections.
requirements: listener must be a valid pn_listener_t*.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned pn_record_t is tied to the listener (exact rules not stated; do not free it directly unless documented elsewhere).
Calls on the same listener must be serialized (except pn_listener_close).

functions.name: pn_listener_close
functions.description: Close the listener. A PN_LISTENER_CLOSE event will be generated when the listener has stopped listening. This call is thread-safe.
requirements: Thread-safe: may be called concurrently with other operations.
Must not be called after the PN_LISTENER_CLOSE event has been handled, as the listener may be freed.
The listener pointer must refer to a valid listener at the time of call.

functions.name: pn_listener_proactor
functions.description: Return the proactor associated with the given listener.
requirements: The listener must be valid and associated with a proactor (association timing not specified here).
Do not assume ownership of the returned pn_proactor_t*; lifetime is managed by the proactor subsystem.
Calls on the same listener must be serialized (except pn_listener_close).

functions.name: pn_event_listener
functions.description: Return the listener associated with an event, or NULL if the event is not associated with a listener.
requirements: event must be a valid pn_event_t*.
Caller must handle a NULL return if the event is not associated with a listener.

functions.name: pn_listener_raw_accept
functions.description: Accept an incoming connection as a raw connection. Must be called after a PN_LISTENER_ACCEPT event. Errors are reported as PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED via pn_proactor_wait(). The proactor owning the listener takes ownership of the provided raw connection and will free it automatically after the final PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED event is handled or when pn_proactor_free() is called. Note: the header comment contains a contradiction about whether raw_connection may be NULL; the parameter is documented both as "cannot be null" and "If NULL a new connection is created." Treat this as ambiguous and prefer the stricter requirement (non-NULL) unless authoritative documentation clarifies otherwise.
requirements: Must be called only after receiving a PN_LISTENER_ACCEPT event for the listener.
raw_connection must be created by pn_raw_connection().

Ownership: after calling, the listener’s proactor takes ownership of raw_connection; the caller must not free it and must not use it after handing it over, except via events/callbacks defined by the proactor.
Error reporting occurs via PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED events returned by pn_proactor_wait(); callers must be prepared to handle these events.
Due to contradictory parameter docs, treat raw_connection as required (non-NULL) unless the specific library version guarantees NULL is allowed.
Listener method calls (other than pn_listener_close) must be serialized for a given listener.

functions.name: pn_netaddr_str
functions.signature: int pn_netaddr_str(const pn_netaddr_t *addr, char *buf, size_t size);
