functions.description: Format a human-readable string for the given network address into buf. Returns the length of the formatted string (excluding the terminating '\0'). If the returned length is >= size, the output was truncated. Typical usage: format an address for logging or display.
requirements: addr must point to a valid pn_netaddr_t obtained from the Proton library; it must remain valid for the duration of the call.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes.
size is the capacity of buf in bytes; if size is too small, the output will be truncated.
If size is 0, behavior and guarantees about writing or termination are unknown (not documented).

functions.name: pn_transport_local_addr
functions.description: Return the local (bound) network address associated with the given transport, or NULL if not available. The returned pointer becomes invalid after the transport closes (after the PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED event is handled). Use with pn_netaddr_str(), pn_netaddr_host_port(), or pn_netaddr_sockaddr() to inspect details.
requirements: t must be a valid, initialized pn_transport_t.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is read-only and becomes invalid after the PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED event is handled for t; do not access it after that point.
Caller must check for a NULL return to handle cases where the address is not available.

functions.name: pn_transport_remote_addr
functions.description: Return the remote peer's network address associated with the given transport, or NULL if not available. The returned pointer becomes invalid after the transport closes (after the PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED event is handled).
requirements: t must be a valid, initialized pn_transport_t.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is read-only and becomes invalid after the PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED event is handled for t; do not access it after that point.
Caller must check for a NULL return to handle cases where the address is not available.

functions.name: pn_listener_addr
functions.description: Return the first listening address associated with the given listener, or NULL if no addresses are available. Addresses are only available after the PN_LISTENER_OPEN event. A listener may expose multiple addresses (for example due to DNS, multi-homed hosts, or IPv4/IPv6); iterate them with pn_netaddr_next(). The returned pointer becomes invalid after the listener closes (after the PN_LISTENER_CLOSED event is handled).
requirements: l must be a valid, initialized pn_listener_t.
Call only after the PN_LISTENER_OPEN event for l; before that, addresses may not be available.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is read-only and becomes invalid after the PN_LISTENER_CLOSED event is handled for l; do not access it after that point.
Caller must check for a NULL return to handle cases where no addresses are available.
Use pn_netaddr_next() to iterate any additional addresses in the list.

functions.name: pn_netaddr_next
functions.description: Given an address that is part of an address list (e.g., from pn_listener_addr()), return the next address in the list, or NULL if at the end of the list or if the provided address is not part of a list.
requirements: na must be a pointer to a valid pn_netaddr_t, typically obtained from this API (e.g., pn_listener_addr).
If na is not part of a list, the function returns NULL.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, should be treated as read-only and shares the lifetime constraints of the owning object (e.g., listener or transport).

functions.name: pn_netaddr_sockaddr
functions.description: On POSIX or Windows platforms, return a pointer to the underlying struct sockaddr for the given network address. Returns NULL if not available (e.g., unsupported platform or address type). The returned pointer is const and should not be modified.
requirements: na must be a valid pn_netaddr_t.
Caller must check for a NULL return and handle the case where a sockaddr view is not available.
The returned pointer is read-only and only valid while the underlying pn_netaddr_t (and its owning object) remain valid.

functions.name: pn_netaddr_socklen
functions.description: Return the size, in bytes, of the underlying struct sockaddr for the given network address on POSIX or Windows. Returns 0 if not available.
requirements: na must be a valid pn_netaddr_t.
Caller must handle a 0 return value indicating that no sockaddr representation is available.

functions.name: pn_netaddr_host_port
functions.signature: int pn_netaddr_host_port(const pn_netaddr_t *na, char *host, size_t hlen, char *port, size_t plen);
functions.description: Extract the host and service/port for the given network address into separate strings. Returns 0 on success, non-0 on error. Useful for logging or user-facing display of address components.
requirements: na must be a valid pn_netaddr_t.
host must point to a writable buffer of at least hlen bytes; hlen is the capacity of host. Exact truncation/termination behavior if too small is not documented.
port must point to a writable buffer of at least plen bytes; plen is the capacity of port. Exact truncation/termination behavior if too small is not documented.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-0 indicates an error (details unspecified).

functions.name: pn_netaddr_local
functions.description: Deprecated. Use pn_transport_local_addr(). Returns the local address of a transport or NULL if not available. The returned pointer becomes invalid after the PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED event is handled.
requirements: t must be a valid pn_transport_t.
Caller must prefer pn_transport_local_addr(); this function is deprecated.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is read-only and becomes invalid after the PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED event is handled.
Caller must check for a NULL return.

functions.name: pn_netaddr_remote
functions.description: Deprecated. Use pn_transport_remote_addr(). Returns the remote address of a transport or NULL if not available. The returned pointer becomes invalid after the PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED event is handled.
requirements: t must be a valid pn_transport_t.
Caller must prefer pn_transport_remote_addr(); this function is deprecated.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is read-only and becomes invalid after the PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED event is handled.
Caller must check for a NULL return.

functions.name: pn_netaddr_listening
functions.description: Deprecated. Use pn_listener_addr(). Returns the first listening address for the given listener, or NULL if none are available. The returned pointer becomes invalid after the PN_LISTENER_CLOSED event is handled.
requirements: l must be a valid pn_listener_t.
Caller must prefer pn_listener_addr(); this function is deprecated.
Call after the PN_LISTENER_OPEN event to ensure addresses are available.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is read-only and becomes invalid after the PN_LISTENER_CLOSED event is handled.
Caller must check for a NULL return.

functions.name: pn_sasl
functions.description: Create or return the SASL layer associated with the given transport. Calling this on the client ensures the AMQP SASL layer is used. For server-side (incoming) connections, you must configure the transport as a server before obtaining the SASL layer. Returns the pn_sasl_t handle for further SASL configuration and queries.
requirements: For incoming (server) connections, pn_transport_set_server() must be called before pn_sasl() to set up a server SASL configuration.
Caller must hold a valid pn_transport_t* that refers to an initialized transport object (inferred from API usage; NULL handling is unspecified).
The returned pn_sasl_t* must be used only with the associated transport.

functions.name: pn_sasl_extended
functions.description: Report whether the library supports extended SASL negotiation (via an external library such as Cyrus SASL) beyond the basic mechanisms (ANONYMOUS, EXTERNAL on client/server, and PLAIN on client). Returns true if extended mechanisms are supported, false otherwise.

functions.name: pn_sasl_done
functions.description: Deprecated. Formerly used by servers to set the outcome of SASL negotiation. The header explicitly states there is no correct way to use this API; do not use in new code.
requirements: Do not use; API is deprecated and documented as having no correct usage.
If used for legacy reasons, pass a valid pn_sasl_t* and a pn_sasl_outcome_t value (actual effects and constraints are unspecified).

functions.name: pn_sasl_outcome
functions.description: Retrieve the current result of SASL negotiation. Returns one of pn_sasl_outcome_t values, including PN_SASL_NONE if negotiation has not completed.
requirements: Caller must handle PN_SASL_NONE (negotiation not completed) and other failure outcomes appropriately.
sasl must refer to a valid SASL layer associated with a transport (NULL handling is unspecified).

functions.name: pn_sasl_get_user
functions.description: Get the authenticated user name. On servers, returns the authenticated user. On clients, returns the user passed to pn_transport_set_user_password(). If SASL was not negotiated, returns NULL. If ANONYMOUS is used, returns the literal "anonymous". The value is only reliable after PN_TRANSPORT_AUTHENTICATED has been received.
requirements: Only rely on the returned value after the PN_TRANSPORT_AUTHENTICATED event.
Caller must handle a NULL return if SASL was not negotiated or authentication failed (pn_sasl_outcome() != PN_SASL_OK).
sasl must refer to a valid SASL layer.

functions.name: pn_sasl_get_authorization
functions.description: Get the requested authorization id (authzid). On servers, returns the requested authorization id. On clients, returns the value passed to pn_transport_set_authorization(). The value is only reliable after PN_TRANSPORT_AUTHENTICATED. Returns NULL if SASL was not negotiated, if ANONYMOUS was used, or if no authorization id was requested.
requirements: Only rely on the returned value after the PN_TRANSPORT_AUTHENTICATED event.
Caller must handle a NULL return (not negotiated, ANONYMOUS, or no authzid requested).
sasl must refer to a valid SASL layer.

functions.name: pn_sasl_get_mech
functions.description: Return the SASL mechanism selected by negotiation (e.g., PLAIN, EXTERNAL, ANONYMOUS). The value is only reliable after PN_TRANSPORT_AUTHENTICATED has been received.
requirements: Only rely on the returned value after the PN_TRANSPORT_AUTHENTICATED event.
sasl must refer to a valid SASL layer.
Caller should be prepared for NULL or unspecified value prior to authentication completing (implied by reliability note).

functions.name: pn_sasl_allowed_mechs
functions.description: Restrict the SASL mechanisms that may be used to those listed in the space-separated string mechs. Can be called on either client or server. Note: GSSAPI and GSS-SPNEGO are disabled by default on clients and must be explicitly enabled in this list if required.
requirements: mechs must be a space-separated list of mechanism names understood by the SASL subsystem.
To enable GSSAPI or GSS-SPNEGO on clients, include them explicitly in mechs.
sasl must refer to a valid SASL layer.

functions.name: pn_sasl_set_allow_insecure_mechs
functions.description: Control whether clear-text password mechanisms (notably PLAIN over unencrypted connections) are allowed. By default insecure mechanisms are disallowed to avoid exposing passwords. Set insecure to true to permit unencrypted PLAIN authentication.
requirements: Understand that setting insecure=true allows clear-text password mechanisms on unencrypted connections.
sasl must refer to a valid SASL layer.

functions.name: pn_sasl_get_allow_insecure_mechs
functions.description: Return the current allow_insecure_mechs setting that controls whether clear-text mechanisms are permitted on unencrypted connections.
requirements: sasl must refer to a valid SASL layer.

functions.name: pn_sasl_config_name
functions.description: Set the SASL configuration name. The implementation constructs the configuration filename by appending ".conf" to this name and searching in the configured path. Defaults to "proton-server" (server) or "proton-client" (client) if not set.
requirements: name is the base configuration name used to locate the SASL config (the function expects a string; NULL handling is unspecified).
sasl must refer to a valid SASL layer.

functions.name: pn_sasl_config_path
functions.description: Set the SASL configuration search path. Current implementation accepts a colon-separated list of directories. If both this API and the PN_SASL_CONFIG_PATH environment variable are used, this API takes precedence. If not set, the underlying implementation default is used.
requirements: path should be a colon-separated list of directories (format per current implementation).
If PN_SASL_CONFIG_PATH is also set, this explicit setting overrides it.
sasl must refer to a valid SASL layer.

functions.name: pnx_sasl_logf
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pnx_sasl_logf(pn_transport_t *transport, pn_log_level_t level, PN_PRINTF_FORMAT const char *format, ...) PN_PRINTF_FORMAT_ATTR(3, 4);
functions.description: Internal logging helper for SASL implementations. Emits a formatted log message associated with the given transport at the specified log level. Intended to be used by SASL plugins while processing authentication or security-layer operations.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
format must be a NUL-terminated printf-style format string
The variadic arguments must match the format string as per printf rules (enforced by PN_PRINTF_FORMAT_ATTR)
May be called from SASL implementation callbacks when logging is needed

functions.name: pnx_sasl_error
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pnx_sasl_error(pn_transport_t *transport, const char* err, const char* condition_name);
functions.description: Report a SASL-related error for the given transport with an error message and condition name. Intended for SASL plugins to signal failures.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
err should point to a NUL-terminated description string (unknown lifetime requirements)
condition_name should point to a NUL-terminated condition identifier string (unknown format)

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_context
functions.description: Retrieve the SASL implementation’s opaque context pointer previously associated with this transport.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context

functions.name: pnx_sasl_set_context
functions.description: Associate an opaque implementation-defined context pointer with the transport’s SASL state. Typically used by a SASL plugin to store per-connection state.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
context may be NULL or implementation-defined (lifetime/ownership rules are unknown)

functions.name: pnx_sasl_is_client
functions.description: Return true if the SASL role for this transport is client, false if server.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context

functions.name: pnx_sasl_is_mechanism_included
functions.description: Test whether the provided mechanism token s is included/allowed for this transport. Intended for SASL plugins when negotiating mechanisms.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
s must be a valid pn_bytes_t buffer containing a mechanism name; content format beyond that is unknown

functions.name: pnx_sasl_is_transport_encrypted
functions.description: Return true if a SASL or SASL-negotiated security layer is providing encryption for this transport.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_allow_insecure_mechanisms
functions.description: Return whether insecure SASL mechanisms are permitted for this transport according to configuration/policy.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_authentication_required
functions.description: Return whether authentication is required for this transport.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_external_username
functions.description: Get the externally provided username (e.g., from external auth such as TLS) associated with this transport, if any.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
The returned pointer is owned by the transport/SASL layer and must not be modified; it may be NULL if unavailable (not specified in header; treat as unknown)

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_external_ssf
functions.description: Get the external security strength factor (SSF) for this transport if provided by an external security layer.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_username
functions.description: Return the SASL username (authentication identity) for this transport, if available.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
The returned pointer is owned by the transport/SASL layer and must not be modified; NULLability is unknown

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_password
functions.description: Return the SASL password/secret for this transport, if available. Typically used by client-side mechanisms.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
The returned pointer is owned by the transport/SASL layer and must not be modified; callers should treat the value as sensitive and avoid logging; NULLability is unknown

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_authorization
functions.description: Return the SASL authorization identity (authzid) for this transport, if set.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
The returned pointer is owned by the transport/SASL layer and must not be modified; NULLability is unknown

functions.name: pnx_sasl_clear_password
functions.description: Clear any stored password/secret from the SASL state associated with the transport.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_remote_fqdn
functions.description: Return the remote fully qualified domain name (FQDN) used/seen by SASL for this transport.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
The returned pointer is owned by the transport/SASL layer and must not be modified; NULLability is unknown

functions.name: pnx_sasl_get_selected_mechanism
functions.description: Return the SASL mechanism name selected for this transport, if selection has occurred.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
The returned pointer is owned by the transport/SASL layer and must not be modified; NULLability is unknown

functions.name: pnx_sasl_set_bytes_out
functions.description: Provide outgoing SASL payload bytes to be written by the transport. Used by SASL implementations during message exchanges or security-layer encoding.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
bytes must reference valid memory for the duration required by the transport write path (exact lifetime semantics unknown)

functions.name: pnx_sasl_set_desired_state
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pnx_sasl_set_desired_state(pn_transport_t *transport, enum pnx_sasl_state desired_state);
functions.description: Request a transition of the SASL state machine to the specified desired state. Used by SASL implementations to drive progress.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
desired_state must be one of the values of enum pnx_sasl_state

functions.name: pnx_sasl_set_selected_mechanism
functions.description: Record the SASL mechanism chosen for this transport. Typically called by the mechanism negotiation logic in a SASL plugin.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
mechanism must point to a NUL-terminated C string naming a SASL mechanism; further constraints are unknown

functions.name: pnx_sasl_set_local_hostname
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pnx_sasl_set_local_hostname(pn_transport_t * transport, const char * fqdn);
functions.description: Set the local hostname/FQDN to be used by SASL for this transport (e.g., for host-based mechanisms or challenges).
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
fqdn must point to a NUL-terminated hostname string; format/validation details are unknown

functions.name: pnx_sasl_set_succeeded
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pnx_sasl_set_succeeded(pn_transport_t *transport, const char *username, const char *authzid);
functions.description: Mark SASL negotiation as succeeded for this transport and record the authenticated username and optional authorization identity.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context
username must point to a NUL-terminated string; whether NULL is permitted is unknown
authzid must point to a NUL-terminated string; whether NULL is permitted is unknown

functions.name: pnx_sasl_set_failed
functions.description: Mark SASL negotiation as failed for this transport. Intended for SASL plugins upon authentication failure or protocol error.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t associated with an active SASL context

functions.name: pnx_sasl_set_implementation
functions.description: Attach a SASL implementation (function table) and its opaque context to this transport. This registers the authenticator used for SASL operations on the connection.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t
impl must point to a populated pnx_sasl_implementation v-table; NULLability not specified
context is an opaque pointer provided to the implementation; ownership/lifetime is implementation-defined (unknown)
The function pointers inside impl are expected to follow the documented interface in this header (names and signatures)

functions.name: pnx_sasl_set_default_implementation
functions.description: Set the process-wide/default SASL implementation used when none is explicitly set on a transport.
requirements: impl must point to a populated pnx_sasl_implementation v-table; NULLability not specified
May affect subsequent transports that do not override the implementation; threading/ordering constraints are unknown

functions.name: pn_ssl_present
functions.description: Returns whether SSL/TLS support is available in the Proton build/runtime. Typical use: check before attempting to configure SSL domains or sessions.
requirements: None beyond providing a valid runtime; returns true if SSL supported, false otherwise.

functions.name: pn_ssl_domain
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new SSL configuration domain used to configure one or more SSL sessions. The mode determines whether sessions created from this domain act as client or server.
requirements: mode must be PN_SSL_MODE_CLIENT or PN_SSL_MODE_SERVER.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned domain with pn_ssl_domain_free().
May return NULL if SSL support is not present.

functions.name: pn_ssl_domain_free
functions.description: Releases an SSL configuration domain previously allocated by pn_ssl_domain().
requirements: domain must have been returned by pn_ssl_domain().
Do not use the domain after calling this function.

functions.name: pn_ssl_domain_set_credentials
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN int pn_ssl_domain_set_credentials(pn_ssl_domain_t *domain, const char *credential_1, const char *credential_2, const char *password)
functions.description: Sets the certificate and private key that identify the local node for all SSL sessions created from this domain. Used by servers and by clients when client authentication is required. Takes effect only for pn_ssl_t objects created after this call returns.
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_ssl_domain_t.
credential_1 specifies the certificate source (PEM/PKCS#11 for OpenSSL; PKCS#12 file or system store for Windows SChannel).
credential_2 is optional: for OpenSSL, an optional PEM or PKCS#11 URI for the private key; for SChannel, the friendly name if multiple certs exist.
password may be NULL if the key is not protected.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl_domain_set_trusted_ca_db
functions.description: Configures the trusted CA certificate database used by this domain to verify peer certificates. Defaults to the system trust store unless overridden. Takes effect only for pn_ssl_t objects created after this call returns.
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_ssl_domain_t.
certificate_db specifies the trusted CA source/path (semantics depend on platform/SSL implementation).
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl_domain_set_peer_authentication
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN int pn_ssl_domain_set_peer_authentication(pn_ssl_domain_t *domain, const pn_ssl_verify_mode_t mode, const char *trusted_CAs)
functions.description: Sets the peer verification policy for sessions created from this domain. By default clients verify certificate and peer name (PN_SSL_VERIFY_PEER_NAME); servers do not verify (PN_SSL_ANONYMOUS_PEER). Optionally advertises a list of trusted CAs to clients when the server verifies peers. Takes effect only for pn_ssl_t objects created after this call returns.
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_ssl_domain_t.
mode must be one of pn_ssl_verify_mode_t values.
To verify a peer, a trusted CA must be configured (see pn_ssl_domain_set_trusted_ca_db()).
Servers that verify peers must provide their own certificate (see pn_ssl_domain_set_credentials()).
trusted_CAs is a path to a CA database advertised to clients when a server verifies peers; may be NULL if not advertising.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl_domain_set_protocols
functions.description: Restricts the TLS protocol versions permitted for sessions from this domain. The list is a space-separated string of allowed protocols: TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3. If not called, all TLS protocols are allowed (no SSLv2/3).
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_ssl_domain_t.
protocols must be a space-separated list comprised of the tokens: TLSv1, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl_domain_set_ciphers
functions.description: Sets the list of permitted ciphers for sessions from this domain. The string syntax is implementation-specific (depends on the underlying SSL library).
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_ssl_domain_t.
ciphers must follow the syntax supported by the underlying SSL implementation.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl_domain_allow_unsecured_client
functions.description: Deprecated. Configures a server domain to accept connections from non-SSL clients by sniffing the incoming stream and allowing plaintext. Disabled by default.
requirements: domain must be a server-configured pn_ssl_domain_t.
Use pn_transport_require_encryption() instead when possible.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl
functions.description: Creates (associates) a new SSL session object with the given transport, enabling the transport to use SSL/TLS.
requirements: transport must be a valid pn_transport_t.
Returns NULL if no SSL session is associated with the transport (e.g., SSL unsupported or allocation/config failure).
The returned pn_ssl_t is owned by the transport.

functions.name: pn_ssl_init
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN int pn_ssl_init(pn_ssl_t *ssl, pn_ssl_domain_t *domain, const char *session_id)
functions.description: Initializes an SSL session using the provided domain configuration or secure defaults when domain is NULL. Clients default to verifying peer name using system CAs; servers default to a test-oriented configuration and generally require explicit credentials for production. Optionally attempts session resumption using session_id.
requirements: ssl must be a valid pn_ssl_t associated with a transport.
domain may be NULL to use a default domain matching the transport role (client/server).
session_id may be NULL; if supplied, it is used for session resumption if a matching prior session exists.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl_get_cipher_name
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN bool pn_ssl_get_cipher_name(pn_ssl_t *ssl, char *buffer, size_t size)
functions.description: Writes the name of the currently active cipher to buffer. Returns false if SSL is not active (no cipher). The active cipher may change due to renegotiation.
requirements: ssl must be a valid pn_ssl_t.
buffer must point to writable storage of at least size bytes; provide size > 0 to receive a NUL-terminated string.
Returns true if a cipher name is written; false if no cipher is in use.

functions.name: pn_ssl_get_ssf
functions.description: Returns the security strength factor (SSF) of the currently active cipher. 0 indicates no security.
requirements: ssl must be a valid pn_ssl_t.

functions.name: pn_ssl_get_protocol_name
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN bool pn_ssl_get_protocol_name(pn_ssl_t *ssl, char *buffer, size_t size)
functions.description: Writes the name of the currently active SSL/TLS protocol version to buffer. Returns false if SSL is not active or not ready. Protocol may change due to renegotiation.
requirements: ssl must be a valid pn_ssl_t.
buffer must point to writable storage of at least size bytes; provide size > 0 to receive a NUL-terminated string.
Returns true on success; false if connection not ready or SSL inactive.

functions.name: pn_ssl_resume_status
functions.description: Indicates whether an active client SSL session was resumed from a previous session, is new, or if resume status is unknown/unsupported. Best-effort only—servers may decline resumption.
requirements: ssl must be a valid pn_ssl_t. The session should be active to yield meaningful status.

functions.name: pn_ssl_set_peer_hostname
functions.description: Overrides the expected identity (hostname) of the remote peer. Used for SNI on clients and for peer certificate hostname verification when enabled (PN_SSL_VERIFY_PEER_NAME).
requirements: ssl must be a valid pn_ssl_t.
hostname must conform to RFC1034 Section 3.5 hostname syntax.
Hostname verification occurs only when PN_SSL_VERIFY_PEER_NAME is configured (see pn_ssl_domain_set_peer_authentication()).
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl_get_peer_hostname
functions.description: Retrieves the configured expected peer identity as set by pn_ssl_set_peer_hostname(). Writes a NUL-terminated string to hostname if provided and large enough; always updates bufsize to the required length (including NUL) or zero if unset.
requirements: ssl must be a valid pn_ssl_t.
bufsize must be non-NULL; on input it specifies hostname buffer size, on output it receives the required size or zero if not set.
hostname may be NULL to query the required size without writing a string.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl_get_remote_subject
functions.description: Returns a NUL-terminated string containing the full subject of the peer’s certificate. The returned pointer is valid until the ssl object is destroyed.
requirements: ssl must be a valid pn_ssl_t.
A peer certificate must be available; otherwise the content may be NULL or unspecified (not stated).
Caller must not free or modify the returned string; it is owned by the ssl object.

functions.name: pn_ssl_get_cert_fingerprint
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN int pn_ssl_get_cert_fingerprint(pn_ssl_t *ssl0, char *fingerprint, size_t fingerprint_length, pn_ssl_hash_alg hash_alg)
functions.description: Computes and writes the peer certificate’s fingerprint as a hex string into fingerprint, using the specified hash algorithm. The result is NUL-terminated. Lengths: MD5 33, SHA1 41, SHA256 65, SHA512 129 characters.
requirements: ssl0 must be a valid pn_ssl_t with a peer certificate available.
fingerprint must point to writable storage of at least fingerprint_length bytes.
fingerprint_length must be >= 33 for MD5, >= 41 for SHA1, >= 65 for SHA256, >= 129 for SHA512.
hash_alg must be one of pn_ssl_hash_alg values (PN_SSL_MD5, PN_SSL_SHA1, PN_SSL_SHA256, PN_SSL_SHA512).
Returns 0 on success; a value < 0 indicates an error.

functions.name: pn_ssl_get_remote_subject_subfield
functions.description: Returns the value of a specific sub-field of the peer certificate’s subject (e.g., country, state/province, locality, organization, organizational unit, common name). The returned string is valid until the ssl object is destroyed.
requirements: ssl0 must be a valid pn_ssl_t.
field must be one of pn_ssl_cert_subject_subfield enum values.
Caller must not free or modify the returned string; it is owned by the ssl object.

functions.name: pn_proactor_addr
functions.signature: PNP_EXTERN int pn_proactor_addr(char *addr, size_t size, const char *host, const char *port);
functions.description: Format a "host:port" address string suitable for pn_proactor_connect()/pn_proactor_listen(). Copies the result into addr with a trailing '\0'. Returns the length of the formatted address excluding the terminator; if the return value is >= size, the output was truncated. Typical usage is to supply a PN_MAX_ADDR-sized buffer and pass host and port strings (which may be empty to imply defaults where later used).
requirements: addr must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
size must describe the actual number of writable bytes in addr (>=1).
host must be a valid, non-NULL C string (may be empty).
port must be a valid, non-NULL C string (may be empty).
Caller should check the return value; if it is >= size the address was truncated.

functions.name: pn_proactor
functions.description: Create a new proactor instance to manage IO for connections/listeners. Must be freed with pn_proactor_free(). Typically created once per thread pool or process depending on the application's architecture.
requirements: Caller must eventually call pn_proactor_free() to release resources.
Do not use the returned proactor after it is freed.

functions.name: pn_proactor_free
functions.description: Free the proactor, aborting open connections/listeners and releasing all associated resources. Automatically triggers close/abort on owned objects.
requirements: proactor must be a valid proactor created by pn_proactor().
After calling, the proactor pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: pn_proactor_connect2
functions.signature: PNP_EXTERN void pn_proactor_connect2(pn_proactor_t *proactor, pn_connection_t *connection, pn_transport_t *transport, const char *addr);
functions.description: Thread-safe. Connect to addr and bind the resulting transport to the given AMQP connection and transport. The proactor takes ownership of connection (if non-NULL) and transport (if non-NULL). Errors are reported asynchronously as PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED events from pn_proactor_wait(). Empty host or port in addr imply local/defaults as documented.
requirements: proactor must be a valid proactor.
addr must be a valid, null-terminated "host:port" string (typically created by pn_proactor_addr()).

connection may be NULL; if non-NULL, ownership transfers to the proactor; the proactor will call pn_connection_free() after the final PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED or when pn_proactor_free() is called unless pn_proactor_release_connection() is used.
transport may be NULL; if non-NULL, ownership transfers to the proactor and it will be freed even if pn_proactor_release_connection() is called.
If host in addr is empty, connects to local host via default protocol; if port is empty, uses port 5672.

functions.name: pn_proactor_connect
functions.signature: PNP_EXTERN void pn_proactor_connect(pn_proactor_t *proactor, pn_connection_t *connection, const char *addr);
functions.description: Deprecated. Use pn_proactor_connect2(). Establishes a connection to addr and binds it to the provided connection. Behavior mirrors pn_proactor_connect2() but without an explicit transport parameter; detailed ownership/behavior is as per the older API and not fully documented here.
requirements: proactor must be valid.
addr must be a valid, null-terminated "host:port" string (typically from pn_proactor_addr()).
connection may be NULL; if non-NULL, it is expected that ownership transfers to the proactor (inferred from pn_proactor_connect2() documentation).
Prefer pn_proactor_connect2() for new code.

functions.name: pn_proactor_listen
functions.signature: PNP_EXTERN void pn_proactor_listen(pn_proactor_t *proactor, pn_listener_t *listener, const char *addr, int backlog);
functions.description: Thread-safe. Begin listening for incoming connections on addr. The proactor takes ownership of listener and will free it after the final PN_LISTENER_CLOSE or when pn_proactor_free() is called. PN_LISTENER_OPEN/PN_LISTENER_CLOSE events indicate readiness or failure; on failure pn_listener_condition() is set. Empty host listens on all protocols/interfaces; empty port uses 5672.
requirements: proactor must be valid.
listener must be a valid listener object; ownership transfers to the proactor which will call pn_listener_free() after the final PN_LISTENER_CLOSE or when pn_proactor_free() is called.
addr must be a valid, null-terminated "host:port" string (typically from pn_proactor_addr()).

backlog controls the number of pending unhandled connection requests; if addr resolves to multiple interfaces/protocols, backlog applies to each (value should be non-negative, inferred from typical backlog semantics).

functions.name: pn_proactor_disconnect
functions.description: Thread-safe. Disconnect all connections and listeners belonging to proactor. Normal close events (PN_LISTENER_CLOSE, PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED, etc.) are generated. A PN_PROACTOR_INACTIVE event will occur once all entities are disconnected and no timeout is pending (or immediately if there is nothing active). If condition is non-NULL, its data is copied to each disconnected transport/listener and available in their close events.
requirements: proactor must be valid.
condition may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must be initialized and remain valid for the call duration (data is copied).
New connections/listeners created before PN_PROACTOR_INACTIVE may prevent the proactor from becoming inactive.

functions.name: pn_proactor_wait
functions.description: Thread-safe. Block until a non-empty batch of proactor events is available and return it. The batch must be processed in sequence, and exactly one pn_proactor_done() must be called when finished. The batch pointer must not be used after pn_proactor_done().
requirements: proactor must be valid.
Caller must process events in order using pn_event_batch_next().
Caller must call pn_proactor_done() exactly once for the returned batch.
Do not use the batch pointer after pn_proactor_done().

functions.name: pn_proactor_get
functions.description: Thread-safe, non-blocking variant of pn_proactor_wait(). Returns a batch if available immediately, otherwise NULL. If a non-NULL batch is returned, handle it identically to pn_proactor_wait(), including calling pn_proactor_done() when finished.
requirements: proactor must be valid.
If the return value is non-NULL, caller must call pn_proactor_done() exactly once for that batch.
Do not use the batch pointer after pn_proactor_done().

functions.name: pn_event_batch_next
functions.description: Remove and return the next event from the batch; returns NULL when the batch is empty. The returned pn_event_t* remains valid only until pn_event_batch_next() is called again on the same batch.
requirements: batch must be a valid batch returned by pn_proactor_wait()/pn_proactor_get().
Do not access the returned event pointer after calling pn_event_batch_next() again on the same batch or after pn_proactor_done() for that batch.
There is no look-ahead/peek; events are obtained exactly once in order.

functions.name: pn_event_batch_proactor
functions.description: Query the batch for its subject; if the subject is a proactor, return it, otherwise NULL. The returned pointer is valid until pn_proactor_done() is called again on the same batch.
requirements: batch must be a valid batch.
Do not use the returned proactor pointer after pn_proactor_done() for that batch.

functions.name: pn_event_batch_listener
functions.description: Query the batch for its subject; if the subject is a listener, return it, otherwise NULL. The returned listener pointer is valid until pn_proactor_done() is called again on the same batch.
requirements: batch must be a valid batch.
Do not use the returned listener pointer after pn_proactor_done() for that batch.

functions.name: pn_event_batch_connection
functions.description: Query the batch for its subject; if the subject is a connection, return it, otherwise NULL. The returned connection pointer is valid until pn_proactor_done() is called again on the same batch.
requirements: batch must be a valid batch.
Do not use the returned connection pointer after pn_proactor_done() for that batch.

functions.name: pn_proactor_done
functions.description: Thread-safe (provided the exactly-once rule is followed). Signal that handling of a batch is complete. Must be called exactly once for each batch returned by pn_proactor_wait() (and, by extension, pn_proactor_get() when non-NULL). After this call the batch pointer must not be used.
requirements: Must be called exactly once for each batch returned by pn_proactor_wait() or pn_proactor_get().
Do not use events (the batch pointer) after calling pn_proactor_done().
May be called from any thread provided the exactly-once rule is respected.

functions.name: pn_proactor_interrupt
functions.description: Thread-safe and async-signal-safe. Request that a PN_PROACTOR_INTERRUPT event be delivered as soon as possible. Multiple requests may be coalesced into a single event.
requirements: proactor must be valid.
May be safely called from a signal handler (async-signal-safe).

functions.name: pn_proactor_set_timeout
functions.description: Thread-safe. Schedule a PN_PROACTOR_TIMEOUT event after timeout milliseconds. If another timeout is set before it fires, the previous is replaced. If no thread is blocked in pn_proactor_wait() when it fires, it will be delivered to the next available thread.
requirements: proactor must be valid.
timeout is a duration in milliseconds; it replaces any previously scheduled timeout.

functions.name: pn_proactor_cancel_timeout
functions.description: Thread-safe. Cancel the pending timeout set by pn_proactor_set_timeout(); does nothing if no timeout is set.
requirements: proactor must be valid.

functions.name: pn_proactor_release_connection
functions.description: Not thread-safe. Release ownership of connection and disassociate it from its proactor. The transport is closed and unbound; no further proactor events will be delivered for this connection. The connection object (and sessions/links) remains intact; the caller must free it (pn_connection_free()) or reuse it in another proactor connect/listen call.
requirements: Must be called from a connection event handler (not thread-safe).
If connection does not belong to a proactor, the call does nothing.
After calling, the caller is responsible for eventually freeing or reusing the connection.

functions.name: pn_connection_wake
functions.description: Thread-safe. Request that a PN_CONNECTION_WAKE event for connection be delivered as soon as possible. Wakes may be coalesced if multiple calls occur close together. Serialized with other proactor events for the same connection.
requirements: connection must be valid; if it does not belong to a proactor, the call does nothing.

functions.name: pn_connection_write_flush
functions.description: Unsettled API. Not thread-safe. From within a connection event handler, generate and send as many currently available AMQP frames for the connection as can be sent without blocking. Intended to reduce latency for long-running handlers; has little effect if called just before pn_proactor_done(). If the connection is not owned by a proactor, does nothing.
requirements: Must be called from a connection event handler (not thread-safe).
Connection must be valid; if it does not belong to a proactor, the call has no effect.

functions.name: pn_connection_proactor
functions.description: Not thread-safe. Return the proactor associated with a connection, or NULL if the connection is not managed by a proactor.
requirements: connection must be valid.
Do not call concurrently without external synchronization (not thread-safe).

functions.name: pn_event_proactor
functions.description: Not thread-safe. Return the proactor associated with an event, or NULL if none (e.g., if the underlying connection is not managed by a proactor).
requirements: event must be a valid pointer obtained from a proactor event batch.
Do not call concurrently without external synchronization (not thread-safe).

functions.name: pn_proactor_now
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of pn_proactor_now_64(). Thread-safe. Return a monotonically increasing milliseconds counter representing real elapsed time since an arbitrary point in the past. Intended for process-local timestamps, not for AMQP message timestamps.
requirements: Caller should prefer pn_proactor_now_64() for new code.

functions.name: pn_proactor_now_64
functions.description: Thread-safe. Return a monotonically increasing 64-bit milliseconds counter representing real elapsed time since an arbitrary point in the past. Intended for process-local timestamps, not for AMQP message timestamps.

functions.name: pn_proactor_raw_connect
functions.signature: PNP_EXTERN void pn_proactor_raw_connect(pn_proactor_t *proactor, pn_raw_connection_t *raw_connection, const char *addr);
functions.description: Thread-safe. Connect to addr and bind to a raw connection. The proactor takes ownership of raw_connection and will free it after the final PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED or when pn_proactor_free() is called. Errors are reported as PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED events. Empty host/port imply defaults as documented.
requirements: proactor must be valid.
raw_connection must be created by pn_raw_connection() and cannot be NULL; ownership transfers to the proactor.
addr must be a valid, null-terminated "host:port" string (typically from pn_proactor_addr()).
If host in addr is empty, connects to local host via default protocol; if port is empty, uses 5672.

functions.name: pn_proactor_import_socket
functions.signature: PNP_EXTERN void pn_proactor_import_socket(pn_proactor_t *proactor, pn_connection_t *connection, pn_transport_t *transport, pn_socket_t fd);
functions.description: Imports an already-connected socket into a proactor and binds it to a connection and transport managed by the proactor. If connection and/or transport are NULL, new ones are created. After import, the proactor owns the connection, transport, and socket; it will close the socket when the connection closes and free the connection after the final PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED event (unless pn_proactor_release_connection() is called) and will always free the transport. Errors are surfaced as PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED events from pn_proactor_wait(). Thread-safe; can be called from any thread.
requirements: proactor must be a valid pn_proactor_t pointer.
fd must be a valid, already-connected socket handle/file descriptor appropriate for the platform (pn_socket_t).
If connection is non-NULL, it must be a valid pn_connection_t intended for this socket; after import, do not free it manually (ownership transfers to the proactor).
If transport is non-NULL, it must be a valid pn_transport_t intended for this socket; after import, do not free it manually (ownership transfers to the proactor).
Do not close fd yourself after import; the proactor closes it when the connection is closed.
Handle PN_TRANSPORT_CLOSED events returned by pn_proactor_wait() to detect errors/closure.
To prevent automatic freeing of the connection, call pn_proactor_release_connection(); the transport will still be freed by the proactor.
May be called concurrently (thread-safe).

functions.name: pn_raw_connection
functions.description: Create a new raw connection object for use with the proactor API. Returns a newly allocated pn_raw_connection_t or NULL on allocation failure. Ownership/lifetime is managed by the proactor once handed to it; there is no API to free it directly.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL return to handle out-of-memory conditions.
Once passed to the proactor, the proactor owns the pn_raw_connection_t and controls its lifecycle; there is no function to free it.
Best practice (per notes): create the connection and attach application-specific context before giving it to the proactor.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_local_addr
functions.description: Return the local socket address information for the raw connection, or NULL if not available. The returned pointer becomes invalid after the transport closes (i.e., after handling PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED).
requirements: Do not dereference or retain the returned pointer after the transport closes (after PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED is handled).
The returned address pointer must be treated as read-only.
May return NULL if the address is not available; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_remote_addr
functions.description: Return the remote socket address information for the raw connection, or NULL if not available. The returned pointer becomes invalid after the transport closes (i.e., after handling PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED).
requirements: Do not dereference or retain the returned pointer after the transport closes (after PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED is handled).
The returned address pointer must be treated as read-only.
May return NULL if the address is not available; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_close
functions.description: Close the raw connection for both reading and writing. Flushes pending write buffers, closes the underlying socket, and releases buffers held by the connection. Will emit PN_RAW_CONNECTION_READ and PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WRITTEN so the application can reclaim buffers, followed by PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED to clean up other state.
requirements: Expect PN_RAW_CONNECTION_READ/PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WRITTEN events for buffer reclamation, and a PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED event after closure; application must handle these to clean up.
Buffers provided to the connection must be considered owned by the connection until returned via take_* APIs/events; do not access them until returned.
Caller must be prepared that close triggers event delivery via the proactor.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_read_close
functions.description: Shutdown the raw connection for reading. Closes the socket for read, releases empty read buffers, and emits PN_RAW_CONNECTION_READ so the application can clean up read buffers (which may still contain unread data). If write side is already closed, PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED will be emitted. To fully close, also call pn_raw_connection_close() or pn_raw_connection_write_close().
requirements: Handle PN_RAW_CONNECTION_READ events that follow to reclaim read buffers; buffers may still contain data not yet consumed.
If pn_raw_connection_write_close() was already called, expect PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED; application must handle it.
To fully close the connection, the application must also close the write side (pn_raw_connection_write_close()) or call pn_raw_connection_close().

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_write_close
functions.description: Shutdown the raw connection for writing. Flushes any pending write buffers, closes the socket for write, releases write buffers, and emits PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WRITTEN so the application can reclaim them. If read side is already closed, PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED will be emitted. To fully close, also call pn_raw_connection_close() or pn_raw_connection_read_close().
requirements: Handle PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WRITTEN events that follow to reclaim write buffers.
If pn_raw_connection_read_close() was already called, expect PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED; application must handle it.
To fully close the connection, the application must also close the read side (pn_raw_connection_read_close()) or call pn_raw_connection_close().

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_read_buffers_capacity
functions.description: Return how many more read buffers the connection can accept via pn_raw_connection_give_read_buffers().
requirements: None beyond passing a valid pn_raw_connection_t pointer.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_write_buffers_capacity
functions.description: Return how many more write buffers the connection can accept via pn_raw_connection_write_buffers().
requirements: None beyond passing a valid pn_raw_connection_t pointer.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_give_read_buffers
functions.description: Provide an array of buffers the connection can use for reading from the socket. If the connection has no read buffers, PN_RAW_CONNECTION_READ will never be generated; PN_RAW_CONNECTION_NEED_READ_BUFFERS is generated when needed and will not reoccur until this call is made. Returns the number of buffers actually accepted (may be less than num if capacity is limited). Ownership of accepted buffers transfers to the connection until returned via take API.
requirements: buffers must point to an array of at least num pn_raw_buffer_t elements.
The application must not access (read or write) any buffers accepted by the connection until they are returned via pn_raw_connection_take_read_buffers().
Returned count may be less than num; only elements [0, returned-1] are taken; caller must not assume later elements were accepted.
The presence of PN_RAW_CONNECTION_NEED_READ_BUFFERS does not imply the socket is readable.
A pn_raw_buffer_t may have bytes==NULL to represent no buffer (per struct note); caller must handle that appropriately if used.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_take_read_buffers
functions.description: Retrieve up to num buffers that have data read from the socket. Fills the provided array in the order data was read. Returns the number of buffers returned (0 if none). After PN_RAW_CONNECTION_READ, repeated calls are safe until 0 is returned.
requirements: buffers must point to an array of at least num pn_raw_buffer_t elements for output.
Caller must handle 0 return when there are no buffers to take.
Buffers are returned in read order; caller must use size and offset fields for valid byte range as documented in pn_raw_buffer_t.
Safe to call repeatedly after PN_RAW_CONNECTION_READ until it returns 0.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_write_buffers
functions.description: Queue an array of buffers to be written to the socket, in the order provided. Returns the number of buffers actually queued (may be less than num if capacity is limited). PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WRITTEN will be generated once the buffers have been written; until then the buffers must not be accessed.
requirements: buffers must point to an array of at least num pn_raw_buffer_t elements.
The application must not access (read or write) any buffers recorded for writing until they are returned via pn_raw_connection_take_written_buffers() / after PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WRITTEN.
Returned count may be less than num; only elements [0, returned-1] are recorded as queued.
Write completion and buffer reclamation is signaled by PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WRITTEN events.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_take_written_buffers
functions.description: Retrieve up to num buffers that have been fully written to the socket. Returns the number of buffers returned (0 if none). After PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WRITTEN, repeated calls are safe until 0 is returned. Buffers are returned in the same order they were provided.
requirements: buffers must point to an array of at least num pn_raw_buffer_t elements for output.
Caller must handle 0 return when there are no buffers to take.
Safe to call repeatedly after PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WRITTEN until it returns 0.
Buffers are returned in the same order they were originally passed to pn_raw_connection_write_buffers().

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_is_read_closed
functions.description: Return true if the raw connection has been shut down for reading; false otherwise.
requirements: None beyond passing a valid pn_raw_connection_t pointer.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_is_write_closed
functions.description: Return true if the raw connection has been shut down for writing; false otherwise.
requirements: None beyond passing a valid pn_raw_connection_t pointer.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_wake
functions.description: Request that a PN_RAW_CONNECTION_WAKE event be delivered for the connection as soon as possible, serialized with other proactor events. Multiple wake requests may be coalesced into one event. Wakes never follow PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED; such requests are dropped. Thread-safe.
requirements: Do not rely on a one-to-one mapping between wake calls and wake events; wakes can be coalesced.
Calling this after a PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED event has been delivered and its event batch released via pn_proactor_done() has undefined behavior; do not call in that state.
Calling this before the return of pn_proactor_raw_connect() or pn_listener_raw_accept() is undefined; do not call until those calls return for the connection.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_condition
functions.description: Return the condition object with additional information about a raw connection error. A raw connection error exists if a PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED event is received and the associated condition is set. The returned pointer is only valid until the end of the handler for the PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED event.
requirements: Only use the returned pn_condition_t during handling of the PN_RAW_CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED event; it becomes invalid after the handler finishes.
Caller must check pn_condition_is_set() to determine if an error is present.
Do not retain or use the pointer after the event batch is released.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_get_context
functions.description: Get the user/application context pointer associated with the raw connection (previously set with pn_raw_connection_set_context).
requirements: None beyond passing a valid pn_raw_connection_t pointer.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_set_context
functions.description: Associate an application-defined context pointer with the raw connection, retrievable via pn_raw_connection_get_context.
requirements: None beyond passing a valid pn_raw_connection_t pointer.

functions.name: pn_raw_connection_attachments
functions.description: Return the attachments record associated with the raw connection, allowing key/value-style attachment of data to the connection.
requirements: None beyond passing a valid pn_raw_connection_t pointer.

functions.name: pn_event_raw_connection
functions.description: Return the raw connection associated with an event, or NULL if the event is not related to a raw connection.
requirements: Caller must handle NULL if the event is not associated with a raw connection.

functions.name: pn_event_batch_raw_connection
functions.description: If the subject of the event batch is a raw connection, return it; otherwise return NULL. The returned raw connection is valid until pn_proactor_done() is called again on the same batch.
requirements: Caller must handle NULL if the batch subject is not a raw connection.
Do not use the returned pointer after pn_proactor_done() is called again on the same batch.

functions.name: pn_handshaker
functions.description: Creates and returns a handler object for connection handshaking in the Proton reactor framework. Intended to be attached/used within the reactor event system to drive/handle the AMQP handshake state machine. Details of lifecycle and ownership are not documented here; these are internal helpers in Proton (marked INTERNAL).
requirements: Returned pointer refers to an internal handler object; exact ownership and destruction responsibilities are unknown (not documented in this header).
Intended usage is with the Proton reactor (see <proton/reactor.h>), but no strict calling order or preconditions are specified in this header.
Thread-safety and error behavior (e.g., NULL on failure) are unknown.

functions.name: pn_iohandler
functions.description: Creates and returns an I/O handler for use with the Proton reactor framework. Typically installed to process I/O-related events and drive reading/writing on transports within the reactor loop. Marked as an internal helper; detailed semantics are not provided here.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to an internal handler object; ownership, lifetime management, and whether the caller must free it are unknown.
Intended to be used with the Proton reactor event system (see <proton/reactor.h>), but no strict preconditions or ordering are specified here.
Thread-safety and error behavior (e.g., NULL on failure) are unknown.

functions.name: pn_flowcontroller
functions.description: Creates and returns a flow-control handler that manages link credit using a window-based policy in the Proton reactor framework. Typically attached to links or connections to automatically maintain credit. This is an internal helper; exact policy details are not documented here.
requirements: Parameter window: inferred to represent a credit window size; should be a non-negative (preferably positive) integer. Exact valid range is not documented.
Returned pointer refers to an internal handler object; ownership and destruction responsibilities are unknown.
Intended usage is within the Proton reactor event system (see <proton/reactor.h>), but no strict preconditions or ordering are specified here.
Thread-safety and error behavior (e.g., NULL on failure) are unknown.

functions.name: pn_handler
functions.description: Allocates a handler object with a user-provided dispatch callback used to process events. Typical usage: create the handler once and register/attach it where events will be delivered.
requirements: dispatch must be a valid function pointer accepting (pn_handler_t*, pn_event_t*, pn_event_type_t).
The returned pn_handler_t* must be released with pn_handler_free() when no longer needed.
Handler instances are not thread-safe unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

functions.name: pn_handler_new
functions.signature: pn_handler_t *pn_handler_new(void (*dispatch)(pn_handler_t *, pn_event_t *, pn_event_type_t), size_t size, void (*finalize)(pn_handler_t *));
functions.description: Allocates a handler with a dispatch callback and reserves extra per-handler memory (size bytes) accessible via pn_handler_mem(). Optionally provides a finalize callback invoked during handler destruction.
requirements: dispatch must be a valid function pointer accepting (pn_handler_t*, pn_event_t*, pn_event_type_t).
size specifies the number of extra bytes to allocate; if non-zero, the memory is accessible through pn_handler_mem().
If provided, finalize must be a valid function pointer taking (pn_handler_t*).
The returned pn_handler_t* must be freed with pn_handler_free().
Behavior for NULL finalize is allowed but not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: pn_handler_free
functions.description: Frees a handler previously created by pn_handler() or pn_handler_new(), releasing any associated resources. If a finalize callback was supplied at creation, it may be called before memory is released.
requirements: handler must be a handler returned by pn_handler() or pn_handler_new().
Do not use the handler after calling pn_handler_free().
Passing NULL is unspecified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: pn_handler_mem
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the extra memory block (of size provided to pn_handler_new()) associated with the handler, useful for storing per-handler state.
requirements: handler must be a valid pn_handler_t* created with pn_handler_new().
If the handler was not created with extra size, the returned pointer semantics are unspecified (unknown).
The returned memory is owned by the handler and becomes invalid after pn_handler_free().

functions.name: pn_handler_add
functions.description: Attaches a child handler to a parent handler so that the parent can delegate or chain event processing to the child.
requirements: handler must be a valid parent pn_handler_t*.
child must be a valid pn_handler_t*.
Ownership/lifetime is not transferred; both must remain valid for the duration of use (inferred, unknown specifics).

functions.name: pn_handler_clear
functions.description: Removes all child handlers or internal state from the handler, resetting its composition/delegation chain.
requirements: handler must be a valid pn_handler_t*.
Any iterators or external references to prior children become invalid after clearing (unknown specifics).

functions.name: pn_handler_dispatch
functions.description: Invokes the handler’s dispatch callback for a given event and event type, delivering the event to the handler chain.
requirements: handler must be a valid pn_handler_t* with a dispatch callback.
event must be a valid pn_event_t* appropriate for the provided type.
type must be a valid pn_event_type_t value.
Caller is responsible for ensuring event lifetime spans the dispatch call.

functions.name: pn_reactor
functions.description: Creates a new reactor instance, the central event loop/coordinator for connections, timers, and tasks.
requirements: The returned pn_reactor_t* must be freed with pn_reactor_free() when no longer needed.
Reactor objects are not documented as thread-safe; use from one thread unless otherwise documented (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_attachments
functions.description: Returns the attachments record for the reactor to associate user data or handlers.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
The returned pn_record_t* remains owned by the reactor; do not free it directly.

functions.name: pn_reactor_get_timeout
functions.description: Gets the current reactor timeout in milliseconds used to bound select/poll waits.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Returned value unit is milliseconds; meaning of special values (e.g., 0, negative) is not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_set_timeout
functions.description: Sets the reactor’s I/O wait timeout in milliseconds, affecting how long the event loop blocks waiting for events.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
timeout is in milliseconds; acceptable range is not documented (unknown).
Call before or during the event loop to affect subsequent waits.

functions.name: pn_reactor_mark
functions.description: Marks and returns a timestamp reference point within the reactor, typically for scheduling/timing purposes.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Semantics of the mark relative to pn_reactor_now() are not fully documented here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_now
functions.description: Returns the reactor’s notion of current time as a timestamp, used for timers and scheduling.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Time base/epoch specifics are not detailed here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_yield
functions.description: Hints the reactor to yield control, allowing other processing or rescheduling within the event loop.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Effect on scheduling is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_free
functions.description: Frees a reactor created by pn_reactor(), releasing all resources owned by it.
requirements: reactor must be a pn_reactor_t* returned by pn_reactor().
Do not use the reactor or any objects exclusively owned by it after this call (exact ownership semantics of children are not specified here, unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_collector
functions.description: Returns the event collector used by the reactor to gather events.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
The returned pn_collector_t* is owned by the reactor; do not free it directly.

functions.name: pn_reactor_get_global_handler
functions.description: Gets the reactor’s global handler, which receives all events emitted by the reactor.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Returned handler is owned by the reactor; do not free it directly.

functions.name: pn_reactor_set_global_handler
functions.description: Sets the reactor’s global handler to receive all events emitted by the reactor.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
handler must be a valid pn_handler_t*.
Caller must ensure handler remains valid for the life of the reactor or until replaced (ownership not transferred; unknown specifics).

functions.name: pn_reactor_get_handler
functions.description: Gets the reactor’s default handler used for top-level events not covered by the global handler.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Returned handler is owned by the reactor; do not free it directly.

functions.name: pn_reactor_set_handler
functions.description: Sets the reactor’s default handler for its own events.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
handler must be a valid pn_handler_t*.
Caller must ensure handler remains valid while in use by the reactor (ownership unspecified).

functions.name: pn_reactor_children
functions.description: Returns the list of child objects managed by the reactor (e.g., connections, acceptors, timers).
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
The returned list is owned by the reactor; mutation and lifetime rules are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_selectable
functions.description: Returns the reactor’s selectable, representing its readiness for I/O multiplexing integration.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
The returned selectable is owned by the reactor; do not free it directly.

functions.name: pn_reactor_update
functions.description: Updates the reactor with state changes for an associated selectable, typically after I/O readiness changes.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t* associated with the reactor.

functions.name: pn_reactor_acceptor
functions.signature: pn_acceptor_t *pn_reactor_acceptor(pn_reactor_t *reactor, const char *host, const char *port, pn_handler_t *handler);
functions.description: Creates a listening acceptor bound to host:port and registers a handler to process events for incoming connections.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
host must be a valid C string specifying the local interface or hostname.
port must be a valid C string specifying the service/port.
handler must be a valid pn_handler_t* to handle acceptor/connection events.
The returned pn_acceptor_t* is managed by the reactor; explicit close via pn_acceptor_close() when needed.

functions.name: pn_reactor_error
functions.description: Returns the reactor’s error object describing the last error encountered by the reactor.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
The returned pn_error_t* is owned by the reactor; do not free it directly.

functions.name: pn_reactor_connection_to_host
functions.signature: pn_connection_t *pn_reactor_connection_to_host(pn_reactor_t *reactor, const char *host, const char *port, pn_handler_t *handler);
functions.description: Creates an outgoing connection managed by the reactor. The reactor’s I/O handler will create a socket to host:port once the connection is opened. Use the provided handler to process all events for this connection.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
host must be a valid C string (e.g., "localhost").
port must be a valid C string (e.g., "5672").
handler must be a valid pn_handler_t* to process connection events.
Caller is responsible for opening the returned connection at the appropriate time; socket is created once the connection is opened (per documentation).

functions.name: pn_reactor_connection
functions.description: Deprecated: creates an outgoing connection managed by the reactor, with the peer host set later via pn_reactor_set_connection_host() before opening. Prefer pn_reactor_connection_to_host().
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
handler must be a valid pn_handler_t*.
Before opening the connection, caller must set the host (and optionally port) using pn_reactor_set_connection_host().

functions.name: pn_reactor_set_connection_host
functions.signature: void pn_reactor_set_connection_host(pn_reactor_t *reactor, pn_connection_t *connection, const char *host, const char *port);
functions.description: Sets or changes the host and optional port used by the reactor to create the outgoing socket for a reactor-managed connection. Must be called prior to (re)opening the connection.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
connection must be a pn_connection_t* created by the reactor.
host must be a valid C string for the remote network address or DNS name.
port may be NULL to use the default "5672".
Call before opening or reopening the connection for the change to take effect.

functions.name: pn_reactor_get_connection_address
functions.description: Returns the peer address for a reactor connection. For outgoing connections, it is the configured host:port; for accepted connections, it is the remote address. The string is valid until the address is changed or the connection is freed.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
connection must be a reactor-managed pn_connection_t*.
Returned pointer must not be modified or freed by the caller.
Address may be NULL if unavailable.
Address format may be numeric IP per note in documentation.

functions.name: pn_reactor_wakeup
functions.description: Wakes the reactor’s event loop, causing it to stop blocking and process pending work.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Return value semantics (e.g., error codes) are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_start
functions.description: Initializes internal state and begins the reactor’s processing lifecycle without entering a full run loop.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Call before pn_reactor_process()/pn_reactor_run() as appropriate (exact sequencing beyond this is not fully documented here, unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_quiesced
functions.description: Returns whether the reactor has no pending work (quiescent).
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Interpretation of quiescence depends on internal state; exact criteria are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_process
functions.description: Processes I/O and events for a single iteration of the reactor, returning a boolean status (e.g., whether more work remains).
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Caller typically loops calling pn_reactor_process() until quiesced or stopped; exact return semantics are not fully documented here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_stop
functions.description: Signals the reactor to stop processing events, causing pn_reactor_run()/process loop to exit.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Effect on existing connections/tasks is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_run
functions.description: Runs the reactor’s event loop until stopped or quiesced, processing events for connections, acceptors, and timers.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
Only call once per reactor instance at a time; reentrancy/threading not documented (unknown).

functions.name: pn_reactor_schedule
functions.description: Schedules a handler to be invoked by the reactor after a delay (milliseconds), returning a task handle for management/cancellation.
requirements: reactor must be a valid pn_reactor_t*.
delay is an integer delay in milliseconds; allowed range and negative handling are not documented here (unknown).
handler must be a valid pn_handler_t*.
The returned pn_task_t* can be used with pn_task_cancel() and pn_task_attachments().

functions.name: pn_acceptor_set_ssl_domain
functions.description: Configures the SSL/TLS domain (credentials/policy) used by the acceptor for incoming connections.
requirements: acceptor must be a valid pn_acceptor_t*.
domain must be a valid pn_ssl_domain_t* configured appropriately for server use.
Must be called before accepting SSL/TLS connections; exact timing not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_acceptor_close
functions.description: Closes a reactor-created acceptor, stopping it from accepting new connections.
requirements: acceptor must be a valid pn_acceptor_t* obtained from the reactor.
Effect on existing accepted connections is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_connection_acceptor
functions.description: Returns the acceptor associated with a given accepted connection, if any.
requirements: connection must be a valid pn_connection_t*.
Returned pn_acceptor_t* is owned by the reactor; do not free it directly.
May return NULL for outgoing connections or if not applicable.

functions.name: pn_timer
functions.description: Creates a timer object associated with an event collector for scheduling time-based tasks.
requirements: collector must be a valid pn_collector_t*.
The returned pn_timer_t* must be managed and eventually released according to library conventions (freeing API not shown here, unknown).

functions.name: pn_timer_deadline
functions.description: Returns the next scheduled deadline timestamp for the timer.
requirements: timer must be a valid pn_timer_t*.
If no tasks are scheduled, the returned value’s semantics are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_timer_tick
functions.description: Advances the timer, causing it to fire due tasks based on the supplied current time.
requirements: timer must be a valid pn_timer_t*.
now must be a timestamp compatible with the timer’s time base (typically from pn_reactor_now()).

functions.name: pn_timer_schedule
functions.description: Schedules a task to run at the specified absolute deadline timestamp, returning a task handle.
requirements: timer must be a valid pn_timer_t*.
deadline must be a valid timestamp in the same time base as pn_timer_deadline()/pn_reactor_now().

functions.name: pn_timer_tasks
functions.description: Returns the number of pending scheduled tasks in the timer.
requirements: timer must be a valid pn_timer_t*.
Return value range and concurrency guarantees are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_task_attachments
functions.description: Returns the attachments record for a scheduled task, allowing user data association.
requirements: task must be a valid pn_task_t*.
The returned pn_record_t* is owned by the task; do not free it directly.

functions.name: pn_task_cancel
functions.description: Cancels a scheduled task so it will not be executed if pending.
requirements: task must be a valid pn_task_t*.
Effect if the task is already running or completed is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: pn_class_reactor
functions.description: Returns the reactor associated with an object of a given Proton class, if any.
requirements: clazz must be a valid pn_class_t* describing the object’s class.
object must point to an instance compatible with clazz.
May return NULL if the object is not associated with any reactor.
