functions.name: pn_object_reactor
functions.description: Returns the reactor associated with the given Proton object, if any.
requirements: object must be a valid Proton object pointer.
May return NULL if no reactor is associated.

functions.name: pn_event_reactor
functions.description: Returns the reactor that generated or is associated with the given event.
requirements: event must be a valid pn_event_t*.
May return NULL if the event is not associated with a reactor (unknown).

functions.name: pn_record_get_handler
functions.description: Gets the handler associated with a record’s attachments, if any.
requirements: record must be a valid pn_record_t*.
Returned handler is not owned by the caller; do not free it.

functions.name: pn_record_set_handler
functions.description: Associates a handler with a record’s attachments.
requirements: record must be a valid pn_record_t*.
handler must be a valid pn_handler_t* or NULL to clear (NULL behavior not documented; unknown).
Caller must ensure handler remains valid while associated (ownership not transferred; unknown specifics).

functions.name: pn_event_root
functions.description: Returns the root handler the current event was dispatched to.
requirements: event must be a valid pn_event_t*.
Returned handler is owned by the framework; do not free it.

functions.name: pn_selectable
functions.description: Allocate and return a new selectable object that can be integrated with an external event loop for read, write, and timer notifications. Use the returned handle with the pn_selectable_* API to configure callbacks, associate a file descriptor, and drive events. Free with pn_selectable_free() when no longer needed.
requirements: Must be freed with pn_selectable_free() to avoid leaks.
The returned pointer must be treated as opaque and only used with pn_selectable_* APIs.
Thread-safety and reference counting semantics are unspecified; callers should assume single-threaded use unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: pn_selectable_on_readable
functions.description: Register a callback to be invoked when the selectable becomes readable. The external event loop should call pn_selectable_readable() to trigger this callback when the associated file descriptor has a read event.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t created by pn_selectable() and not yet freed.
readable must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(pn_selectable_t*). It must remain valid until replaced or the selectable is freed.
Whether NULL is permitted for the callback is unspecified; if uncertain, provide a non-NULL handler.

functions.name: pn_selectable_on_writable
functions.description: Register a callback to be invoked when the selectable becomes writable. The external event loop should call pn_selectable_writable() to trigger this callback when the associated file descriptor has a write event.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
writable must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(pn_selectable_t*). It must remain valid until replaced or the selectable is freed.
Whether NULL is permitted for the callback is unspecified; if uncertain, provide a non-NULL handler.

functions.name: pn_selectable_on_expired
functions.description: Register a callback to be invoked when the selectable’s deadline expires. The external event loop should call pn_selectable_expired() when the current time reaches or exceeds the selectable’s deadline.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
expired must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(pn_selectable_t*). It must remain valid until replaced or the selectable is freed.
Whether NULL is permitted for the callback is unspecified; if uncertain, provide a non-NULL handler.

functions.name: pn_selectable_on_error
functions.description: Register a callback to be invoked when an error occurs on the selectable’s file descriptor. The external event loop should call pn_selectable_error() to trigger this callback when an error condition is detected.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
error must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(pn_selectable_t*). It must remain valid until replaced or the selectable is freed.
Whether NULL is permitted for the callback is unspecified; if uncertain, provide a non-NULL handler.

functions.name: pn_selectable_on_release
functions.description: Register a callback invoked on release of the selectable. Exact semantics of "release" are not fully documented here; typically used to notify that the selectable can be returned to a pool or that external resources can be dropped.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
release must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(pn_selectable_t*). It must remain valid until replaced or the selectable is freed.
Specific timing/ordering of the release callback is unknown; do not assume it replaces pn_selectable_free().

functions.name: pn_selectable_on_finalize
functions.description: Register a finalize callback to be invoked when the selectable is being finalized. Details are not documented here; by convention finalize callbacks allow custom cleanup prior to destruction.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
finalize must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(pn_selectable_t*). It must remain valid until replaced or the selectable is freed.
Exact invocation time relative to pn_selectable_free() is not specified; avoid heavy re-entrant API calls from finalize unless documented safe.

functions.name: pn_selectable_attachments
functions.description: Return the attachments record for the selectable, allowing callers to associate arbitrary key/value data with this selectable using the Proton record API.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
The returned pn_record_t* must be used according to the pn_record API (from Proton).
Thread-safety of modifications is unspecified; assume single-threaded unless otherwise documented.

functions.name: pn_selectable_get_fd
functions.description: Get the file descriptor (pn_socket_t) associated with the selectable. This is the descriptor the external loop should poll for read/write events.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
If no descriptor has been set, the returned value and its meaning are unspecified in this header.

functions.name: pn_selectable_set_fd
functions.description: Associate a file descriptor (pn_socket_t) with the selectable. The external loop will monitor this descriptor for read/write readiness and drive notifications via pn_selectable_readable()/pn_selectable_writable().
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
fd must be a pn_socket_t referring to the intended I/O handle for this selectable. Validity of PN_INVALID_SOCKET is unspecified here.
The descriptor should be compatible with non-blocking/event-driven use (typical for Proton).

functions.name: pn_selectable_is_reading
functions.description: Return whether the selectable is currently interested in read events. External event loops can use this to decide whether to monitor the descriptor for readability.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.

functions.name: pn_selectable_set_reading
functions.description: Enable or disable interest in read events for the selectable. Event loops should honor this flag when registering the file descriptor for readability notifications.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
reading specifies the desired read-interest state; no additional constraints.

functions.name: pn_selectable_is_writing
functions.description: Return whether the selectable is currently interested in write events. External event loops can use this to decide whether to monitor the descriptor for writability.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.

functions.name: pn_selectable_set_writing
functions.description: Enable or disable interest in write events for the selectable. Event loops should honor this flag when registering the file descriptor for writability notifications.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
writing specifies the desired write-interest state; no additional constraints.

functions.name: pn_selectable_get_deadline
functions.description: Get the next deadline for the selectable. A non-zero value indicates the time at which the selectable wants a timer notification; zero indicates no deadline.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
Interpret a return value of 0 as "no deadline" as per the documentation.

functions.name: pn_selectable_set_deadline
functions.description: Set the next deadline for the selectable. A deadline of zero disables timer interest; non-zero requests a timer notification at that time.
requirements: sel must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
deadline may be zero to indicate no deadline; other range/epoch details are unspecified in this header.

functions.name: pn_selectable_readable
functions.description: Notify the selectable that its file descriptor is readable. Typically called by the external event loop when a read event occurs; will dispatch the registered readable callback if any.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
Should be called only when the associated file descriptor is readable.
The selectable should be associated with the descriptor that triggered the event (via pn_selectable_set_fd()).

functions.name: pn_selectable_writable
functions.description: Notify the selectable that its file descriptor is writable. Typically called by the external event loop when a write event occurs; will dispatch the registered writable callback if any.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
Should be called only when the associated file descriptor is writable.
The selectable should be associated with the descriptor that triggered the event (via pn_selectable_set_fd()).

functions.name: pn_selectable_error
functions.description: Notify the selectable that an error occurred on its file descriptor. Typically called by the external event loop when an error condition is detected; will dispatch the registered error callback if any.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
Should be called only when an error condition is detected for the associated file descriptor.

functions.name: pn_selectable_expired
functions.description: Notify the selectable that its deadline has expired. Typically called by the external event loop when the current time reaches the value from pn_selectable_get_deadline().
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
Should be called only when the deadline has passed or at expiration time.

functions.name: pn_selectable_is_registered
functions.description: Return whether the selectable is marked as registered with an external event loop. This is a bookkeeping flag controlled by pn_selectable_set_registered().
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.

functions.name: pn_selectable_set_registered
functions.description: Set the registered flag for the selectable to indicate whether it is currently registered with an external event loop. This flag is for tracking only.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
registered is a boolean flag; no additional constraints.

functions.name: pn_selectable_is_terminal
functions.description: Return whether the selectable is in the terminal state. A terminal selectable will never again be interested in any events and should be removed from event loops and freed.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
Callers should remove terminal selectables from external loops and eventually free them.

functions.name: pn_selectable_terminate
functions.description: Put the selectable into the terminal state. After this call, the selectable will not be interested in any further events.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
After termination, callers should stop delivering events to this selectable and remove it from event loop registrations.
The selectable should be freed to reclaim resources after termination.

functions.name: pn_selectable_release
functions.description: Release the selectable. Specific release semantics are not described in this header; typically used with an on-release callback to signal that external references can be dropped.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
If pn_selectable_on_release() was set, its callback may be invoked; exact ordering is unspecified.

functions.name: pn_selectable_free
functions.description: Free a selectable object and reclaim its resources. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: selectable may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid pn_selectable_t previously allocated by pn_selectable() and not already freed.
After this call, the selectable pointer must not be used.

functions.name: pn_selectable_collect
functions.description: Configure the selectable with callbacks that emit readable, writable, and expired events into the supplied collector. This integrates the selectable with Proton’s event collector mechanism instead of user-provided per-event callbacks.
requirements: selectable must be a valid pn_selectable_t and not freed.
collector must be a valid pn_collector_t pointer as defined by Proton’s event API; NULL allowance is unspecified.
Should be called before driving events if collector-based event handling is desired.

functions.name: pn_log_enable
functions.description: Enable or disable global logging for the library. This call overrides the default environment-variable-controlled behavior (PN_TRACE_LOG). Pass true to enable logging or false to disable it. Typically called during process initialization before any logging output is desired.
requirements: Argument enabled must be either true (enable) or false (disable).
This setting overrides PN_TRACE_LOG environment control for subsequent logging.
Callers should invoke this early enough that the desired setting applies to later log messages; effect on previously emitted messages is none.

functions.name: pn_log_logger
functions.description: Install a callback that will receive each log message when logging is enabled. By default, a logger that prints to stderr is used. Passing NULL disables logging regardless of pn_log_enable() or environment settings. Use this to redirect logs to custom sinks.
requirements: If provided, logger must be a valid function pointer with signature void(const char*).
Passing NULL intentionally disables logging, overriding pn_log_enable() and PN_TRACE_LOG.
The logger will be invoked with a const char* message; the implementation must not attempt to modify the message.

functions.name: pn_default_logger
functions.description: Returns the global default logger for the library. Typical usage is to obtain this early in application startup and configure its masks/sink; new loggers use the default logger as a template.
requirements: none explicitly stated in the header; the returned pointer should be treated as a valid pn_logger_t*

functions.name: pn_logger_level_name
functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for a logging level. Intended to convert a pn_log_level_t value to a string for display or diagnostics. Behavior for combined/invalid bit patterns is not documented.
requirements: Parameter level should be a pn_log_level_t value; for meaningful results pass a single defined level flag (e.g., PN_LEVEL_INFO) rather than a bitwise combination.

functions.name: pn_logger_subsystem_name
functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for a logging subsystem. Intended to convert a pn_log_subsystem_t value to a string. Behavior for combined/invalid bit patterns is not documented.
requirements: Parameter subsystem should be a pn_log_subsystem_t value; for meaningful results pass a single defined subsystem flag (e.g., PN_SUBSYSTEM_IO) rather than a bitwise combination.

functions.name: pn_logger_set_mask
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_logger_set_mask(pn_logger_t *logger, uint16_t subsystem, uint16_t level);
functions.description: Sets (enables) specific tracing flags on a logger to control which subsystems and levels will be logged. PN_LEVEL_CRITICAL is always logged; otherwise, a message logs only if both its subsystem and level match enabled bits.
requirements: logger must be a valid pn_logger_t*.
subsystem is a bitmask of pn_log_subsystem_t values to enable; pass PN_SUBSYSTEM_NONE to leave subsystem flags unchanged.
level is a bitmask of pn_log_level_t values to enable; pass PN_LEVEL_NONE to leave level flags unchanged.

functions.name: pn_logger_reset_mask
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_logger_reset_mask(pn_logger_t *logger, uint16_t subsystem, uint16_t level);
functions.description: Clears (disables) specific tracing flags on a logger to control which subsystems and levels will be logged. PN_LEVEL_CRITICAL is always logged; otherwise, a message logs only if both its subsystem and level match enabled bits.
requirements: logger must be a valid pn_logger_t*.
subsystem is a bitmask of pn_log_subsystem_t values to disable; pass PN_SUBSYSTEM_NONE to leave subsystem flags unchanged.
level is a bitmask of pn_log_level_t values to disable; pass PN_LEVEL_NONE to leave level flags unchanged.

functions.name: pn_logger_set_log_sink
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_logger_set_log_sink(pn_logger_t *logger, pn_log_sink_t sink, intptr_t sink_context);
functions.description: Sets the tracing (log sink) callback for a logger and an associated user-specified context value. The sink will be called for each log message that passes filtering, allowing applications to redirect logging.
requirements: logger must be a valid pn_logger_t*.
sink should be a function compatible with pn_log_sink_t (intptr_t, pn_log_subsystem_t, pn_log_level_t, const char*).
sink_context is an opaque value passed to the sink on each invocation.
Behavior if sink is NULL is not documented in the header.

functions.name: pn_logger_get_log_sink
functions.description: Returns the tracing (log sink) callback currently configured on the logger.
requirements: logger must be a valid pn_logger_t*.

functions.name: pn_logger_get_log_sink_context
functions.description: Returns the user-specified sink context associated with the logger’s tracing callback.
requirements: logger must be a valid pn_logger_t*.

functions.name: pn_logger_logf
functions.signature: PN_EXTERN void pn_logger_logf(pn_logger_t *logger, pn_log_subsystem_t subsystem, pn_log_level_t level, PN_PRINTF_FORMAT const char *fmt, ...) PN_PRINTF_FORMAT_ATTR(4, 5);
functions.description: Logs a message via the logger using a printf-style format string and arguments. Intended primarily for Proton internals but available for applications to produce messages processed the same way as library logs.
requirements: logger must be a valid pn_logger_t*.
subsystem should be a pn_log_subsystem_t value (typically a single subsystem bit).
level should be a pn_log_level_t value (messages at PN_LEVEL_CRITICAL are always logged; others are subject to the logger’s masks).
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
Message emission is subject to the logger’s current mask; if filters do not match, the message may not be delivered to the sink.

functions.name: pn_url
functions.description: Create an empty (parsed) URL object. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead. Typical usage: call pn_url() to obtain a pn_url_t*, then use setters to populate it or pn_url_free() to destroy it.
requirements: Caller must check the return value before use; allocation failure behavior is not documented (NULL return is possible but unspecified).
The returned pn_url_t* must be freed with pn_url_free() to avoid leaks.
Do not use the object after it has been freed.

functions.name: pn_url_parse
functions.description: Parse a URL string into a pn_url_t. Returns a parsed URL object on success, or NULL if the input string is not a valid URL. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead. Use getters to access parts or pn_url_free() to destroy.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid NUL-terminated C string pointer (non-NULL).
Input must follow the documented URL syntax: [ <scheme> :// ] [ <user> [ : <password> ] @ ] <host> [ : <port> ] [ / <path> ].
scheme, user, password, and port must not contain any of '@', ':', '/'.
If host begins with '[', it may contain any character up to ']' (IPv6 literal allowed). Otherwise host must not contain '@', ':', '/'.
path may contain any character.
Caller must handle a NULL return to indicate parse failure.
The returned pn_url_t* must be freed with pn_url_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: pn_url_free
functions.description: Free a pn_url_t and any resources it owns. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a pn_url_t previously created by pn_url() or pn_url_parse() and not already freed.
Behavior for url == NULL is not documented; callers should not pass NULL unless confirmed elsewhere.
After return, the url object and any strings obtained from it must not be used.

functions.name: pn_url_clear
functions.description: Clear the contents of the URL object (unset all parts). Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid, initialized pn_url_t that has not been freed.
After clearing, previously returned part pointers (e.g., from getters or pn_url_str) become invalid if the URL is modified; callers should reacquire them.

functions.name: pn_url_str
functions.description: Return the string form of the URL. The returned string is owned by the pn_url_t and will become invalid if it is modified. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid, initialized pn_url_t that has not been freed.
The returned pointer is owned by the URL; the caller must not free it.
The returned string becomes invalid if the URL is modified (per documentation wording).
The documentation does not state whether the function can return NULL; callers should be prepared for unknown behavior and check if necessary.

functions.name: pn_url_get_scheme
functions.description: Get the scheme part of the URL (e.g., "amqp"). Values belong to the URL and may be NULL if not set. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Return value may be NULL if the scheme is not set; callers must handle NULL.
Returned pointer is owned by the URL; do not free it and it may become invalid if the URL is modified or freed.

functions.name: pn_url_get_username
functions.description: Get the username part of the URL. Values belong to the URL and may be NULL if not set. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Return value may be NULL if the username is not set; callers must handle NULL.
Returned pointer is owned by the URL; do not free it and it may become invalid if the URL is modified or freed.

functions.name: pn_url_get_password
functions.description: Get the password part of the URL. Values belong to the URL and may be NULL if not set. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Return value may be NULL if the password is not set; callers must handle NULL.
Returned pointer is owned by the URL; do not free it and it may become invalid if the URL is modified or freed.

functions.name: pn_url_get_host
functions.description: Get the host part of the URL. Values belong to the URL and may be NULL if not set. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Return value may be NULL if the host is not set; callers must handle NULL.
Returned pointer is owned by the URL; do not free it and it may become invalid if the URL is modified or freed.

functions.name: pn_url_get_port
functions.description: Get the port part of the URL. Values belong to the URL and may be NULL if not set. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Return value may be NULL if the port is not set; callers must handle NULL.
Returned pointer is owned by the URL; do not free it and it may become invalid if the URL is modified or freed.

functions.name: pn_url_get_path
functions.description: Get the path part of the URL. Values belong to the URL and may be NULL if not set. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Return value may be NULL if the path is not set; callers must handle NULL.
Returned pointer is owned by the URL; do not free it and it may become invalid if the URL is modified or freed.

functions.name: pn_url_set_scheme
functions.description: Set (or unset) the URL scheme. Values are copied; passing NULL unsets the part. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Parameter scheme may be NULL to indicate the scheme is not set.
Values are copied; the input buffer need not remain valid after the call.

functions.name: pn_url_set_username
functions.description: Set (or unset) the URL username. Values are copied; passing NULL unsets the part. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Parameter username may be NULL to indicate the username is not set.
Values are copied; the input buffer need not remain valid after the call.

functions.name: pn_url_set_password
functions.description: Set (or unset) the URL password. Values are copied; passing NULL unsets the part. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Parameter password may be NULL to indicate the password is not set.
Values are copied; the input buffer need not remain valid after the call.

functions.name: pn_url_set_host
functions.description: Set (or unset) the URL host. Values are copied; passing NULL unsets the part. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Parameter host may be NULL to indicate the host is not set.
Values are copied; the input buffer need not remain valid after the call.

functions.name: pn_url_set_port
functions.description: Set (or unset) the URL port. Values are copied; passing NULL unsets the part. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Parameter port may be NULL to indicate the port is not set.
Values are copied; the input buffer need not remain valid after the call.

functions.name: pn_url_set_path
functions.description: Set (or unset) the URL path. Values are copied; passing NULL unsets the part. Deprecated: Use a third‑party URL library instead.
requirements: Parameter url must be a valid pn_url_t that has not been freed.
Parameter path may be NULL to indicate the path is not set.
Values are copied; the input buffer need not remain valid after the call.

functions.name: pn_tls_config
functions.description: Allocates and returns a TLS configuration object (domain) that holds settings used by one or more TLS sessions created from it. Choose client or server role via mode. Returns NULL on failure or if TLS support is unavailable.
requirements: mode must be a valid pn_tls_mode_t value: PN_TLS_MODE_CLIENT or PN_TLS_MODE_SERVER.
Caller owns the returned pn_tls_config_t* and must free it with pn_tls_config_free.
Do not use the returned pointer after it is freed.

functions.name: pn_tls_config_free
functions.description: Releases a TLS configuration domain created by pn_tls_config. After this call, the domain pointer must not be used.
requirements: domain must be a pn_tls_config_t* returned by pn_tls_config (or NULL-safe behavior is unknown).
All TLS sessions that depend on this domain should no longer be created from it; existing sessions adopt the configuration at creation time.
Do not use domain after free.

functions.name: pn_tls_config_set_credentials
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN int pn_tls_config_set_credentials(pn_tls_config_t *domain, const char *credential_1, const char *credential_2, const char *password);
functions.description: Configures the certificate/credentials that identify the local node for all future TLS sessions created from domain. Supports OpenSSL-style PEM or Windows SChannel stores as documented. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_tls_config_t*.
credential_1 must identify the certificate source (e.g., PEM file or PKCS#12/store).
credential_2 is optional (e.g., private key PEM or friendly name).
password is optional; provide if the key is password-protected, else NULL.
Takes effect only for pn_tls_t objects created after this call returns.

functions.name: pn_tls_config_set_trusted_certs
functions.description: Sets the database of trusted CA certificates used to verify peer certificates for sessions created after this call. Defaults to the system trust store if not set. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_tls_config_t*.
certificate_db must refer to a database/path understood by the underlying TLS implementation.
Takes effect only for pn_tls_t objects created after this call returns.

functions.name: pn_tls_config_set_peer_authentication
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN int pn_tls_config_set_peer_authentication(pn_tls_config_t *domain, const pn_tls_verify_mode_t mode, const char *trusted_CAs);
functions.description: Configures the level of verification applied to peer certificates for sessions created after this call. By default clients verify certificate and peer name; servers do not verify unless configured. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_tls_config_t*.
mode must be a valid pn_tls_verify_mode_t value (e.g., PN_TLS_VERIFY_PEER_NAME).
To verify peers, a trusted CA database must be configured (see pn_tls_config_set_trusted_certs).
Servers that verify peers must also provide their own certificate (see pn_tls_config_set_credentials).
trusted_CAs is a path advertised by servers to clients when server verification is enabled.
Takes effect only for pn_tls_t objects created after this call returns.

functions.name: pn_tls_config_set_impl_ciphers
functions.description: Sets the list of permitted ciphers for sessions created after this call. The syntax of the cipher list is implementation-dependent. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_tls_config_t*.
ciphers must follow the underlying TLS implementation’s expected syntax.
Takes effect only for pn_tls_t objects created after this call returns.

functions.name: pn_tls
functions.description: Creates a new TLS session object configured from domain. Returns NULL on memory allocation failure or if domain is NULL.
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_tls_config_t*; passing NULL results in NULL return.
Caller owns the returned pn_tls_t* and must free it with pn_tls_free.
The session adopts the configuration present in domain at creation time; subsequent domain changes do not affect this session.

functions.name: pn_tls_start
functions.description: Starts the TLS session, initiating any required handshake work (e.g., clienthello generation). After starting, further configuration changes have no effect. Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Call before pn_tls_process; calling configuration setters after this has no effect on this session.
Call exactly once per pn_tls_t before processing.

functions.name: pn_tls_free
functions.description: Releases a TLS session created by pn_tls. After freeing, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: tls must be a pn_tls_t* returned by pn_tls (or NULL-safe behavior is unknown).
Do not use tls after free.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_cipher
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN bool pn_tls_get_cipher(pn_tls_t *tls, const char **cipher, size_t *size);
functions.description: Retrieves a non–null-terminated text description of the currently active cipher and its length. Returns true if a cipher is active; false if TLS is not active.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
cipher and size must point to storage to receive the results; on no active cipher, they are set to NULL and 0 respectively.
Cipher may change over time due to renegotiation; the returned pointer is not specified to be stable beyond immediate use.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_ssf
functions.description: Returns the security strength factor of the currently active cipher. 0 indicates no security.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Interpret a return value of 0 as no active security.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_protocol_version
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN bool pn_tls_get_protocol_version(pn_tls_t *tls, const char **version, size_t *size);
functions.description: Retrieves a non–null-terminated text description of the active TLS protocol version and its length. Returns true if active; false if TLS is not active or negotiation not complete.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
version and size must be valid pointers; on not active, they are set to NULL and 0 respectively.
Protocol may change due to renegotiation.

functions.name: pn_tls_set_peer_hostname
functions.description: Sets the expected remote peer identity (hostname). Used for SNI on clients and for name verification against the peer certificate when PN_TLS_VERIFY_PEER_NAME is enabled. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
hostname must conform to RFC1034 Section 3.5 (DNS hostname syntax).
Name verification occurs only if PN_TLS_VERIFY_PEER_NAME is configured via the domain.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_peer_hostname
functions.description: Retrieves the configured expected peer hostname set via pn_tls_set_peer_hostname. If hostname is NULL, no string is written; bufsize is set to the required size (including the null terminator). Returns 0 on success.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
bufsize must be non-NULL. On input, set to the size of the hostname buffer; on output, set to the required size (including null).
If provided, hostname must point to a buffer of at least the input bufsize bytes.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_remote_subject
functions.description: Returns a null-terminated string of the full subject from the peer’s certificate. The returned pointer remains valid until the tls object is destroyed.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Use or copy the returned string before destroying tls.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_cert_fingerprint
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN int pn_tls_get_cert_fingerprint(pn_tls_t *tls0, char *fingerprint, size_t fingerprint_length, pn_tls_hash_alg hash_alg);
functions.description: Computes the hexadecimal fingerprint of the peer certificate using the specified hash algorithm and writes a null-terminated string into fingerprint. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: tls0 must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
fingerprint must point to writable storage.
fingerprint_length must be sufficient for the selected hash: >=33 (MD5), >=41 (SHA1), >=65 (SHA256), >=129 (SHA512).
hash_alg must be one of pn_tls_hash_alg values (PN_TLS_MD5, PN_TLS_SHA1, PN_TLS_SHA256, PN_TLS_SHA512).
On success the output is a null-terminated uppercase/lowercase unspecified hex string of the required length minus 1 plus terminator.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_remote_subject_subfield
functions.description: Returns a null-terminated string containing the requested subject subfield (e.g., CN, O, OU, L, ST, C) from the peer’s certificate. The string remains valid until the tls object is destroyed.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
field must be a valid pn_tls_cert_subject_subfield enum value.
Use or copy the returned string before destroying tls.

functions.name: pn_tls_is_encrypt_output_pending
functions.description: Returns true if there is encrypted output data pending to be taken; false otherwise.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Pending data status may change after pn_tls_process() calls.

functions.name: pn_tls_is_decrypt_output_pending
functions.description: Returns true if there is decrypted output data pending to be taken; false otherwise.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Pending data status may change after pn_tls_process() calls.

functions.name: pn_tls_is_secure
functions.description: Returns true if a TLS session has been successfully negotiated. False indicates handshake in progress or a protocol error.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Use alongside error/status APIs to distinguish in-progress from error states.

functions.name: pn_tls_give_encrypt_output_buffers
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN size_t pn_tls_give_encrypt_output_buffers(pn_tls_t* tls, pn_raw_buffer_t const* buffers, size_t count);
functions.description: Provides application-owned buffers for the TLS engine to write encrypted output results into. Transfers ownership for the number of buffers returned. Returns the number of buffers accepted (may be less than count).
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
buffers must point to an array of at least count pn_raw_buffer_t elements.
Ownership of the returned number of buffers transfers to the TLS engine until they are taken back via pn_tls_take_encrypt_output_buffers.
Callers should be prepared for partial acceptance and retry until capacity allows.

functions.name: pn_tls_give_decrypt_output_buffers
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN size_t pn_tls_give_decrypt_output_buffers(pn_tls_t* tls, pn_raw_buffer_t const* buffers, size_t count);
functions.description: Provides application-owned buffers for the TLS engine to write decrypted output results into. Transfers ownership for the number of buffers returned. Returns the number of buffers accepted (may be less than count).
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
buffers must point to an array of at least count pn_raw_buffer_t elements.
Ownership of the returned number of buffers transfers to the TLS engine until they are taken back via pn_tls_take_decrypt_output_buffers.
Callers should be prepared for partial acceptance and retry until capacity allows.

functions.name: pn_tls_take_decrypt_output_buffers
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN size_t pn_tls_take_decrypt_output_buffers(pn_tls_t* tls, pn_raw_buffer_t* buffers, size_t count);
functions.description: Takes back application ownership of decrypted result buffers produced by the TLS engine. Returns the number of buffers returned. Call repeatedly until zero to drain all available buffers. After pn_tls_stop(), all remaining buffers are returned.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
buffers must point to an array with capacity for at least count entries to receive returned buffers.
Call repeatedly until the return value is 0 to ensure all available buffers are retrieved.

functions.name: pn_tls_take_encrypt_output_buffers
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN size_t pn_tls_take_encrypt_output_buffers(pn_tls_t* tls, pn_raw_buffer_t* buffers, size_t count);
functions.description: Takes back application ownership of encrypted result buffers produced by the TLS engine. Returns the number of buffers returned. Call repeatedly until zero to drain all available buffers. After pn_tls_stop(), all remaining buffers are returned.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
buffers must point to an array with capacity for at least count entries to receive returned buffers.
Call repeatedly until the return value is 0 to ensure all available buffers are retrieved.

functions.name: pn_tls_give_encrypt_input_buffers
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN size_t pn_tls_give_encrypt_input_buffers(pn_tls_t* tls, pn_raw_buffer_t const* bufs, size_t count_bufs);
functions.description: Stages plaintext input buffers for future encryption by the TLS engine. Ownership of accepted buffers transfers to the engine. Returns the number of buffers accepted (bounded by capacity).
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
bufs must point to an array of at least count_bufs pn_raw_buffer_t elements.
Ownership of the returned number of buffers transfers to the TLS engine until reclaimed via pn_tls_take_encrypt_input_buffers.
After pn_tls_close_output(), this function will no longer accept buffers.

functions.name: pn_tls_give_decrypt_input_buffers
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN size_t pn_tls_give_decrypt_input_buffers(pn_tls_t* tls, pn_raw_buffer_t const* bufs, size_t count_bufs);
functions.description: Stages ciphertext input buffers for decryption by the TLS engine. Ownership of accepted buffers transfers to the engine. Returns the number of buffers accepted (bounded by capacity).
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
bufs must point to an array of at least count_bufs pn_raw_buffer_t elements.
Ownership of the returned number of buffers transfers to the TLS engine until reclaimed via pn_tls_take_decrypt_input_buffers.

functions.name: pn_tls_take_encrypt_input_buffers
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN size_t pn_tls_take_encrypt_input_buffers(pn_tls_t* tls, pn_raw_buffer_t* buffers, size_t count);
functions.description: Takes back plaintext input buffers previously given for encryption whose data has been fully processed (or after pn_tls_stop()). Returns the number of buffers returned; call until zero to drain.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
buffers must point to an array with capacity for at least count entries.
Call repeatedly until the return value is 0 to ensure all eligible buffers are retrieved.

functions.name: pn_tls_take_decrypt_input_buffers
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN size_t pn_tls_take_decrypt_input_buffers(pn_tls_t* tls, pn_raw_buffer_t* buffers, size_t count);
functions.description: Takes back ciphertext input buffers previously given for decryption whose data has been fully processed (or after pn_tls_stop()). Returns the number of buffers returned; call until zero to drain.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
buffers must point to an array with capacity for at least count entries.
Call repeatedly until the return value is 0 to ensure all eligible buffers are retrieved.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_encrypt_input_buffer_capacity
functions.description: Returns the number of additional encrypt input buffers the engine can currently accept.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Capacity changes over time as buffers are processed and taken.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_decrypt_input_buffer_capacity
functions.description: Returns the number of additional decrypt input buffers the engine can currently accept.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Capacity changes over time as buffers are processed and taken.

functions.name: pn_tls_need_encrypt_output_buffers
functions.description: Returns true if there is no remaining space in the encrypted result buffers and encrypted data is available since the last pn_tls_process(). Indicates the engine needs more encrypt output buffers.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Interpret true as a need to provide more encrypt output buffers via pn_tls_give_encrypt_output_buffers.

functions.name: pn_tls_need_decrypt_output_buffers
functions.description: Returns true if there is no remaining space in the decrypted result buffers and decrypted data is available since the last pn_tls_process(). Indicates the engine needs more decrypt output buffers.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Interpret true as a need to provide more decrypt output buffers via pn_tls_give_decrypt_output_buffers.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_encrypt_output_buffer_capacity
functions.description: Returns the number of additional encrypt output buffers the engine can currently hold.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Capacity changes as buffers are taken/given.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_decrypt_output_buffer_capacity
functions.description: Returns the number of additional decrypt output buffers the engine can currently hold.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Capacity changes as buffers are taken/given.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_decrypt_output_buffer_count
functions.description: Returns the number of decrypted output buffers ready to be returned by pn_tls_take_decrypt_output_buffers since the last pn_tls_process() or pn_tls_stop().
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Use to size arrays when taking buffers.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_encrypt_output_buffer_count
functions.description: Returns the number of encrypted output buffers ready to be returned by pn_tls_take_encrypt_output_buffers since the last pn_tls_process() or pn_tls_stop().
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Use to size arrays when taking buffers.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_last_decrypt_output_buffer_size
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the last decrypted output buffer returned by take since the last pn_tls_process() call.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Meaningful after a take operation that returned at least one decrypted buffer.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_last_encrypt_output_buffer_size
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the last encrypted output buffer returned by take since the last pn_tls_process() call.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Meaningful after a take operation that returned at least one encrypted buffer.

functions.name: pn_tls_set_encrypt_input_buffer_max_capacity
functions.description: Sets the maximum capacity (number of buffers) for encrypt input buffers for this session. Zero means use default. Has no effect after pn_tls_start().
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Must be called before pn_tls_start() to take effect.
s is a capacity count; zero selects default.

functions.name: pn_tls_set_decrypt_input_buffer_max_capacity
functions.description: Sets the maximum capacity (number of buffers) for decrypt input buffers for this session. Zero means use default. Has no effect after pn_tls_start().
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Must be called before pn_tls_start() to take effect.
s is a capacity count; zero selects default.

functions.name: pn_tls_set_encrypt_output_buffer_max_capacity
functions.description: Sets the maximum capacity (number of buffers) for encrypt output buffers for this session. Zero means use default. Has no effect after pn_tls_start().
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Must be called before pn_tls_start() to take effect.
s is a capacity count; zero selects default.

functions.name: pn_tls_set_decrypt_output_buffer_max_capacity
functions.description: Sets the maximum capacity (number of buffers) for decrypt output buffers for this session. Zero means use default. Has no effect after pn_tls_start().
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Must be called before pn_tls_start() to take effect.
s is a capacity count; zero selects default.

functions.name: pn_tls_process
functions.description: Processes as much pending input as possible, producing encrypted and decrypted output into provided buffers. Also checks for TLS engine errors. Returns 0 on success; returns an error if called before pn_tls_start() or after pn_tls_stop().
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Must be called only after pn_tls_start() and before pn_tls_stop().
Ensure appropriate input and output buffers have been provided via the give* APIs to allow progress.

functions.name: pn_tls_stop
functions.description: Stops the TLS session. Future pn_tls_process() or give-buffer calls are no-ops. Unused result buffers become zero-length results and can be reclaimed. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
After stopping, retrieve and reclaim all remaining buffers via the take* APIs.

functions.name: pn_tls_is_input_closed
functions.description: Returns true if the peer’s TLS closure record has been received, indicating a clean shutdown and no truncation attack.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Use to confirm orderly shutdown after reading pending data.

functions.name: pn_tls_close_output
functions.description: Closes the encrypt (outgoing) side and appends the TLS closure record to pending encrypted output. After this call, pn_tls_give_encrypt_input_buffers() will no longer accept buffers.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
Ensure pending encrypted output is drained via pn_tls_take_encrypt_output_buffers after calling.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_session_error
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the TLS session failed to start or was aborted. When non-zero, the application should stop reads, drain remaining encrypted content to propagate the error to the peer, then close the underlying connection.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
On non-zero error, drain encrypted output until pn_tls_is_encrypt_output_pending() is false before closing.
Specific non-zero codes are implementation-defined; negative codes such as PN_TLS_INIT_ERR may apply.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_session_error_string
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN size_t pn_tls_get_session_error_string(pn_tls_t* tls, char *buf, size_t buf_len);
functions.description: Writes a human-readable description of the fatal TLS session error into buf and returns the number of bytes written. Returns 0 if there is no error or if buf is NULL or buf_len is 0.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
If provided, buf must have capacity buf_len bytes to receive a null-terminated string (termination not explicitly guaranteed; follow returned size).
Call after detecting a non-zero session error.

functions.name: pn_tls_config_set_alpn_protocols
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN int pn_tls_config_set_alpn_protocols(pn_tls_config_t *domain, const char **protocols, size_t protocol_count);
functions.description: Configures ALPN (RFC 7301) protocol list for sessions created from this domain. Clients send the list in preference order; servers select the first match against the client’s list. Set protocols=NULL and protocol_count=0 to disable ALPN. Returns 0 on success; PN_ARG_ERROR on invalid inputs; PN_OUT_OF_MEMORY on allocation failure.
requirements: domain must be a valid pn_tls_config_t*.
If protocol_count > 0, protocols must be a valid array of protocol_count pointers, none of which are NULL.
Each protocol name must be a UTF-8 octet sequence, null-terminated, and no more than 255 bytes long (excluding the terminator).
Takes effect only for pn_tls_t objects created after this call returns.

functions.name: pn_tls_get_alpn_protocol
functions.signature: PN_TLS_EXTERN bool pn_tls_get_alpn_protocol(pn_tls_t *tls, const char **protocol_name, size_t *size);
functions.description: Gets the negotiated application protocol name and its length. The name is not null-terminated. Returns true if a protocol was negotiated; false if negotiation failed, is incomplete, or was not requested.
requirements: tls must be a valid pn_tls_t*.
protocol_name and size must be valid pointers; on no negotiated protocol they are set to NULL and 0 respectively.

functions.name: pn_messenger
functions.description: Constructs a new pn_messenger_t instance. If name is NULL, a UUID-based global name is chosen. Intended entry point to the Messenger API (deprecated in favor of Proactor or Proton C++).
requirements: If name is non-NULL, it must point to a NUL-terminated string.
Returned messenger must be freed with pn_messenger_free.
Messenger API is single-threaded; only pn_messenger_interrupt may be called concurrently from another thread.

functions.name: pn_messenger_name
functions.description: Returns the global name of the messenger.
requirements: messenger must be a valid pn_messenger_t created by pn_messenger and not yet freed.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_certificate
functions.description: Sets the path to the certificate used to identify the messenger to peers. The path’s validity is not checked here.
requirements: messenger must be a valid, initialized pn_messenger_t.
certificate must be a NUL-terminated file-system path string; may refer to a readable certificate file.
Caller should check return value for non-zero error codes.

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_certificate
functions.description: Gets the certificate file path previously set with pn_messenger_set_certificate. Default is NULL.
requirements: messenger must be a valid pn_messenger_t.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_private_key
functions.description: Sets the path to the private key file corresponding to the certificate.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
private_key must be a NUL-terminated path to the private key file.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error (<0).

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_private_key
functions.description: Gets the previously configured private key file path.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_password
functions.description: Sets the password for the private key file.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
password must be a NUL-terminated string containing the private key password (if required by the key file).
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_password
functions.description: Gets the password used for the private key file.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_trusted_certificates
functions.description: Sets the trusted certificates database used to validate peer certificates.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
cert_db must be a NUL-terminated path to a certificate database file.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_trusted_certificates
functions.description: Gets the path to the trusted certificates database.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_timeout
functions.description: Sets the default timeout (milliseconds) for blocking operations. Calls that would block return when this timeout is reached if set > 0.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
timeout is in milliseconds; values > 0 enable time-limited blocking behavior.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_timeout
functions.description: Gets the messenger’s timeout in milliseconds.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_is_blocking
functions.description: Returns whether blocking behavior is enabled for send/recv operations.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_blocking
functions.description: Enables or disables blocking behavior for pn_messenger_send and pn_messenger_recv.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_is_passive
functions.description: Returns whether passive mode is enabled. In passive mode, messenger does no internal I/O; selectables must be serviced externally.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_passive
functions.description: Enables or disables passive mode. In passive mode, I/O is exposed via pn_messenger_selectable for external event loops.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.
If enabling passive mode, caller must be prepared to extract and service all selectables until terminal and free them.

functions.name: pn_messenger_free
functions.description: Frees a messenger and its resources. Safe to pass NULL.
requirements: If messenger is non-NULL, it must not be used after this call.
It is safe to call with messenger == NULL.

functions.name: pn_messenger_errno
functions.description: Returns the messenger’s most recent error code. Error code is sticky and not automatically cleared by successful API calls.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
Caller should use pn_messenger_error to access/clear details if desired.

functions.name: pn_messenger_error
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the messenger’s pn_error_t object (valid until the messenger is freed) to inspect or clear the error.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
Returned pn_error_t pointer becomes invalid after messenger is freed.

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_outgoing_window
functions.description: Returns the size of the outgoing tracking window (limits how many recent outgoing messages have status tracked). Default is 0.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_outgoing_window
functions.description: Sets the size of the outgoing tracking window (number of outgoing deliveries to track).
requirements: messenger must be valid.
window should be a non-negative integer (inferred from semantics of a window size).
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_incoming_window
functions.description: Returns the size of the incoming tracking window (limits how many received messages can be explicitly accepted/rejected). Default is 0.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_incoming_window
functions.description: Sets the size of the incoming tracking window.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
window should be a non-negative integer (inferred).
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_start
functions.description: No-op placeholder for future compatibility. For safety, do not send or receive before starting the messenger.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_stop
functions.description: Performs an orderly shutdown of all underlying connections. May return PN_INPROGRESS in non-blocking mode; use pn_messenger_stopped to poll completion.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
If in non-blocking mode and PN_INPROGRESS is returned, caller must poll pn_messenger_stopped until true before assuming shutdown complete.
Caller must check return value for success (0), PN_INPROGRESS, or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_stopped
functions.description: Non-blocking check whether the messenger has reached the stopped state.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_subscribe
functions.description: Creates a subscription to receive messages from the specified source address.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
source must be a NUL-terminated address string using the documented address syntax.
Returned pn_subscription_t is owned by the messenger; its lifetime is tied to the messenger.

functions.name: pn_messenger_subscribe_ttl
functions.description: Creates a subscription to a source with a specified lifetime TTL after the link is closed.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
source must be a NUL-terminated address.
timeout specifies maximum time to keep the subscription alive once the link is closed (seconds).

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_link
functions.description: Returns a link by address and role (sender=true for sender link, false for receiver). Returns NULL if no matching link.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
address must identify the link.
sender must reflect the desired link direction.

functions.name: pn_subscription_get_context
functions.description: Gets the application-defined context pointer associated with a subscription.
requirements: sub must be a valid pn_subscription_t obtained from the messenger.

functions.name: pn_subscription_set_context
functions.description: Associates an application-defined context pointer with a subscription.
requirements: sub must be valid.
context pointer must remain valid as long as the application expects to retrieve it (ownership and lifetime managed by caller).

functions.name: pn_subscription_address
functions.description: Returns the source address of a subscription.
requirements: sub must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_put
functions.description: Enqueues a message on the outgoing queue. May also send immediately if it can do so without blocking. This call does not block.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
msg must be a valid, initialized pn_message_t; set at least its address and any required fields by the destination.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_status
functions.description: Returns the current status of the delivery associated with tracker. May return PN_STATUS_UNKNOWN if the tracker is outside tracking windows.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
tracker must be obtained from pn_messenger_outgoing_tracker or pn_messenger_incoming_tracker and still within the corresponding window to get definitive status.

functions.name: pn_messenger_delivery
functions.description: Returns the pn_delivery_t for the delivery identified by tracker, or NULL if outside tracking windows.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
tracker must refer to a tracked delivery.

functions.name: pn_messenger_buffered
functions.description: Returns true if the delivery associated with tracker is still buffered (waiting to be sent). False does not imply it was sent over the wire.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
tracker must refer to a delivery still within the outgoing tracking window to yield meaningful results.

functions.name: pn_messenger_settle
functions.signature: int pn_messenger_settle(pn_messenger_t *messenger, pn_tracker_t tracker, int flags);
functions.description: Stops tracking status for the given tracker. If flags includes PN_CUMULATIVE, frees tracking for all deliveries up to and including tracker.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
tracker must refer to a known delivery.
flags must be 0 or PN_CUMULATIVE.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_outgoing_tracker
functions.description: Returns the tracker for the most recent outgoing message passed to pn_messenger_put, as long as it is still in the outgoing window. Note: the documentation text states the return is undefined if pn_messenger_get has never been called; this appears inconsistent and likely means pn_messenger_put—callers should ensure at least one outgoing message has been put.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
At least one successful pn_messenger_put should have been called to obtain a meaningful tracker.
Tracker may be invalid if the message fell out of the outgoing window.

functions.name: pn_messenger_work
functions.description: Performs send/receive work for queued messages for up to timeout milliseconds. Returns 0 if no work, 1 if work was done, or <0 on error. timeout: -1 blocks forever, 0 returns immediately.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
timeout must be an integer in milliseconds; -1 means infinite blocking, 0 means non-blocking.
Caller must check return value for 1/0, or <0 for error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_interrupt
functions.description: Interrupts a messenger that may be blocking in another thread, causing it to return with PN_INTR. The only function intended for concurrent use from another thread.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
May be called from a different thread than other messenger calls.

functions.name: pn_messenger_send
functions.description: Sends messages from the outgoing queue. In blocking mode, blocks until n messages are fully processed (status determined). n = -1 means all. In non-blocking mode may return PN_INPROGRESS if unable to complete without blocking. May return PN_TIMEOUT if the configured timeout is reached.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
n must be -1 or a non-negative integer indicating how many messages to send.
Caller must check return value for success (0), PN_INPROGRESS, PN_TIMEOUT, or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_recv
functions.description: Receives up to limit messages into the incoming queue. limit = -1 means receive as many as can be internally buffered. In blocking mode, blocks until at least one message is available. Calling with limit = 0 cancels any outstanding receive.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
limit must be -1, 0, or a non-negative integer.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_receiving
functions.description: Returns the remaining capacity of the incoming queue (number of additional messages that can be received), not counting messages already queued.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_get
functions.description: Copies the head message from the incoming queue into message and removes it. If message is NULL, discards the head message. Returns PN_EOS if no messages are available. Non-blocking.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
If message is non-NULL, it must be a valid pn_message_t ready to receive content.
Caller must handle PN_EOS return when no messages remain.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_incoming_tracker
functions.description: Returns the tracker for the most recent message retrieved by pn_messenger_get. Used to accept/reject messages (possibly cumulative). Undefined if pn_messenger_get has not been called successfully.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
At least one successful pn_messenger_get must have been called to obtain a meaningful tracker.

functions.name: pn_messenger_incoming_subscription
functions.description: Returns the subscription of the most recent message retrieved by pn_messenger_get, or NULL if none.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
At least one successful pn_messenger_get must have been called to return non-NULL.

functions.name: pn_messenger_tracker_link
functions.description: Returns the link associated with the message referenced by tracker, or NULL if it cannot be determined.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
tracker must refer to a known delivery.

functions.name: pn_messenger_outgoing
functions.description: Returns the number of messages currently in the outgoing queue.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_incoming
functions.description: Returns the number of messages currently in the incoming queue.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_route
functions.signature: int pn_messenger_route(pn_messenger_t *messenger, const char *pattern, const char *address);
functions.description: Adds a routing rule: if a message’s address matches pattern (supports '%' to match any char except '/', and '*' to match any char including '/'), route it using address (which may include substitution variables like $1, $2 from matches). Rules are evaluated in order; first match applies.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
pattern must be a NUL-terminated glob pattern using '%' and '*'.
address must be a NUL-terminated AMQP address; may include substitution variables like $1, $2.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_rewrite
functions.signature: int pn_messenger_rewrite(pn_messenger_t *messenger, const char *pattern, const char *address);
functions.description: Adds an outgoing address rewrite rule applied after routing is finalized. Commonly used to scrub usernames/passwords from addresses sent on the wire. Matching syntax same as pn_messenger_route.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
pattern must be a NUL-terminated glob pattern.
address must be a NUL-terminated address template for rewrite.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_selectable
functions.description: Extracts the next selectable from a passive messenger for external I/O servicing. Call repeatedly until it returns NULL. Each returned selectable must be serviced until terminal and then freed. If a selectable is "registered", it may be returned whenever its interest set changes.
requirements: messenger must be valid and in passive mode (pn_messenger_set_passive(true)).
Caller must repeatedly call until NULL to extract all available selectables.
All selectables returned must be serviced until terminal and then freed.
If a selectable has its registered flag true, it may be returned multiple times.

functions.name: pn_messenger_deadline
functions.description: Returns the nearest deadline among selectables associated with the messenger (useful for polling/select timeouts).
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_flags
functions.description: Sets control flags that enable additional behavior. Defined flags include PN_FLAGS_CHECK_ROUTES (validate routes on start) and PN_FLAGS_ALLOW_INSECURE_MECHS (allow PLAIN on unencrypted connections).
requirements: messenger must be valid.
flags may be 0 or a bitwise OR of PN_FLAGS_CHECK_ROUTES and/or PN_FLAGS_ALLOW_INSECURE_MECHS (per defined macros).
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_flags
functions.description: Returns the currently set control flags for the messenger.
requirements: messenger must be valid.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_snd_settle_mode
functions.description: Sets the local sender settle mode for the underlying link(s).
requirements: messenger must be valid.
mode must be a valid pn_snd_settle_mode_t enum value.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_rcv_settle_mode
functions.description: Sets the local receiver settle mode for the underlying link(s).
requirements: messenger must be valid.
mode must be a valid pn_rcv_settle_mode_t enum value.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or error.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_tracer
functions.description: Sets a tracer callback for the messenger to receive trace output.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
tracer must be a valid callback function pointer; it must remain valid while tracing is enabled.

functions.name: pn_messenger_get_remote_idle_timeout
functions.description: Returns the remote idle timeout (milliseconds) for the specified remote service address, or -1 on error.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
address must be a NUL-terminated remote service address string.

functions.name: pn_messenger_set_ssl_peer_authentication_mode
functions.description: Sets the SSL peer authentication mode required when a trust certificate is used.
requirements: messenger must be valid.
mode must be a valid pn_ssl_verify_mode_t value.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or -1 on error.
